fix(trusty-mpm): apply tmux history-limit after server-up, before pane creation (#3386) (#3722)

* fix(trusty-mpm): apply tmux history-limit after server-up, before pane creation (#3386)

The resume-after-tmux-server-death path issued `set-option -g` calls
before any server-starting tmux command had run. Unlike `new-session`,
`set-option -g` has no auto-start-server behavior in tmux — it silently
fails "no server running", and the failure was logged as non-fatal.
The subsequent `new-session` call (the one command that DOES auto-start
a server) then created a pane on a fresh server that never received the
configured history-limit, freezing it at tmux's factory default of 2000
and causing active scrollback eviction for the rest of the session.

`create_managed_session` (the single session-creation choke point every
call site routes through) now explicitly confirms the tmux server is up
via a new `TmuxCommand::StartServer` (idempotent, retried up to 3 times
with backoff) before applying the scrollback/mouse options, and verifies
`history-limit` actually landed via a new `TmuxCommand::ShowGlobalOption`
probe before the pane-creating `new-session` runs. Retry exhaustion or a
verification mismatch logs a `warn!` naming #3386.

Since the resume path (`SessionManager::resume` -> `create_and_verify_pane`
-> `RealTmuxDriver::create_session` -> `TmuxDriver::create_session`) already
routes through this one choke point, no separate resume-path change was
needed to close the race there too.

* fix(trusty-mpm): relaunch/rename resolvers prefer live-pane record over name-match (#3714)

Two managed session records sharing a display name (the already-duplicated
code paths, all rooted in the same "trust a bare name-string match" flaw:

- `nested_managed_match` (the bare-`tm`-inside-tmux relaunch resolver) tied
  purely on `created_at`, so a stale duplicate created after the real live
  session always won, reliably reproducing the reported dead-pane refusal.
  It now tie-breaks in order: (1) the invoking process's own confirmed tmux
  pane identity, (2) a verifiably-alive candidate over a dead one, (3) most
  recent as the last resort — and refuses with a full-id disambiguation
  listing (`pick_least_ambiguous`) rather than silently picking a row when a
  tie survives every tier.

- `SessionManager::rename`'s "physically rename the tmux session to match"
  step resolved the target tmux session via `live_names.contains(old_name)`
  — a bare name-string membership check. Renaming a stale duplicate whose
  own pane was gone could therefore rename a DIFFERENT, live, attached
  operator's session that merely shared the old name (reproduced live in
  the issue's remediation: `tm sessions rename` on a stale `tm-tagents`
  duplicate retitled the real, attached `tm-tagents` session). `rename` now
  resolves liveness via the target record's own recorded `pane_id`
  (pane-scoped, via `ManagedTmuxDriver::pane_exists`) and renames only the
  DB record — with a clear notice — when that identity can't be confirmed.

- `reconcile_live_state` (the `tm ls`/`session info` display reconciler)
  used the same name-string check, which is why a single record could
  simultaneously report `state: "active"` and `persisted_state: "stopped"`
  — different code paths reading `state` vs `persisted_state` disagreed
  about the identical row. It now reconciles `state` pane-scoped too.

  or write_scrollback, and refuses the write with warn! naming the session

  present, .trusty-mpm/ subdir absent) is unaffected.

  subdir, so capture_into can log that at info! instead of the previous
  always-debug! success path.

  (CanonicalizeFailureStreaks) to the #1845 F3 canonicalize-fallback in the
  per-minute prune_orphaned_worktrees sweep, escalating to error! after 10
  consecutive sweeps (~10 minutes) - the original incident's F3 WARN fired
  unnoticed for ~8h with no way to distinguish "just started" from
  "sustained for hours". In-memory only, no persistence.

  same workspace-root-recreation hazard: only snapshot.rs:111 fits the
  shape (a write path deriving a directory from a session's workspace_path
  at stop/reap time). session_launch/settings.rs's four sites are
  deploy-time (already cleared by the investigation); store.rs:229 targets
  the daemon's own persistent data_dir, not a session workspace root, so it

* fix: move BM25/chunk rehydrate off the query deadline + deterministic cap order (#3683 slice 1, #3684)

Defect 1 (#3683 root defect): ensure_bm25_entities_loaded/ensure_chunks_loaded
used to scan the full redb corpus and publish the results inline, awaited
directly by callers including interactive query handlers wrapped in
apply_query_timeout's tokio::time::timeout. On expiry that whole future was
cancelled, discarding the rehydrate's completed work and leaving the index
cold, so the next query paid the full scan again -- a self-sustaining
livelock under repeated timeouts on a large corpus (27-40s observed on a
315K-chunk NFS-backed index).

which either joins an already-in-flight rehydrate for this index or becomes
the leader and spawns idle_evict::spawn_detached_rehydrate as an independent
tokio::spawn task (mirroring open_guard's #3659 detached-attempt pattern).
The task commits (chunks + BM25 + entities + clearing both *_evicted flags)
regardless of how many callers gave up waiting for it; callers only ever
cancel their own bounded wait (idle_evict::rehydrate_wait_budget, default 4s),
never the task itself. This also kills a pre-existing double

Code-critic review round 3 on PR #3690 (commit 925770ff) returned WARN with
one remaining HIGH: the round-2 evict-vs-rehydrate fix compared

load and the stores for a concurrent evict's own bump-generation +
set-flag-true pair to land and get silently clobbered back to `false` by
the commit's stale store — the finding-2 bug recurring through a narrower
door, with zero test coverage (the existing
`rehydrate_commit_skips_flag_clear_when_evict_races_it` only covers a race
landing BEFORE the generation load, via `TEST_DELAY_BEFORE_COMMIT_MS`).

`rehydrate_generation` is now a `std::sync::Mutex<u64>`. Both sides hold
that same lock across their entire sequence instead of touching an atomic
independently:

  `crates/trusty-search/src/core/indexer/idle_evict.rs` (`clear_bm25_entities`)

  `crates/trusty-search/src/core/indexer/idle_evict.rs`
  (`spawn_detached_rehydrate`'s commit branch).

exclusive: either the evict's section runs entirely before the commit's

* fix(trusty-agents): check git merge-file exit status before trusting its stdout

`ConflictResolver::resolve_conflict` read the merge subprocess's stdout while
ignoring its exit status. `git merge-file` multiplexes three outcomes onto one
integer -- 0 clean, 1..=127 conflict count, anything above that a git error --
and on error it prints nothing. The old marker scan (`windows(7) == b"<<<<<<<"`)
trivially finds no markers in an empty buffer, so a failed git was classified as
a clean merge and the resolver wrote a zero-byte file over both sub-agents' work.

fix(trusty-search): eliminate stack-overflow crash in chunker/entity AST walk (#3628)

walk_for_chunks (core/chunker/walk.rs) and walk_rust (core/entity.rs) were
native recursive descents whose stack depth tracked raw tree-sitter
parse-tree depth. That depth is attacker-influenced — it comes straight from
file content being indexed — so a deeply nested global-scope construct (e.g.
deeply templated C++ headers, or any deeply nested expression/type outside a
function body, which was already pruned) could exceed the process stack and
abort the whole daemon with "fatal runtime error: stack overflow", taking
every other index down with it (issue #3537).

Confirmed root cause with an out-of-tree repro: a global-scope declaration
with 200,000 levels of nested parens reliably aborted the process on both a
1 MiB and a normal 8 MiB thread stack; the same input now completes cleanly.

Fix: convert both walks to iteration (explicit heap-allocated work stack,
matching the pattern collect_calls already used in the same file), which
removes the crash regardless of nesting depth. Also add a bounded
max-walk-depth guard (logged once per file, not silent) plus a matching cap
on collect_calls's own per-node subtree walk — needed because
classify_node's Node::parent() lookups are not O(1), so without a depth cap
a long chain of nested classified containers (mod/class/impl) degrades to
superlinear traversal cost and can still hang the indexing worker even once
the crash itself is fixed. A single pathological file now degrades to
"partially chunked, logged" rather than crashing or hanging the daemon.

* fix(trusty-search): honor TRUSTY_DATA_DIR in CLI daemon discovery

The index/list/reindex/search subcommands (and port/serve/monitor web,
which shared the same discovery code) all resolved the daemon's address
via trusty_common::read_daemon_addr("trusty-search") / write_daemon_addr,

* fix(ci): close glob/parenthetical blind spots in Test: pointer lint

check_test_pointers.sh silently dropped glob-shaped citations
(`foo_*` failed the identifier filter and produced zero candidates)
and stopped scanning a multi-citation annotation at the first

  the leading-run scan, and doesn't itself misparse a nested paren
  inside an embedded code span like `` `read()` ``) so multi-citation
  annotations are read in full.

  non-allowlistable failure instead of a silent truncation — the
  parser now fails loudly on anything it cannot interpret.

previously-invisible dangling citations (pre-existing drift the old
parser could never see, not new regressions). 20 were fixed directly
in the doc comment (corrected to the real test name or a resolving
glob, or reworded so a legitimate cross-crate citation is no longer a
bare backtick span); 53 that genuinely require writing a new test are
grandfathered in .test-pointer-allowlist.tsv, matching the ratchet's

fix(trusty-search): bound the .gitignore upward walk to the caller's root (#3582)

find_or_create_gitignore walked upward with no boundary, stopping only
if it happened to hit a `.git` directory along the way. With no `.git`
above the root (any test tempdir(), or any production root that isn't
itself inside a git repo), the walk continued to the filesystem root —
able to find and write a `.gitignore` outside the directory the caller
pointed the tool at. That is the production risk #3564 flagged, and it
is also the exact cause of the reproducible gitignore_entry_added_idempotently
failure whenever a stray .gitignore exists at the shared $TMPDIR root.

Fix: make the walk boundary an explicit, injected parameter instead of
inferring it from `.git` presence. ensure_gitignored now always passes
root_path as its own boundary, so the walk can never read or write
anything outside it, in tests or production, regardless of what `.git`
markers exist on disk. Not-found behavior is unchanged: create at the
boundary (root_path/.gitignore).

The previous "find a parent .gitignore in a monorepo" behavior is
removed: keeping it would have preserved the same escape risk for
project roots nested inside a larger repo. gitignore_stays_within_root_boundary
proves an ancestor .gitignore (even with a .git marker) is neither read
nor mutated, and was confirmed to fail against the pre-fix
single-argument find_or_create_gitignore before the fix was applied.

fix(release): detect unpublished version drift + dependency-ordered dry-run guard (#3568)

* fix(release): detect unpublished version drift + dependency-ordered dry-run guard

Adds `trusty-publish-guard`, a new internal (publish = false) crate that
detects the #3366 defect class: a workspace crate whose Cargo.toml version
is already live on crates.io, but whose local src/ tree no longer matches
what was actually published under that version number. This is exactly what
happened to trusty-common (0.23.3, later re-observed at 0.23.7) and
trusty-agents-common (0.2.2): source commits landed on main without a
version bump while the old version was already published, so
`cargo publish --dry-run` for a downstream crate (trusty-mpm) failed with
"symbol not found" errors for symbols that only existed in the drifted,
unpublished source.

Confirmed still live on current main: running the new checker against this
workspace found 8 of 17 publishable crates currently drifted this way,
including trusty-common itself (commit 12e9d37d added embedder-module
source on top of the already-published 0.23.7 without bumping the version).
That pre-existing drift is now visible in the tool's own manual run output
(see PR description) but is NOT fixed by this PR — bumping 8 crates'
versions is a separate, larger effort out of scope for this issue and
likely to collide with other in-flight work.

Design:
- All crates.io access is isolated behind a `PublishedFetcher` trait
  (crates/trusty-publish-guard/src/fetch.rs); the extraction/diff/decision
  engine (src/lib.rs) is unit-tested against an in-memory fake tarball, no
  network required. A lookup failure fails CLOSED (never silently coerced
  into a pass) — see the "prefer FAILS LOUDLY over warns" design constraint.
- Wired via scripts/check-version-parity.sh + make version-parity-check, and
  automatically on every push to main via
  .github/workflows/version-parity.yml (push-to-main only, not pull_request
  — this check is only meaningful against what actually landed on main, and
  the issue's own proposal explicitly recommends avoiding per-PR noise).

Also adds scripts/publish-dry-run-order.sh (+ `make publish-dry-run-order`):
computes a topological publish order from `cargo metadata` and runs
`cargo publish --dry-run -p <crate>` per crate in dependency order, stopping
at the first failure. This addresses the RELATED but distinct 2026-07-20
publish-ordering incident (a crate published before a sibling it depends on
was live) by making the previously-manual ordering recipe
(.claude/skills/cargo-publish/SKILL.md "Cross-Crate Publish Ordering")
mechanical. Kept as a manual preflight (like the existing
check-publish-ready.sh / preflight-publish.sh scripts) rather than
CI-automated: packaging every publishable crate's tarball on every push is
comparatively expensive and only meaningful immediately before a release,
unlike the continuously-relevant version-parity check.

Not touched: check-publish-ready.sh and preflight-publish.sh already cover
"publish only from merged main" and "version not already live" — no changes
needed there.

* fix(release): enforce tag-ancestry + dependency-ordered dry-run in release.yml

Scope extension on #3366: converts two more pieces of tribal knowledge into
actual CI enforcement inside .github/workflows/release.yml, which an audit
confirmed never ran `cargo publish`/`--dry-run` anywhere and never verified
a pushed tag came from merged main.

1. New `preflight` job (needs: setup; everything else now needs it via
   `build`'s updated `needs: [setup, preflight]`, cascading through
   `release`/`homebrew-bump`'s existing `needs.build.result` checks):

   - Ancestry guard: fetches full history and runs
     `git merge-base --is-ancestor` on the tagged commit (dereferenced via
     `HEAD^{commit}`, never trusting `github.sha` or a naive
     `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` comparison, which can never match on a
     tag push and would silently disable every release) against the true
     `origin/main` tip. A tag from an unmerged branch now fails loudly and
     skips the entire pipeline instead of firing it. No-ops (documented, not
     silently skipped) on workflow_dispatch, which has no tag to check.
   - Resolves the tagged crate's real crates.io package identity (`name`,
     `publish`) directly from its Cargo.toml, independent of the binary-
     release allowlist (`bundled` flag) above — a library-only crate like
     trusty-common is `bundled=true` (no standalone binary) but is exactly
     the kind of real, publishable package #3366 was about.

2. New `publish-dry-run` job (needs: [setup, preflight]; runs
   scripts/publish-dry-run-order.sh, scoped to just the tagged crate + its
   publishable dependency closure) converts "always dry-run first, in
   dependency order" from a documented recipe in
   .claude/skills/cargo-publish/SKILL.md into something that fires
   automatically on every `*-v*` tag push, independent of whether a human
   remembered to run the equivalent `make` target. Scoping to one crate's
   closure (not the whole workspace, and not per-PR) is what keeps this
   affordable: it runs exactly once, exactly when a release is actually
   happening. Deliberately NOT a dependency of build/release/homebrew-bump —
   a failing crates.io dry-run says nothing about whether the GitHub binary
   tarball is safe to build, and coupling them would import crates.io's
   documented propagation lag into the binary-release path as pure
   flakiness. Its own failure still turns the tag's workflow run red.

Adversarial review of #3568 (WARN, 2 findings), both addressed here.

HIGH — SKIP_UI_BUILD made the publish-dry-run job blind to UI bundle
staleness for trusty-search/trusty-memory/trusty-analyze/trusty-console.
Investigated both options the review offered rather than picking blind:

- "Install pnpm, let cargo publish rebuild for real" is STRUCTURALLY
  IMPOSSIBLE for trusty-search and trusty-console specifically — confirmed
  via `cargo package --list -p trusty-console`: their Cargo.toml `include`
  ships only the pre-built `ui-dist/`/`ui/dist/` bundle, `ui/src` is never
  even in the tarball. This isn't a CI shortcut that could be relaxed; it's
  what `cargo publish` (real or dry-run) already does today, matching
  docs/reference/release-workflow.md's existing SKIP_UI_BUILD=1 requirement
  for these crates.
- This confirms the drift risk is real, not hypothetical: `git log 28648d38..HEAD
  -- crates/trusty-search/ui/src` shows the Foundry v2 token migration
  (972171e8) changed ui/src AFTER crates/trusty-search/ui-dist/ was last
  regenerated (28648d38, 2026-07-07) — a real, currently-live staleness gap,
  reproduced locally: a fresh `pnpm run build` from current ui/src produces
  different asset hashes/content than the committed ui-dist/.

Fix: new `ui-freshness-check` job, scoped to the four UI-embedding crates
only, needs: [setup, preflight]. Snapshots the committed embed directory
(ui-dist/ for trusty-search per its build.rs's copy-from-ui/dist step,
ui/dist/ directly for the other three — confirmed per-crate via their
build.rs), runs a real `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm run build`
from current ui/src (same toolchain-setup pattern ci.yml's same-day
ui-checks job established, issue #3508/#3571), then `diff -rq`s the
snapshot against the fresh output. Fails loudly on any difference, including
a build failure (the more common and more dangerous form of drift).

This deliberately does NOT attempt a hash-normalizing comparator:
ci.yml's ui-checks job (merged the same day, #3571) already evaluated and
rejected naive rebuild-then-diff for exactly these crates, because Vite's
content-hashed filenames can legitimately shift across a toolchain patch
bump with no real behavior change — a real, documented flakiness risk this
job does not solve. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` bounds (does not
eliminate) that risk to Node-runtime-version drift specifically. Chose
fail-closed anyway (matching this PR's whole "fail loudly, no advisory
checks" design constraint) because the remedy is identical whether a
failure is a true or false positive: regenerate and commit the bundle. If a
false positive is ever actually observed, that's the trigger to build the
hash-normalizing comparator ci.yml deferred — documented explicitly in the
job's header rather than silently left as a surprise.

`publish-dry-run`'s header comment now explicitly states it provides ZERO
UI-freshness coverage and why, instead of leaving that gap implicit.
docs/reference/release-workflow.md and .claude/skills/cargo-publish/SKILL.md

mentioned SKIP_UI_BUILD at all, unlike the correct guidance already in

fix(trusty-agents): gworkspace OpenRPC discovery silently found zero tools (#3577) (#3586)

* fix(trusty-agents): teach the OpenRPC registry to parse the real methods[] wire format instead of a never-implemented tools[] shape

`DirectDriver::discover()` deserialized rpc.discover's raw result
directly into `EndpointManifest` via `serde_json::from_value`. Because
`EndpointManifest.tools` carries `#[serde(default)]`, that call silently
succeeded with `tools: vec![]` on every real server's response instead of
erroring — no endpoint anywhere in this codebase (trusty-memory,
trusty-search, trusty-gworkspace) has ever emitted the bespoke
`{"tools": [...]}` shape the type expected. All three emit standard
OpenRPC 1.3.2 (`{"openrpc", "info", "methods": [...]}`) — trusty-memory
and trusty-search via the shared `trusty_common::mcp::openrpc` builder
built specifically to keep every server's manifest identically shaped,
and trusty-gworkspace via its own structurally-identical implementation.
Practical effect: the `gworkspace` endpoint (enabled by default since
#3056) discovered zero tools in production.

Endpoint survey (Part A): only `[[tool_registry.endpoints]]` entries with
`driver = "direct"` go through this discovery path — trusty-memory,
trusty-search (both currently `enabled = false`, pending `--rpc` mode)
and gworkspace (`enabled = true`). `[[mcp.services]]` entries (trusty-mpm,
granola-notes, duetto-memory) are a separate, unaffected mechanism. Since
every current AND planned `direct` endpoint already speaks OpenRPC, and a
shared crate exists specifically to keep them that way, teaching the
client to consume real OpenRPC is the durable fix: the next OpenRPC
server added to the registry works for free, versus a per-server
emit-side change that leaves the underlying client bug for the next
endpoint to rediscover.

Changes:
- `discovery::parse_manifest` (new) recognizes a top-level `methods`
  array (the real shape) or `tools` array (the legacy/still-tested
  shape); a payload with NEITHER key returns a hard `Err` naming the
  endpoint and the top-level keys actually present — the exact condition
  that used to silently deserialize to zero tools.
- `discovery::method_to_tool` converts one OpenRPC method into a
  `DiscoveredTool`: reconstructs a JSON Schema `input_schema` from
  `params[]`, takes `output_schema` from `result.schema`, and resolves
  `scope` from `x-scopes` (generic dotted string, used as-is) or
  `x-google-scopes` (OAuth URLs, mapped via the new `google_scope`
  module).
- `google_scope::dotted_scope_for_google_scopes` maps a tool's Google
  OAuth scope URLs to one dotted scope (e.g. `google.gmail.write`).
  Every gworkspace OAuth scope except `userinfo.profile` is the
  full-access (never `.readonly`) variant of its API, so access is
  classified `write` by what the OAuth grant PERMITS, not by what a
  given tool call happens to do today — a read-labeled tool whose
  behavior later drifts to also write must not silently escape a

* fix(supervisor): a failed respawn after a wedge-kill silently ended supervision without give-up

Root cause of the residual CI flake in the concurrent-fallback test (and
a real production bug, independent of any test): supervision_loop's
top-of-loop match on `child_slot` treated an EMPTY slot as unconditional
proof of an explicit shutdown and returned immediately — before this fix,
that was true only for the cooperative-shutdown path. But the `Unhealthy`
(wedge-kill) branch also clears `child_slot` via `guard.take()` before
attempting a respawn; if that respawn attempt itself then failed to
produce a live child, the next loop iteration would see the same empty
slot and incorrectly `return` as if intentionally shut down — silently
abandoning crash-restart supervision without ever incrementing
consecutive_failures or reaching should_give_up/gave_up_tx. A daemon
could end up with a dead sidecar, no supervision, and no fallback signal
ever firing.

Adds `RestartTrigger::RespawnFailed` for this case: an empty slot with no
concurrent shutdown request in flight is now treated as one more
crash-cycle (counted, logged, subject to should_give_up) instead of a
silent early return. Reinstates the test's original 5s timeout and
removes the #[ignore] tag from
fallback_does_not_trip_on_concurrent_failures_before_supervisor_gives_up
now that the actual race is fixed at the source — 15/15 clean runs
(previously ~1-in-8 to ~1-in-10 spurious timeouts even with a widened 20s

* fix(trusty-installer): health gate and supervisor bootstrap use concrete install path, not PATH-shadowable name lookup

The web installer's health gate (trusty-common::update::verify_installed_binary)
and the trusty-mpm supervisor's downgrade-guard candidate version
(plist_bootstrap::resolve_tm_binary) both resolved the "candidate version" by
NAME after tctl install had already written the binary to a known, concrete
path — verify_installed_binary checks ~/.cargo/bin before ~/.local/bin, and
resolve_tm_binary tries `which tm` first. On a host with a pre-existing
`cargo install trusty-mpm` at ~/.cargo/bin/tm earlier on $PATH than the fresh
~/.local/bin/tm prebuilt install, both lookups silently read the STALE
binary, so the health gate "passed" against the wrong file and the supervisor
bootstrap compared the old version against itself and refused to update —
the documented `curl | sh` upgrade path became a silent no-op for exactly
the population most likely to run it.

Fix:
- New trusty_common::update::verify_installed_binary_at_path probes a KNOWN,
  CONCRETE path directly (no name resolution, no PATH fallback). install_one
  now health-gates the exact path download::try_install_prebuilt reports
  having written (or the exact cargo bin dir for the cargo-install fallback),
  and hard-errors if the reported version does not match what the installer
  believes it just placed — never a silent pass.
- install_mpm_supervisor / install_mpm_supervisor_macos now take the
  just-installed tm_path as a parameter instead of re-deriving it via
  resolve_tm_binary's `which tm` lookup, so the downgrade-guard candidate
  version is immune to PATH order.
- upgrade_one's non-daemon branches (tctl upgrade) get the same concrete-path
  treatment for consistency; the daemon-restart path (upgrade_and_restart,
  shared with trusty-memory/trusty-search's own self-upgrade tool) is
  intentionally left on the name-based primitive as a separate, larger-blast-
  radius follow-up.
- New commands::shadow_check module: after a successful install, detects
  whether a plain shell invocation of the binary name would actually resolve
  to the just-installed file or a stale, earlier-PATH copy. A genuine shadow
  is reported loudly (naming both paths and both versions) and flips the
  member's outcome — and the process exit code — to a failure, matching this
  codebase's established policy (#2566, #2560) that a "looks installed,
  actually not live" condition must never be a silent success.

Regression coverage reproduces the realistic shape the prior isolated-HOME
E2E missed: an isolated home directory that ALSO contains a stale, older
binary in a directory placed earlier on a synthetic $PATH than the install
prefix (crates/trusty-installer/tests/path_shadow_e2e.rs,

a real trusty-embedderd-py child (torch+MPS, hundreds of MB-GB). On a probe

fix(trusty-mpm): stable daemon-lifetime session numbering in tm ls (#3044)

* fix(trusty-mpm): stable daemon-lifetime session numbering in tm ls (closes #3034)

Session numbers in `tm ls` (both the static table and the interactive
picker) were previously a plain positional index recomputed on every
fetch, so deleting a session shifted every later row's number — an
operator (or PM agent) holding a number from an earlier listing could
act on the wrong session.

The daemon now owns the numbering: a new in-memory-only `SlotRegistry`
on `SessionManager` assigns each session a stable slot the first time
it is listed, and never reuses a number for the life of the daemon
process (no persistence, so numbering resets cleanly on restart). The
`GET /api/v1/sessions/managed` list endpoint observes the FULL,
unfiltered record set into the registry before applying any
`?source_id=` filter, then returns one row per known slot — live rows
carry the real summary, and a slot whose session has disappeared from
the store (hard-delete, decommission-reap, or prune — any removal
path) renders as a `deleted: true` tombstone with blank fields.

The CLI's static table and interactive picker (shared by `tm ls` and
bare `tm`) both render the daemon-assigned `slot` instead of a
recomputed index, show a `-- deleted --` placeholder for a tombstoned
row, and resolve every typed number (including `d<N>` delete) by
searching for that `slot` value rather than doing index arithmetic —
so a number that resolves to a tombstone produces a clear
`SlotDeleted` error instead of silently falling through to whichever
session now occupies a neighboring position.

* fix(trusty-code): reject symlinked plugin leaf files, CWE-59 (#3547)

Re-review after the 4 prior fixes confirmed them closed, but found a
different vector: discover_agents/load_plugin_agent and
discover_one_plugin_skills/resolve_plugin_skill_body read discovered
.md/SKILL.md files with std::fs::read_to_string and test with
is_dir()/is_file() — all of which follow symlinks. A hostile plugin can
ship agents/leak.md (or skills/leak/SKILL.md, or make the skill directory
itself a symlink) pointing at an arbitrary host file (e.g. ~/.ssh/id_rsa).
The existing directory-path guard (safe_plugin_subdir) and name guard
(is_valid_namespaced_name) both pass for this — they guard the directory
and the name, not the leaf FILE identity — and since dispatch is wired,
the target's content would reach an LLM prompt verbatim.

Fix: new plugins::path_is_contained canonicalizes the leaf path and
requires it stay contained within the already-validated agents_dir/
skills_dir. Because canonicalize resolves every symlink in the path (not
just the final component), one check per call site catches a symlinked
leaf file, a symlinked intermediate directory (skills/<name> itself), or
both. Applied at every point a discovered file's content is actually
read: plugins::agents::load_plugin_agent (covers both the agents.list
listing path and the find_plugin_agent_config dispatch path, since both
route through it), plugins::skills::discover_one_plugin_skills (the
skills.list listing path), and plugins::skills::resolve_plugin_skill_body
(the use_skill resolution path, with a second independent check as
defense in depth on top of the discovery-level exclusion).

Also fixes a bug this surfaced: runner::agent_config_exists treated
Some(Err(_)) (found but rejected) as "exists", letting a symlink-rejected
namespaced name slip past delegate_to_agent's pre-flight gate. Now
requires Some(Ok(_)) for a namespaced name.

* fix(embedder): two-tier .ready recheck + progress-aware shutdown watchdog

Re-review fast-follow addressing two MEDIUM trade-offs on PR #3529 before
merge, both localized to the sidecar shutdown/bootstrap path.

FIX 1 — .ready smoke check re-imported torch on every respawn
(crates/trusty-embedderd-py/src/bootstrap.rs):

- ensure_venv() is called by the trusty-embedderd-py LAUNCHER binary on
  EVERY respawn (crash-restart, post-idle-shutdown re-spawn) — a short-lived
  process that execs into python right after. The prior `.ready` recheck ran
  `import sentence_transformers` (which imports torch) on every such call,
  duplicating a large slice of cold-start cost and undercutting the
  1800s-default idle-shutdown rationale (cheap restarts).
- Split into two variants: ensure_venv() now uses the CHEAP, torch-free
  verify_venv_alive() (installed-package marker-file check + a bare
  `python -c "import sys; sys.exit(0)"` liveness probe, bounded to 5s) on
  every respawn. ensure_venv_eager() — called ONCE by trusty-search's daemon
  at `start` (commands/start/embedder.rs) — keeps the FULL
  verify_full_import_smoke() (real `import sentence_transformers`, bounded
  to 10s), since that cost is paid only once per daemon lifetime.
- 6 new/renamed unit tests in bootstrap_tests.rs cover both recheck depths
  and the corruption/rebuild path for each.

FIX 2 — shutdown join bounded total drain time, not hang-detection
(crates/trusty-embedderd-py/python/trusty_embed_sidecar/sidecar.py):

- A flat `join(timeout=10s)` bounded the ENTIRE drain of up to max_queue=64
  legitimately-slow encodes; a reindex burst arriving at SIGTERM could
  exceed 10s of healthy work and force os._exit, dropping in-flight (not
  hung) replies.
- Replaced with a progress-aware watchdog: the worker marks a monotonic
  _ProgressTracker timestamp after each completed item;
  _join_with_progress_watchdog polls in 1s increments and only force-exits
  once NO item has completed for 20s (a genuine wedge, e.g. a hung MPS
  encode()) — bounding on lack of progress, not total drain time.
- New tests (test_shutdown_watchdog.py): a slow-but-progressing worker
  drains fully without force-exit; a truly wedged worker force-exits within
  the no-progress window. Both fail (ImportError) against the prior flat-
  timeout sidecar.py and pass against this one.

fix(trusty-mpm): zombie session restart 409s in interactive picker (#3534)

* fix(trusty-mpm): zombie session restart 409s in interactive picker (closes #3531)

The interactive session picker offers "restart <name> (stopped)" for a
zombie session (tmux window gone, daemon record still active/provisioning),
but the restart then rejects with "cannot resume a session in state
'active'". Root cause: #3302 made the list/get endpoints reconcile the
DISPLAYED `state` against live tmux for UX (so a running session never
reads "(stopped)") — but that same reconciled value was also fed into the
#2001 zombie-vs-plain-restart classification (guided_resume::plan_resume),
collapsing a zombie down to the same "stopped" string a genuinely stopped
session shows. The picker's restart selection then took the plain restart
path instead of the auto-reconcile path, and the daemon's /resume (which
validates the REAL persisted state) rejected it with a 409.

`SessionSummary`/`ManagedSessionSummary` gain a `persisted_state` field
carrying the raw, un-reconciled state captured once at conversion time,
untouched by the later display reconciliation. The CLI's resume/restart
classification (shared by the interactive picker, the bare-`tm` guided
default, and `tm session(s) resume <id>`) now keys off `persisted_state`
instead of the display value, so the #2001 auto-reconcile (/runtime-stop
then /resume) fires correctly instead of dead-ending. Falls back to
`state` when talking to an older daemon that predates the field.

Manual recovery for anyone hitting this on an older build: `tm session
stop <id>` (forces the stale record to Stopped via /runtime-stop), then
resume/restart normally.

Adds a hermetic end-to-end regression test reproducing the exact zombie
shape (tmux absent, daemon state active) against a real daemon instance,
plus pure-function unit tests for the classification fix.

Closes #3531

* fix(trusty-gworkspace): guard tokens.json against concurrent writers, fix orphaned default on remove

TokenStorage's read-modify-write of tokens.json had no locking: two
concurrent writers (e.g. two profiles refreshing at once, in the same
or different processes) could each load() the map before either
save()d, silently losing one profile's write. TokenStorage::update()
now serialises callers in-process and holds an advisory cross-process
lock on a sidecar tokens.json.lock file for the full load-mutate-save
cycle; every mutation path (OAuthManager::refresh, consent persist,
CLI accounts default/remove) is routed through it.

Separately, removing the current default profile used to leave zero
default entries, silently breaking BaseClient::resolve_stored's
default-profile fallback for every subsequent call with no explicit
account. remove_profile() now deterministically reassigns the default
to another remaining profile (alphabetically next) when this happens.

storage.rs is split into storage/mod.rs + storage/tests.rs (mirroring
the existing oauth/flow/mod.rs + flow/tests.rs split) to keep the
production file under the repo's 500-SLOC cap after the new logic.

Closes #3502.

perf(embedder): default to non-quantized MiniLM (drop INT8) (#3511)

* perf(embedder): default to non-quantized MiniLM (drop INT8 default)

The default fastembed model, AllMiniLML6V2Q (INT8, dynamically
quantized), is measurably worse than the non-quantized fp32 variant on
the CPU EP this model actually runs on (CoreML's GetCapability rejects
the INT8 op set outright, so CoreML contributes nothing regardless of
platform): ~2.1x slower (MatMulInteger/DynamicQuantizeLinear
dequant-requant ops are themselves expensive) and less accurate (0.9897
mean cosine similarity vs a genuine sentence-transformers reference,
vs 1.000000 for fp32 in a real, verified run on this repo's own cached
model files).

Adds resolve_default_embedding_model(), which resolves
EmbeddingModel::AllMiniLML6V2 (fp32) by default, or AllMiniLML6V2Q when
TRUSTY_EMBEDDER_MODEL=int8/quantized/q is set (an explicit opt-in for
operators who need the smaller ~23MB footprint vs fp32's ~87MB more
than they need speed or accuracy). The existing two-model
fallback-on-init-failure safety net is preserved, just parameterised by
the resolved primary/fallback pair instead of hardcoded model names.

fp16 was considered (per the #3486 experiment) and deliberately not
chosen: the CPU EP this model runs on has no native fp16 compute path,
and the experiment's fp16 arm required a fragile hand-built
ORT-optimizer conversion pipeline fastembed does not ship or support
loading natively. AllMiniLML6V2 (fp32) is fastembed's own natively-
shipped non-quantized variant.

RequireStaticInputShapes and all existing batch caps are unchanged
(the #3486 experiment showed relaxing static shapes reproduces a
#24-style RSS blowup — not touched here).

fix(embedder): platform-conditional ORT intra-op thread default (#3500)

macOS/CoreML embedder sessions were unconditionally pinned to a single
ORT intra-op thread by PR #1668's global thread-pool commit. That pin
fixes a real deadlock, but the deadlock is specific to the CUDA EP on
AL2023 Linux + a dynamically-loaded ORT runtime (code-intelligence
#1542) — it does not exist on the CoreML/CPU-EP path used everywhere
else. Applying it unconditionally throttled macOS embedding throughput
~3.5x for no safety benefit (issue #3493 P0; independently reproduced
in the parallel #3486 CoreML/fp16 experiment's threading-only A/B).

default_ort_intra_threads() now resolves to 1 only when the
embedder-cuda feature is compiled in (the only build that can ever
register the CUDA EP and hit the PR #1668 barrier deadlock); every
other build (Apple Silicon CoreML, generic CPU-only) resolves to
std::thread::available_parallelism(), matching fastembed's own
per-session default. TRUSTY_ORT_INTRA_THREADS remains the escape
hatch to override either default.

Also fixes several stale bare "#1542" comment references that would
autolink to this repo's own unrelated issue #1542 (a BM25 tokenizer
bug) instead of the actual fix, PR #1668.

* fix(trusty-tui): close stuck-busy deadlock exposed by the busy-gating fix

Re-review on PR #3477 found the concurrency fix's own FIX 1 (block a
second submit while busy) exposed a HIGH-severity deadlock: ReplApp::busy
is cleared ONLY by a terminal AssistantOutput{done:true} reaching the
reducer, but dispatch_pending's Ok(true) arm did nothing on task
completion, trusting the engine to have already sent one. Three real,
spec-required CodeEngine paths return Ok(true) without ever sending a
terminal chunk (/workstream list/activate, a reconnect-exhausted event
pump, a daemon-initiated session cancellation — all push only
StatusMessage/WorkstreamUpdated), so any of those left busy stuck true
forever and the busy-gating meant the user could never submit again
(recoverable only by the accident of Ctrl-C).

Fixed at the dispatch layer (the shared contract every TuiEngine is
subject to, not by trusting each engine to self-terminate):
forward_while_current_generation now tracks a saw_terminal flag,
flipped when it relays a done:true AssistantOutput or Quit.
dispatch_pending's completion step drops its turn_tx clone and awaits
the forwarder to fully drain (the synchronization point that makes
saw_terminal race-free), then — only if no terminal was seen AND this
turn's generation is still live — sends a new dedicated
ReplEvent::TurnFinished that clears busy/streaming_idx and touches
nothing else (not a reused empty AssistantOutput, which would push a
stray blank chat entry). The Err path goes through the same
drain-then-check sequence for consistency.

Net invariant: every handle_input completion path — Ok(true) with a
done chunk, Ok(true) with none, Ok(false), and Err — deterministically
leaves busy == false once no task is in flight.

Added end-to-end regression tests driving the real reducer through the
real channel for all three previously-broken shapes (zero events,
status-message-only, and engine error), plus direct forwarder tests for
the saw_terminal flag. Documented the tx-lifetime contract on
TuiEngine::handle_input this relies on. Rebased onto latest main (Slice
7 #3476).

* fix(trusty-tui): close TOCTOU race in the stuck-busy safety net's completion check

Final re-review on PR #3477 found the stuck-busy fix's own completion
arm had a check-then-act race: it loaded the shared generation counter
and compared it to the turn's own number before deciding whether to
send TurnFinished, on a spawned task with nothing synchronizing that
load against a concurrent cancel + resubmit both bumping the counter
in the gap before the send. A stale TurnFinished from turn N could
land after a newer turn N+2 was already in flight and clear its busy/
streaming_idx, reintroducing the streaming-splice corruption class
this whole PR closes.

Fixed by construction instead of narrowing the window: moved the
generation validation into the reducer, which runs serially on the
same task that bumps the counter, so there is no cross-thread
check-then-act at all.

- ReplEvent::TurnFinished now carries generation: u64; the completion
  task always sends it (stamped with its own turn number), no
  load-then-branch.
- TuiModel gained set_current_generation, called by dispatch_pending
  on the single serial event-loop task at the exact point it bumps the
  shared AtomicU64 (both the cancel and submit branches).
- ReplApp tracks current_generation; the reducer's TurnFinished arm
  clears busy/streaming_idx only if generation == current_generation,
  otherwise it's a no-op — a comparison that now runs serially against
  a value only ever written from the same task that reads it back.

Added a deterministic reducer-level regression test
(apply_turn_finished_with_stale_generation_is_ignored) proving a stale
TurnFinished is ignored once a newer generation is live — the point of
the by-construction fix is that this is the reducer's own logic, not a
live thread race that needs reproducing.

* fix(trusty-mpm): gitignore harness scaffolding + detect tracked collisions

tm writes composed agents (.claude/agents/), skills (.claude/skills/), and
output styles (.claude/output-styles/) directly into a project's working
tree. If any of those paths is ever committed, the next session's
regeneration writes the same path back as local content, and a later
`git merge --ff-only origin/main` aborts with "your local changes would be
overwritten" — the verified duetto-eve-agents#111 reproduction (28 commits
stranded, resolved only by manual `git rm -r --cached` + a hand-written
.gitignore).

Option 1 (prevent): `core::scaffold_gitignore::ensure_scaffold_gitignored`
appends a small, clearly-delimited managed block naming exactly the three
harness-owned subtrees to `<project_dir>/.gitignore` whenever `project_dir`
is a git working tree. Idempotent, and scoped narrowly so `.claude/settings.json`
and the project `.mcp.json` (legitimately shared, tracked config) are never
swept up. Wired into `prepare_session_inner` so every session launch keeps
the block current; a write failure is non-fatal and only logged.

Option 2 (detect): a new `scaffold_tracking` doctor probe computes the true
intersection of `git ls-files`-tracked scaffolding paths and the paths tm's
own agent/skill manifests (+ the bundled output-style list) say it
regenerates, and warns with the exact colliding paths plus a copy-pasteable
`git rm -r --cached` remediation. Warn-only — it never mutates the git
index itself, since an automated `git rm --cached` on a miscomputed path
set is exactly the destructive footgun the issue warns against. Split into
`daemon::doctor_scaffold_tracking` to keep `doctor.rs` from growing further.

fix(trusty-search): degrade file watcher loudly on network-mounted index roots (#3424)

* feat(trusty-search): detect network-mounted index roots and degrade the watcher loudly

The native file watcher (inotify/FSEvents) is a local-host-only kernel
mechanism and cannot observe writes made by another host onto a shared
EFS/NFS/SMB mount. Previously the watcher started successfully on such a
mount, the daemon reported healthy, and the watcher silently never fired
for cross-host changes.

Adds service::network_fs::classify_root, which detects a network-mounted
path via statfs (macOS f_fstypename; Linux f_type magic number plus a
/proc/mounts fallback for named network FUSE backends), using the
already-vendored `nix` crate (fs feature). Detection is conservative and
fails open to Local on any error or ambiguity (e.g. a bare `fuse` mount is
never flagged) so it can only ever produce a false negative, never block a
legitimate local watcher.

WatcherManager now refuses to start a watcher for a network-mounted root
instead of silently starting one that can never fire, and records the
actionable reason. The condition is surfaced on GET /health
(indexes_watcher_network_degraded, folded into the existing degraded
status convention) and GET /indexes/:id/status (watcher.*), naming
POST /indexes/:id/index-file and POST /indexes/:id/remove-file as the
supported next step.

Also officially documents those two endpoints (and the index_file /
remove_file MCP tools) as the supported, stability-committed
incremental-indexing path for network-mounted and build/serve-split
deployments, with a worked example, in README.md and CLAUDE.md's endpoint
catalogue.

* fix(trusty-code-gui): defer workstream activation until after task-run succeeds

Addresses code-critic PR #3375 review (HIGH): submit() force-activated
the newly-minted workstream BEFORE POST /tasks. If the task run then
failed, the flow stopped with an empty workstream left ACTIVE — force:true
had already unconditionally deactivated whatever was active before, with
no restore, and the error text never mentioned the stranded workstream.
Worse, retrying re-minted a whole new workstream from scratch (no id
reuse), so each retry compounded another orphan.

Fix: reorder to create -> run -> activate (activation deliberately LAST,
not second). Since task.run's workstream_id binds by id alone with no
activation precondition, deferring activation costs nothing and removes
both the activation-steal-on-failure and orphan-goes-active problems.

- pendingWorkstreamId/pendingWorkstreamName now persist across a
  create-succeeded-but-task-failed attempt, so a retry reuses the same
  workstream instead of minting another; only a failure at the create
  step itself causes the next attempt to mint fresh.
- The task-run error message now names the already-created workstream
  ("...was created but not activated; it will be reused if you retry").
- Strengthened NewWorkstreamForm.test.ts to assert the call SEQUENCE
  (create -> run -> activate, activation never fires before a successful
  task-run), that a task-run failure issues no activate call, and that a
  retry reuses the same workstream_id without a second POST /workstreams.
- Updated lib/new-workstream.ts, DOC-39 §7A, DOC-48 §8 Phase C+, and both
  CHANGELOGs to describe the corrected order.

fix(trusty-common): single canonical palace-id derivation so catch-up and memory daemon agree without git remote or env override (#3357)

Closes #1772

`trusty_common::catchup::derive_palace_id_for` (and a duplicate copy in
`trusty-code`'s `derive_palace_id_for_project`, which explicitly mirrored it)
each carried their own divergent 4th fallback: a RAW, unslugified
`file_name()` basename used whenever `derive_palace_id` returned `None`. The
memory daemon's `cwd_palace_slug_at` (trusty-memory) has no such fallback and

unslugified fallback could also leak a storage-unsafe token as a palace id.

and fall back only to a fixed, non-derived placeholder ("unknown-project")
when every precedence level yields `None` — never re-deriving anything from
the directory locally. `derive_palace_id` remains the single source of truth
for every real precedence level (env override > git owner/repo > parent/dir),
so catch-up and the daemon can no longer diverge on a real project.

Added unit tests proving agreement between the catch-up-path derivation and
a direct `derive_palace_id` call (the same call the daemon path makes) for
the no-remote/no-env case, plus regression tests confirming the env-override
and valid-git-remote cases are unchanged.

child. `find_claude_pid_in_tmux`'s `pgrep -P <pane_pid>` returned None

Adds an optional `gh_account` field to the project registration/config
(Project/ProjectConfig, register + PATCH routes, MCP project_register tool,
`tm projects register --gh-account`) that lets an operator pin which
gh-authenticated account a project's spawned sessions use. Bob regularly
switches between two GitHub accounts on the same machine; `gh auth switch`
is a single global pointer, so a concurrently-running session in a
different project tree kept flipping it under a running admin-merge.

At every managed session spawn/relaunch, core::gh_account::
resolve_gh_account_env_for_workspace detects the workspace's git origin,
matches it against the registered project, and — when gh_account is set —
resolves a token via `gh auth token -u <account>` and injects GH_TOKEN plus
GH_USER into the spawned Claude Code process's environment (the same `env`
prefix mechanism CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN already uses), so `gh` identity is
deterministic for that session's Bash-tool gh calls regardless of the
host's global gh auth switch state.

Resolution is fail-open throughout: a missing gh binary, an account that
isn't logged in, or any other failure logs a tracing::warn! and the spawn
proceeds without GH_TOKEN — it never blocks the session. Only the account
NAME is ever persisted; the token is resolved fresh from the keyring at
spawn time and never written to disk or logged.

* fix(trusty-mpm): eliminate double-kill-after-reap and pipe-conversion child leak in spawn_disclaim (#2997 review)

  spawned immediately after posix_spawnp succeeds, before the fd

* fix(trusty-common): make EmbedderSupervisor::shutdown reachable + don't respawn on intentional idle shutdown (closes #2979)

start_supervisor_task consumed self and returned nothing, so shutdown()
(also self-consuming) became unreachable the moment a caller detached
the background task -- the only way trusty-search ever used the type.
Its idle-shutdown watchdog worked around this with a raw SIGTERM/SIGKILL
by OS PID, which raced the supervision loop's child.wait() and could be
misclassified as a crash, respawning the sidecar the watchdog had just
stopped.

start_supervisor_task now returns a SupervisorHandle whose shutdown()
flips a watch::Receiver<bool> the supervision loop selects on (both
while waiting on the child and during the respawn back-off sleep). The
loop kills and reaps the child itself and returns without ever entering
the crash-restart path, so an intentional shutdown can no longer be
misclassified. trusty-search's idle_watchdog now calls
SupervisorHandle::shutdown() instead of killing by raw PID.

* fix(trusty-common): stop shutdown-channel-close busy-spin in supervision_loop (#3023 review)

A second code-critic pass on PR #3023 found: watch::Receiver::changed()
resolves Ready(Err(_)) on every poll once its sender closes, which happens
whenever a SupervisorHandle is dropped without .shutdown() ever being
awaited. Both select! branches racing shutdown_rx.changed() ignored the
Result, so an immediately-ready Err never yields to the scheduler and
busy-spins a tokio worker for the child's remaining lifetime (HIGH). The
respawn back-off branch had the same root cause, but treating Err as "no
shutdown yet" skipped the intended back-off delay and respawned
immediately every pass (MEDIUM).

Both select! arms now distinguish Err (channel closed, no shutdown
requested) from Ok(true) (shutdown requested) via a shutdown_closed flag
that permanently disables the branch after a close, and the back-off arm
sleeps out the full delay on Err instead of skipping it.

the app_pid_slot store(0) ordering relies on do_spawn's async latency (LOW).

Regression test: supervisor_dropped_handle_does_not_busy_spin drops a
SupervisorHandle without shutdown() and asserts a cfg(test)-only iteration
counter stays bounded over 300ms, then confirms supervision still
functions (kills the child out-of-band and asserts a respawn). Verified
this test fails (335k+ iterations/300ms) against the pre-fix code and
passes cleanly against the fix, run 5x with no flakes.

* fix(trusty-review): reject path-traversal in repo-sourced template/voice names (SECURITY)

Path::join silently discards the base directory when the joined component is
itself absolute (base.join("/abs/HOSTILE.md") -> /abs/HOSTILE.md) and never
collapses `..`. Both the review-template name ([review].template) and the
voice-package name ([voice].package) can flow unsanitized from a
repo-discovered .trusty-review.toml -- attacker-controlled, since any PR
author can commit that file -- into ReviewTemplateLoader::load /
VoiceLoader::load's path joins, then the file contents get appended into the
LLM system prompt. An absolute or ../ value allows arbitrary local file read
(including a file committed into the PR under review) -> prompt injection.

Adds crate::identifier::is_valid_identifier: a strict allow-list (ASCII
alphanumeric/-/_ only, non-empty) applied at two layers:

- Config resolution (config::voice::load_voice_package,
  config::review_template::load_review_template): a repo/env/file/cli value
  that fails validation is rejected with a tracing::warn! and resolution
  falls through to the next precedence tier, rather than propagating the
  hostile value onto ReviewConfig.
- The loaders themselves (voice::loader::VoiceLoader::load,
  review_template::ReviewTemplateLoader::load), as defense-in-depth for
  every caller regardless of source: a new InvalidName error variant is
  returned BEFORE any path join or filesystem access (including the
  extra_dirs loop).

Also corrects the review-template override path in RunArgs's doc comment and
the README (both claimed ~/.trusty-review/templates/review/, but the loader
actually uses dirs::config_dir() -- ~/.config/... on Linux, ~/Library/
Application Support/... on macOS).

never post to GitHub, with no separate posting check needed.

tempfile before its per-model loop, since stdin can only be read to EOF once.

* fix(trusty-review): guard git-range args against option injection (--end-of-options) + parse tests (refs #2993)

--base/--head values were concatenated into a single positional arg with no

* fix(trusty-code): skip \ No newline at end of file footer in unified-diff applier

parse_hunks (crates/trusty-code/src/tools/fs/edit_format/diff.rs)
hard-errored on any hunk-body line whose first byte was not
space/-/+. This included the standard git diff footer marker line
`\ No newline at end of file`, so a real git-diff-style payload
containing that marker failed to apply with a spurious
DiffHunkHeader error instead of being applied.

The marker is metadata about the preceding line (that it lacked a
trailing newline in the source), not a hunk-body line with content to
apply, so it is skipped rather than treated as malformed.

#2975 code-critic HIGH finding: an initial version of this fix only
skipped the marker at parse time and decided the OUTPUT's
trailing-newline state solely from the ORIGINAL file's trailing byte —
but the marker's POSITION carries meaning: after a `-` line, the OLD
file lacked a trailing newline; after a `+` line, the NEW file lacks
one. A hunk that changes which side lacks a trailing newline (e.g.
`-b` + footer + `+B`, removing the no-newline state, or `+b` + footer,
introducing it) silently produced the wrong final byte — a regression
from the pre-#2150 fail-closed behavior (hard error, no corruption).

Fixed by tracking, per hunk, which line kind (`Removal`/`Addition`/
`Context`) each footer marker followed (`Hunk::old_tail_no_newline` /
`new_tail_no_newline`). `apply_unified_diff` now only overrides the
default trailing-newline decision when the LAST hunk reaches
end-of-file and carries an explicit marker: new/both-side marked ->
no trailing newline; old-side-only marked -> the diff removes the
no-newline state, so the output DOES get one; no marker -> unchanged
default. Documented explicitly in both functions' docs.

Added apply_footer_marker_after_removal_only_forces_trailing_newline,
apply_footer_marker_after_addition_removes_trailing_newline, and
apply_footer_marker_on_both_sides_keeps_no_trailing_newline, covering
both state-change directions plus the unchanged case.

* fix(ci): fastembed pre-seed fail-soft was inert — set -e neutralized inside if-condition

Code-critic review of PR #2981 caught a HIGH-severity bug in the
fail-soft wrapper added for #2554: invoking `seed_models` directly as
an `if` condition (`if seed_models; then … else … fi`) silently
disables bash's `errexit` for every command inside the function body,
even though the function re-declares `set -euo pipefail` itself. Per
the bash manual, "this behavior applies even when the failing command
is ... contained within a shell function called by a command in the
list" (i.e. an if/while test). Reproduced empirically with a minimal
repro before applying the fix.

Effect of the bug: a mid-download curl failure was silently swallowed,
execution fell through to the function's final `du -sh ... || true`
(always exit 0), the function reported success, the `::warning::`
annotation never fired, and a partial/corrupt cache directory would
have been persisted by actions/cache's post-step and served as a false
"hit" on every subsequent run until the cache key rotated.

Fix: invoke seed_models as a plain statement in a subshell — never as
a conditional's test — and capture its exit status explicitly:

    set +e; ( seed_models ); rc=$?; set -e
    if [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ]; then rm -rf "${CACHE_DIR}"; echo "::warning::…"; fi

Also removes the (now-guaranteed-partial) cache directory on failure
so actions/cache never persists a corrupt tree under the run's key —
an absent cache is a safe "miss" next run; a partial one would look
like a permanent false "hit".

Re-verified end-to-end (not just the minimal repro): extracted the
full pre-seed script body, forced every curl call to fail via a fake
curl on PATH, and ran it under bash 5.3 (matching the Ubuntu runner,
not macOS's stock bash 3.2) — confirmed the retry loop exhausts, the
::warning:: fires with the correct rc, the step exits 0, and the
cache directory is removed.

Also corrects a LOW finding: the PR description claimed the pre-fix
boolean in_block algorithm reported 3 SLOC on the nested-comment
fixture; running that exact algorithm against the exact fixture shows
it actually reports 2 (the stray outer `*/` was miscounted as a code
line). PR body corrected via gh pr edit.

feat(trusty-search): native document indexing — pdf/docx/xlsx text extraction (#2932)

* feat(trusty-search): native document indexing — pdf/docx/xlsx text extraction

The walker previously hard-skipped .pdf (BINARY_EXTS) and silently dropped
.docx/.xls/.xlsx/.xlsm (absent from SOURCE_EXTS), and the live watcher's
handle_modified assumed UTF-8 text via read_to_string, which fails outright
on OOXML zip containers. Office documents in an indexed repo were therefore
invisible to search with no workaround short of pre-extracting text outside
the daemon.

Add a native extraction layer (crates/trusty-search/src/core/extract/) with
one submodule per format:

- pdf: pdf-extract (pure-Rust, no poppler/pdfium shell-out). A PDF whose
  extracted text is empty after trimming (most likely scanned/image-only;
  OCR is out of scope for v1) surfaces a warning instead of silently
  indexing nothing.
- docx: a small streaming quick-xml parse of word/document.xml inside the
  zip container, matching this workspace's own-the-parsing convention
  rather than pulling in a full docx crate for single-purpose paragraph
  extraction. Headers/footers are out of scope for v1.
- xlsx/xls/xlsm: calamine, rendering each sheet as a `== <sheet> ==`
  section of tab-joined rows so downstream chunking keeps rows grouped
  under their sheet instead of losing structure to a flat prose dump.

extract::read_content is the single seam both service::reindex::batch and
service::watch_loop call through instead of read_to_string, so the two

Closes #2922

- Serialize UsearchStore::save() end-to-end (save_lock) so a shutdown
  flush racing an in-flight incremental persist for the same store can
  never interleave tmp-file writes or race a stale rename past a fresh
  one.
- Scale the graceful-shutdown per-index flush deadline by each index's
  on-disk HNSW snapshot size (30s floor + 1s/20MB, 20min cap) instead
  of a flat 10s, honoring TRUSTY_SHUTDOWN_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_SECS as an
  explicit override; flush indexes with bounded concurrency
  (TRUSTY_SHUTDOWN_FLUSH_CONCURRENCY, default 4) instead of strictly
  sequentially.
- Detect a truncated/corrupt on-disk HNSW snapshot on load via a
  pre-view() size floor (scaled from the sidecar's own vector
  count/dim so it never false-positives on tiny test/dev snapshots)
  plus a post-view zero-vector-vs-populated-sidecar guard. The
  pre-view floor also fixes a real SIGSEGV: usearch::Index::view() on
  a small truncated file does not reliably return Err.
- Propagate a new CodeIndexer::hnsw_load_failed flag from
  build_store_for_entry through build_indexer_from_entry so
  hnsw_snapshot_ready no longer trusts bare file existence — /health
  and the warm-boot stage classifier now report semantic search
  not-ready when a snapshot silently fell back to empty, instead of

The tcode UI's core bet is that a change is explained by the agent, the
searches, and the memories that produced it — not by the prompt. The event
stream could not support that: tool events named no agent, and the two
retrieval tools flattened everything they knew into truncated prose.

Agent attribution (the keystone):

- `ToolEventSink`'s hooks take `agent` as a per-call PARAMETER, not sink
  state, because ONE `Arc<dyn ToolEventSink>` is shared by the PM's loop and
  every delegated sub-agent's loop — a sink holding its own name could only
  ever report one of them. The dispatching `AgentLoop` is the only layer that
  knows its identity, so it passes it per call (`AgentLoop::with_agent`),
  wired at both production sites.
- `agent` is the agent NAME, matching the key the rest of the taxonomy
  already uses (`AgentSpawned.agent`, `PmDelegating.agent`,
  `LlmRequested.agent_name`) so a UI can join them directly. Unattributed
  loops emit the documented `UNATTRIBUTED_AGENT` sentinel, never "".

Structured retrieval events (additive — the generic events still fire
unchanged, so existing consumers see the same stream):
- `search_performed{agent, lane, query, hit_count, latency_ms}` — `lane` is
  the lane trusty-search ACTUALLY served: a semantic/symbol query answered by
  the stage-not-ready lexical retry (#2783) reports "lexical", not the mode
  the model asked for. `hit_count` is null when uncountable, never a
  misleading 0.
- `memory_recalled{agent, query, results:[{score, injected}]}` — `injected:
  false` means exactly "recalled but not entered into context". The scores and
  the drop-lowest-scored truncation already existed inside `recall_session`;
  they now escape the rendered text.

Tools report this via `ToolResult::with_telemetry`, which the loop forwards to
the new `ToolEventSink::tool_telemetry` hook. Tools stay pure functions of
their arguments — no sink, no session, no agent name — so attribution keeps
one source of truth and each tool stays unit-testable without a bus. The
fail-open paths attach no telemetry: they never reached a lane, so there is no
search to report.

`ToolResult::Success` becomes a struct variant; `ok`/`content`/`is_error` are
unchanged, so no tool call site moved. `tool_telemetry` has a default no-op

fix(trusty-code): bound re-delegation cap to retries, not total delegations (#2856)

* fix(trusty-code): bound re-delegation cap to retries, not total delegations

MAX_REDELEGATIONS = 3 was documented as bounding retries after failure, but
record_attempt incremented on every engineer invocation run-wide and was never
reset per call. A *successful* delegation therefore permanently consumed budget
a later one then lacked.

A PM using delegation for legitimate reconnaissance — the normal PM shape — was
silently guillotined: the 4th call was refused WITHOUT the inner runner ever
being invoked (zero engineer turns, no code written), and the latched signal
then fired run_task's with_stop_signal, halting the PM loop at the next turn
boundary — unrecoverable by design. L4 run-6 issued 3 read-only recon
delegations and had its 4th, the actual build, refused: partial/exit 6, 0/9
tests, 0/5 deliverables. Runs 3/4/5 succeeded only by luck of issuing one fewer
recon call. Cost: 2-in-7 total-loss runs caused by the harness, not the model.

This is the pre-existing #2265 design, not a #2805 regression; #2805 fixed the
symptom (the gratuitous post-completion re-delegate) and remains correct.

The fix separates two concerns that were conflated:

* MAX_REDELEGATIONS now bounds attempts within a SINGLE delegation, via a
  counter local to run_with_retries and reset at loop entry. Exhausting it is
  recoverable — it latches retry_budget_exhausted (informational, for the
  report label) but no longer stops the PM loop, matching the precedent of
  #2683/#2805's post-completion refusal.
* MAX_ENGINEER_INVOCATIONS = 12 (4x the per-delegation budget) bounds engineer
  invocations run-wide, preserving the cap's actual purpose: a genuinely
  failing engineer stays bounded. Only this ceiling — a condition no fresh
  delegation could clear — latches cap_reached and fires the stop signal.

assemble_report keys off both flags, so a genuinely retry-exhausted run still
reports partial/exit 6 with a deliverable and never downgrades to an opaque
run_failure. #2805's EngineerCompletionSignal success mapping is untouched.

Observability: the cap was completely silent — run-6's stderr had no trace of
it and the mechanism was only findable by cross-run forensics on the report's
task label. Both conditions now warn! to stderr.

Tests: successful_delegations_never_consume_a_later_delegations_budget is the
regression test (fails pre-fix on the 4th delegation). The fix #5 test is
rebuilt around the ceiling — it previously asserted pm_turns == 1, which
encoded this bug itself.

* fix(sld-lint): address code-critic findings (path escape, catalog self-label, HASH block scoping, ratchet semantics)

CRITICAL — absolute-path bypass of the traversal guard. Renamed
`sld::grammar::has_traversal` to `is_unsafe_path`, extending it to reject
absolute paths (Unix `/`, Windows `C:\`/`C:/`/UNC `\\`) in addition to `..`
traversal — `PathBuf::join` silently discards its base for an absolute
argument, so the old check let a `path: /etc/passwd.md` reference read
outside the repo via trusty-sld-lint's `root.join(path)` lookup closure.
Hardened that closure too (now `safe_read`): it canonicalizes both `root`
and the joined candidate and refuses to read unless the candidate is still
rooted under `root` — a second, independent layer that also catches a
symlink escape `is_unsafe_path`'s string-level check cannot see. Added
`grammar_rejects_absolute`, `safe_read_rejects_absolute`,
`safe_read_rejects_dotdot_escape`, and `safe_read_rejects_symlink_escape`
regression tests.

the first `DOC-<n>` occurrence anywhere in a file, so a `spec_refs:`
frontmatter cross-reference or a superseded-banner mention of another DOC-N
appearing before a spec's own title could misattribute it. Now scans only

feat(trusty-code): daemon-side directory inspection API (UI Phase-1) (#2859)

* feat(trusty-code): daemon-side directory inspection API (UI Phase-1)

Add `fs.list_dir`, a new `fs.*` JSON-RPC namespace on `/rpc` alongside
`session.*`/`task.*`, backing the UI's "Open a project" folder picker
(screen 7a).

The UI is a thin client: no UI target touches the filesystem directly,
including Tauri — which technically could, but must not, since that would
let the desktop build do something the web build cannot and fork one UI
into two behaviours. Browsing local disk to pick a project therefore has
to be a daemon call.

`fs.list_dir(path?, include_hidden?)` returns `{path, display_path,
parent, entries[{name, path, is_dir, is_git_repo}]}`. One response serves
both of 7a's jobs: `display_path`/`parent` drive the breadcrumb and
up-navigation, while `is_git_repo` is simultaneously the `git` badge and
the discriminator for the three-state project binding model (projectless
→ non-git dir → git repo). A non-git directory is a first-class success
with `is_git_repo: false`, never an error (#2728). `~` is expanded and
paths canonicalized server-side, matching the `expand_tilde` convention
already used in trusty-mpm and trusty-agents; `path` defaults to `~` so
the projectless cold start is just `fs.list_dir({})`.

Git-ness handles BOTH on-disk shapes: `.git` as a directory, and `.git`
as a FILE carrying a `gitdir:` pointer — what a linked worktree (and a
submodule) has. An `is_dir()`-only check badges every worktree non-git;
that is the bug PR #2839 hit in build.rs, and this workspace's own
checkouts are linked worktrees. Detection is two stats (plus one small
read for the rare `.git`-file) rather than a `git rev-parse` subprocess
per entry, since this runs across every row on an interactive picker's
hot path.

Errors are typed and distinguishable rather than stringly, reusing the
vision spec's existing §13.2 taxonomy instead of inventing fs-specific
codes: -32002 not_found, -32003 invalid_argument (path is a file),
-32001 permission_denied, -32603 internal. New RpcError::not_found and
::permission_denied constructors back the first two.

No path guard, deliberately — no denylist, sandbox root, permission
layer, or macOS TCC state machine. tcode is a local app whose daemon runs
as the user with the user's own entitlements, so a listing discloses
nothing `ls` would not; decisively, the same API already exposes
`task.run`, which executes arbitrary code as the user, so guarding browse
while that sits one method away is ceremony, not security. Recorded as a
module doc comment so a future reader does not "fix" it.

Verified end-to-end against a live `tcode serve --http`: a demo tree
renders 7a exactly (acme-api/marketing-site git, data-pipeline git via a
real linked worktree, scratch —), and a real macOS TCC refusal surfaces
as an ordinary typed -32001.

feat(trusty-code): projectless mode + unified project binding (UI Phase-1) (#2860)

"Project" was one concept split across two disagreeing API surfaces:
`task.run` took a REQUIRED `project: PathBuf` (`task/protocol.rs:48`), while
`session.create` took an untyped, free-form `project: Option<String>` label
(`session/protocol.rs:157`) that was never validated, never bound, and
disconnected from the path `task.run` demanded — a label that could not be
indexed and a path that could not be omitted, i.e. two halves of one missing
object.

Because the path was required, a projectless workstream was inexpressible: the
daemon could not even START without a project, so the shell's entry screen
(DOC-39 screen 7a, "Open a project" — a workstream that exists BEFORE a project
is chosen) was literally unimplementable. Every other Phase-1 surface renders
inside a shell whose entry state did not exist.

Both surfaces now converge on one typed `binding::ProjectBinding` with the
spec's three states: projectless (no index, no diff target, no palace),
directory (bound, non-git — INDEXES), and git_repo (bound, full affordances).

Binding is NOT gated on `.git`. The design proposal's own text ("binds the
moment work touches files in a git repo") is wrong and contradicts shipped
behaviour — it would exclude the non-git working dirs (#2728) and OS temp dirs
(#2747) we deliberately support. The git/non-git split decides only which git
affordances are offered, never whether the project binds or indexes. Git
detection is now a single implementation (`binding::is_git_worktree`) that
`run_task::diff` delegates to, so a `git_repo` binding can never disagree with
the diff strategy it selects.

The three things that assumed a project each get a defined behaviour, never a
panic: indexing is skipped when projectless; the project-scoped memory palace is
skipped (`memory_sink_for` takes `Option<&Path>`; the scratch root is
deliberately NOT substituted, which would mint an orphaned palace per run); and
the fs/bash tools are rooted at an ephemeral scratch dir, discarded at run end
and logged at warn to stderr so a projectless write is observable, not silent.
CLAUDE.md, catch-up, skills, and the settings.json mode tier already degraded to
"absent" and needed no projectless special-casing.

Scope: bind-later semantics are NOT implemented — the binding is established at
daemon startup and the bind hook is specified rather than built, since
bind-on-first-touch requires the fs tools to report upward into a workstream
object the spec explicitly defers out of Phase 1. Clone-from-URL is out of scope
per the spec (§6.3) and remains a follow-up.

BREAKING (Rust API + `session.create` semantics; `task.run`'s JSON-RPC params
are UNCHANGED — its `project` was a `register()` argument, never a request
field, so no JSON-RPC caller breaks). The next release must be 0.3.0, not a
patch bump. See CHANGELOG for the full surface and rationale.

Tests: a projectless task runs end-to-end without panicking (daemon spawned with
no --project, `$HOME` pointed at a user-level agents fixture, exercising the
~/.claude/agents fallback); a non-git dir binds as `directory` and is NOT
projectless; a git repo binds as `git_repo`; plus the index/palace/mode paths
that assume a project.

Refs #2855, spec DOC-39 §4.2/§5.5 (ACs 2.1–2.4, 16.1–16.3)

Addresses the two MEDIUMs from the #2846 PR review (#2849):

1. Reclaim-vs-search race (lanes.rs): bm25_search / grep_fallback_search
   called ensure_*_loaded() then acquired a SEPARATE read lock, so a
   memory-pressure reclaim firing under active load (unlike idle-evict,
   which only ever raced after 60s of quiet) could clear the structure
   in that window and silently return an empty lexical/grep lane. Both
   lanes now retry (bounded, REHYDRATE_RACE_RETRIES=3) when they observe
   empty + the evicted flag set under the same read guard, rehydrating
   in place instead of degrading recall. Deterministic regression tests
   reproduce the exact interleaving via lock contention (not statistical
   stress) and were verified to fail against the pre-fix code.

2. No hysteresis (tickers.rs): steady-state RSS at/above the high-water

   indefinitely. A new should_reclaim_now rising-edge gate, backed by
   SearchAppState::last_reclaim_rss_mb, only reclaims again once RSS has
   risen past where the last sweep left it; the baseline resets when RSS
   drops back under the mark so the next pressure episode always
   reclaims on its first crossing.

* fix(trusty-code): watch the reflog so a packed branch ref can't stale the embedded SHA

Addresses the MEDIUM from review on #2839.

Emitting any `rerun-if-changed` opts build.rs out of Cargo's default "re-run
when any package file changes" heuristic, so only declared paths are watched.
With the branch ref PACKED (`git gc --auto` / `git pack-refs`) there is no
loose ref file for `rerun_if_exists` to watch, and a later commit rewrites
neither HEAD's content nor any other watched path — so build.rs would not
re-run and the embedded SHA/date would go silently stale until a `cargo clean`.
A binary reporting a stale SHA is the exact failure #2823 exists to eliminate.

Also watch the append-only reflog (`logs/HEAD`), which is touched by
effectively every ref-changing operation whether or not the ref is packed.
That closes the gap without reverting to an unconditional always-re-run.

Verified in a throwaway repo — with the ref packed, a commit leaves HEAD's
content untouched (no rebuild) while the reflog changes (rebuild). Pinned by
`packed_branch_ref_leaves_only_the_reflog_witnessing_a_commit` so a future
"the reflog watch looks redundant" cleanup fails loudly.

Two things surfaced while testing:

- `git rev-parse --git-path` returns a CWD-relative path in a plain checkout
  but an absolute one in a linked worktree. `rerun_if_exists` now canonicalizes
  before emitting, so what Cargo resolves the directive against is unambiguous
  regardless of tree shape.
- Corrected the narrative in the CHANGELOG and build.rs docs: the original
  `.git/HEAD` directive never resolved in ANY tree, git or not. It was
  relative, and Cargo resolves relative directives against the PACKAGE root —
  `crates/trusty-code/.git/HEAD`, which is absent even in a normal checkout.
  So build.rs re-ran on every build always, not only in a non-git tree.
