fix(trusty-code): make deliverable completion robust to turn-budget variance (#2838)

On the bake-off L4 task, tcode's completion of the FULL required-artifact set
was nondeterministic across identical runs (same prompt, same model). The
transcripts localize the cause precisely:

  run-2: engineer used turns 9..=48 of the report transcript — exactly the
         40-turn InProcessRunnerConfig budget — and its FINAL turn opened
         "All 132 tests pass. Now let me create the README and ARCHITECTURE
         files:". ARCHITECTURE.md was never written.
  run-3: same task, engineer finished in 29 turns, all 5 deliverables shipped.

The provided suite passed 9/9 in both, so the code was never the problem. Both
runs authored ~130 tests of their own (~1000 LOC across 6 files) and both spent
~17-19 turns on one-file-per-turn `write_file` calls, using the `write_files`
batch tool exactly once. The inefficiency is the CONSTANT across runs; what
varied was the margin left when the engineer finally reached the docs it had
queued last. Ordering docs last is what makes them — and only them — the
deliverable exposed to turn-budget variance.

Fix is behavioural, in the BASE preamble (bumped 1.7.0 -> 1.8.0): enumerate the
required-artifact set as a checklist up front and track what remains; treat
task-named documentation as a deliverable rather than an epilogue; write
required documents at the point the design settles (code exists, project suite
passes) and ahead of any discretionary work; never begin discretionary work
while a required artifact is missing; scale self-authored tests to the stated
requirements; batch a multi-document tail through `write_files`; sweep the
checklist once more before finishing.

Deliberately NOT a turn-budget bump: run-2 spent MORE turns (49 report entries)
than both runs that completed (29, 39), so the budget was not the binding
constraint, and L5 would only outgrow a raised number.

Adds two preamble content assertions and refreshes the hash tripwire.

fix(trusty-search): bound graceful-stop flush so it can't hang until SIGKILL (#1746) (#2830)

* fix(trusty-search): bound graceful-stop flush so it can't hang until SIGKILL

The shutdown flush wrapped each index's snapshot in tokio::time::timeout, but
the flush performs blocking synchronous work — usearch's Index::save is a C++
FFI call that never yields. Once a poll enters that FFI the same task cannot be
re-polled, so the timeout's timer branch never fires and the deadline is
silently defeated. A single stalled ~500 MB HNSW save (or an index write-lock
held by an in-flight background reindex, #1717) wedged the sequential shutdown
loop until systemd's TimeoutStopSec (300s) fired a SIGKILL.

Run each index's flush on its own detached task and enforce the deadline on the
JoinHandle (an honest yield point) so a blocking/stalled flush can no longer
wedge the loop. Also hard-exit via std::process::exit(0) once run_daemon
returns, so a worker stuck in blocking FFI or a CUDA/embedder teardown deadlock
cannot block tokio's runtime teardown at exit; the stdio trusty-embedderd
sidecar exits on stdin EOF, so no child is orphaned.

No data-loss behaviour change — the #1711 empty-snapshot guard is untouched.

Closes #1746

fix(trusty-mpm): stop triggering media-library / app-data TCC prompts from managed children (#2820)

* fix(trusty-mpm): stop triggering media-library / app-data TCC prompts

Managed claude/agent children touch TCC-protected resources (Apple Music
media library `kTCCServiceMediaLibrary`, other apps' data
`kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAppData`) from within their normal worktree cwds.
tm forks the tmux server that parents every child WITHOUT disclaiming, so
macOS resolves the "responsible process" up the spawn chain to the signed
`trusty-mpm` binary — the consent dialog names trusty-mpm and, because each
transient child has no stable code identity, the decision is never cached →
a prompt storm.

tm's own filesystem traversal is already fenced off from those paths (#2760);
this is child-initiated access mis-attributed to the signed parent, and the
installed binary is correctly Developer-ID signed with a stable
identifier-anchored DR (so it is NOT signing drift).

Fix: add `core::spawn_disclaim::disclaimed_output`, which spawns via
`posix_spawnp` with the macOS `responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim` attribute
so each managed child (and the tmux server it forks) becomes its OWN responsible
process. The disclaim is service-agnostic — it re-attributes every child-initiated
prompt class at once. The private SPI is resolved via `dlsym` (absent → normal
spawn, zero regression); `TM_DISABLE_SPAWN_DISCLAIM=1` is an operational bypass.
Wired into the crate-wide tmux choke point (`core::tmux::run_tmux_with_bin`,
covering the server fork) and the direct daemon `claude --version` probe.

Known limitation: tmux shares one server; disclaim applies only when tm forks
it (not when `new-session -A` attaches to a pre-existing server).

* feat(trusty-code): reduce redundant full-suite test re-runs

The delegated engineer re-runs the full test suite 7-14x per bake-off L1
run as repeated "one final run to confirm" passes, even when no code has
changed since the last clean pass — inflating tcode's turn count far above
claude-code's on the same challenge.

Add the `redundant_run` module: the complement to the `verify_gate` (#2279).
Where that gate guarantees the suite runs at least once, this stops it running
more than needed. `is_redundant_test_rerun` is a pure predicate over a loop's
transcript — a proposed `bash` test invocation is redundant iff the most recent
prior test invocation already PASSED (exit 0) and nothing that could have
changed the tree (a write_file/write_files/edit, or any non-test bash command)
has run since. It reuses `verify_gate`'s is_test_command / bash_command_from_call
so the two gates can never drift.

`AgentLoop::dispatch_all` consults it (opt-in via
`with_redundant_run_suppression`, attached at the single delegated-engineer

* fix(trusty-code): enforce command identity in redundant-rerun gate

was a bare bool set by any is_test_command-matching bash call that exited 0,
and is_redundant_test_rerun returned it WITHOUT comparing to the pending call's
own command. Consequences: a narrow pass (`cargo test -p a`) wrongly suppressed

  true only when a baseline command exists and matches it, via `same_test_command`
  (exact equality after trimming outer whitespace only — documented as the sole
  normalization). Command-identity matching makes the `--no-run` concern moot: a
  compile-only run can only ever suppress a byte-identical compile-only run, never
  a real test run.

fix(trusty-code): bound PM re-delegation to prevent degenerate delegate loop (#2805)

A delegated engineer that completes via an explicit successful `finish_task`
(all tests passing) could still be mislabeled `partial`/exit-6: the PM would
fire one more gratuitous "re-verify" `delegate_to_agent` round, and when that
round ran the PM's loop out of turns/wall-clock time, `run_task` reported the
complete, correct, all-tests-green run as `partial` — corrupting run
status/telemetry.

Fix (both halves requested in the issue):

- (b) Do not re-delegate once the finish gate is satisfied. A run-scoped
  `EngineerCompletionSignal` latches when a delegation returns an
  `AgentOutput` with `finish_status == Completed` (threaded via a new
  `AgentOutput.finish_status`, set in `build_finish_output`). The PM's
  `DelegateToAgentTool` refuses any subsequent `delegate_to_agent` with a
  recoverable error nudging it to `finish_task`, so the engineer is never
  gratuitously re-invoked.

- Data integrity. `run_task::assemble_report` now checks the completion latch
  FIRST: a completed engineer maps to `Success` (non-empty diff) or
  `NoChanges` (empty diff), never `Partial`/`DeadlineExceeded`/`RunFailure`,
  regardless of how the PM's own loop later terminated.

The existing `MAX_REDELEGATIONS` cap (a) still bounds actual engineer retries.

Extracted `delegate.rs`'s inline tests to a sibling `delegate_tests.rs`
(test-classified) to stay under the 500-SLOC production cap, mirroring the
crate's `goals_tests.rs`/`trusty_search_tests.rs` convention.

fix(trusty-common): harden mid-task incremental index-file updates against transient send failures (#2796)

* fix(trusty-common): harden mid-task incremental index-file updates against transient send failures

The per-file `POST /indexes/{id}/index-file` call built a fresh
`reqwest::blocking::Client` for every file and swallowed any single
transport-level `send()` failure. Under sustained mid-task load (issue
#2785: an L4 tcode run saw 27 failures across 23 files) this dropped the
update outright, so files written during the task never became searchable.

Two fixes, both fail-open and non-blocking:
- Connection reuse: build ONE pooled client per write batch in
  `index_files_inner` and thread it through, so rapid successive writes
  ride keep-alive connections instead of paying a fresh TCP connect (and
  its transient-failure risk) per file.
- Retry-with-backoff: `post_index_file_with_retries` retries transport
  errors up to 3 attempts with bounded exponential backoff
  (`retry_backoff`: 50/150ms, capped 1s). HTTP non-2xx is NOT retried (a
  4xx/404 won't self-heal). Worst-case added stall ~200ms, on a detached
  thread.

Public signature of `index_files_best_effort` is unchanged; all call
sites in trusty-code are unaffected.

Tests: `post_index_file_retries_transient_send_failure` (loopback server
drops the first connection, answers 200 on the retry — asserts Indexed +
exactly 2 connections) and `retry_backoff_is_bounded_and_increasing`.

Closes #2785

* fix(trusty-mpm): reconcile zombie-Active sessions on in-place relaunch instead of 409 dead-end

* feat(trusty-mpm): auto-nudge idle-parked managed sessions

Follow-up to #2610/PR #2620, which shipped detection + a stderr warning
for idle-parking (a delegated agent ending its turn on a self-spawned
monitor/notification that can never re-wake it). This closes the loop:
the daemon now surfaces the park and, when opted in, auto-nudges the
parked managed session instead of relying on a human PM to resume it.

Detection heuristic (per issue comment 4984128989 + the #2620 design
notes): a `Stop`/`SubagentStop` hook whose payload carries the existing
`idle_parking` flag, correlated to an Active managed session that has NO
live tracked children (no Queued/Running delegation) — i.e. the stall is
real, not a legitimate mid-watch. Only then is a foreground-block
instruction injected into the parked pane.

Safety rails (conservative by construction):
- Opt-in: `[idle_nudge].enabled = false` by default (zero behavior change).
- Per-session cap (`max_nudges_per_session`, default 2) — never loops.
- Cooldown (`cooldown_secs`, default 300) between nudges to one session.
- "No live children" precondition guards a still-working session.
- Only nudges tmux-managed sessions that correlate to a Claude session id.
- Runs off the hook hot path via `tokio::spawn`; entirely best-effort.

Architecture:
- `core::idle_nudge` — pure `IdleNudgeConfig`, `NudgeLedger`, and the
  `decide_nudge` gate folding every rail into one testable decision.
- `daemon::idle_nudge` — effectful correlate→gate→inject→record, plus the
  `spawn_if_parked` trigger the `ingest_hook` handler calls in one line.
- `[idle_nudge]` config section embedded in `MpmConfig`.
- `DaemonState` owns the per-session nudge ledger.

The `api.rs` allowlist budget rises by exactly 1 SLOC for the single-line
hook dispatch; splitting that grandfathered monolith is a separate refactor.

project,local`, which never reads the managed `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json`
`mcpServers` map where `tm mcp add` writes. So native trusty MCP servers
registered via `tm mcp` were invisible to daemon-managed sessions, despite the
"available in all your projects" claim.

Add a new `session_launch::native_mcp` injector, called from `prepare_session`
alongside the memory/search injectors, that reads the managed registry via the
same `core::mcp_config` reader `tm mcp` uses, filters it to an explicit
native-only allowlist (slack-mcp, telegram-mcp, gworkspace-mcp, trusty-analyze),
and merges each matched server's public shape (command/args, never env)
idempotently into the workspace `.mcp.json`. trusty-memory/trusty-search are
excluded (dedicated pinning injectors own them); third-party/HTTP managed
servers (github, Duetto endpoints, …) are never injected.

Secret handling (code-critic BLOCK follow-up): `.mcp.json` is git-tracked in
every real project, so a native server's `env` block (e.g. SLACK_BOT_TOKEN,
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN) is never written there — a fleet agent's routine `git add
-A && commit && push` would otherwise leak it into remote history. Instead,
`split_public_and_secret_env` strips `env` from the `.mcp.json` entry
categorically (not by a key-name heuristic, to avoid false negatives) and
`route_native_mcp_secrets` delivers the real values via a workspace-root
`.env.local`, which the native binaries' own credential resolver
(`trusty_common::inference::credentials::resolve_key`, confirmed at
crates/trusty-channels/src/{slack,telegram}/api/client.rs) already reads via
its env -> .env.local -> secure-store precedence. Before writing any secret
content, `ensure_env_local_git_excluded` confirms `.env.local` is listed in the
workspace's real `git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude` file (mirroring the
proven pattern in `daemon::managed_routes::inproject::untracked_sync`); if that
can't be confirmed (not a git repo), secret delivery is skipped entirely rather
than risking an unexcluded file. A literal `git add -A` + `git diff --cached`
regression test proves `.env.local` can never be staged.

The injector runs before the trust pre-seed, so the injected `.mcp.json` names
flow into `enabledMcpjsonServers` and skip Claude's "new MCP servers found"
dialog. The managed config dir resolves from FrameworkPaths (home-relative, as
`tm mcp` does), keeping launch-prep hermetic under test isolation.

fix(trusty-mpm): reconcile zombie-active sessions on in-place relaunch (closes #2743) (#2744)

Bare `tm`, run inside a managed pane after its `claude` process exited but
before the daemon flipped the record to `stopped`, dead-ended: the in-place
relaunch asked the daemon to reactivate, got 409 Conflict, then fell back to a
`switch-client` reconnect to the session the operator was already inside — a
no-op that stranded them in a bare shell.

Root cause: the #2453 stale-`Active` reconcile on the reactivate route is
self-referential. It reconciles only when every pane of the record's tmux
session is an idle shell, but at reactivate time the requesting `tm` IS the
pane's foreground command, so the pane reads as "runtime still alive" and the
reconcile is refused with 409 — always, for this path.

Fix:
- `PaneInfo` gains a stable tmux `pane_id`; `list_managed_panes` captures it.
- The reactivate route accepts `?caller_pane_id=`; the reconcile neutralizes
  the caller's OWN pane (treats it as idle) before the liveness check. A pane
  cannot run `tm` in the foreground AND a live interactive `claude`, so this is
  sound. A genuinely live SIBLING window still blocks the reconcile (409),
  preserving the #2157 boundary — never kills a live session.
- `bin/tm` forwards its current pane_id on both in-place entry points.
- Self-reconnect no-op fix: when provably inside the record's own pane and the
  relaunch can't proceed, `tm` no longer does the misleading switch-client
  no-op; it reports honestly and prints a `claude --resume <id>` hint.
- Extract guided_inplace.rs's inline test module to a child tests.rs to stay
  under the 500-SLOC production cap.

fix(trusty-mpm): pm_guard recognizes git global flags and stops scanning quoted content (#2741)

The PM Bash guard denied an allowlisted `git commit` as a "shell edit"
because its deny-pattern scanners were quote-unaware: a `>` / `->` inside
a single-quoted `-m` message body tripped the file-write-redirection
heuristic (Bob's live repro), and a leading `-C <path>` global flag hid
the `commit` subcommand from the two-token matcher (which also under-denied
`git -C <path> apply`).

Root cause: `has_file_write_redirection`, `split_shell_segments`, and
`classify_command_substitutions` byte-scanned the raw command including
quoted argument content; git's own global flags were never skipped.

Fix (new `pm_guard_bash/shell_lex.rs`):
- `QuoteScan` builds a per-byte single/double-quote map; the segment
  splitter, redirection scan, and substitution scan skip quoted bytes when
  quotes are balanced, falling back to the proven quote-unaware scan when
  unbalanced (conservative direction).
- `git_subcommand` shlex-splits the segment and resolves the real git
  subcommand past global flags (`-C <path>`, `-c <kv>`, `--git-dir=…`, …),
  so `git -C <path> commit` is allowed and `git -C <path> apply` still denies.
- Compensating control in `sed_awk::awk_is_readonly`: since the outer
  scanners no longer see quoted `|`/`>`, awk now detects in-program
  co-process pipes (`print | "cmd"`) and output redirects (`print > "f"`)
  itself, preserving those true positives.

The mod.rs inline tests moved to a sibling `tests.rs` (test-file cap) to
keep the production file under the 500-SLOC cap; new regression tests cover
Bob's exact repro, the git-global-flag matrix, quoted-operator prose, and
the preserved deny/allow true-positive matrix.

Closes #2734

* fix(tga): dedupe external-source resolution on ticket key, not message

Code-critic HIGH finding on PR #2720: message-level dedupe does not
protect the resolver's per-TICKET cache. Two differently-worded commits
referencing the same ticket produce two distinct messages; both can race
the cache's non-atomic check-fetch-populate under concurrency and fire
duplicate fetches for the same hot ticket.

Adds ExternalSourceResolver::warm_cache (crates/trusty-git-analytics/src/
classify/sources/resolver/warm.rs), which extracts and dedupes ticket
keys/refs across the full batch of unique messages per source BEFORE any
fetch, then resolves each unique key with bounded concurrency. The
pipeline warms the cache before per-message resolve, so resolve becomes
cache-hit-only and race-free by construction.

(resolve_unique_bounds_concurrency) with a deterministic max-in-flight
gauge (AtomicUsize increment/decrement), removing the #2714-class flake
risk. Adds a wiremock regression test with distinct messages sharing one

* fix(trusty-mpm): harden agents against idle parking — never end a turn to wait (closes #2610)

Delegated merge/release/engineer agents kept ending their turn to "wait" on a
self-spawned background monitor/watcher that can never re-wake a stopped agent,
stranding the delegation chain until a human resumed them. The #2501 remediation
(BASE-AGENT Foreground Execution guidance) reduced but did not eliminate this;
2026-07-14 saw 6 fresh incidents even with explicit dispatch-prompt prohibitions.

Layered fix:

- BASE-AGENT.md: promote Foreground Execution into a hard, prominent
  "NEVER End Your Turn To Wait" rule — background monitors/watchers/pollers are
  FORBIDDEN as a wake mechanism; ending a turn with "waiting for/monitoring/
  standing by/will report when" language is a PROTOCOL VIOLATION. Adds the
  canonical CI-wait pattern (`gh pr checks <pr> --watch --fail-fast`, blocking
  foreground, re-issue on timeout) and the canonical long-command pattern.
- Persona reinforcement: full CI/long-wait sections in the two worst offenders
  (version-control, local-ops); a short pointer in BASE-ENGINEER (inherited by
  every engineer persona) for the quality-gate-run case.
- Mechanical back-stop: new pure, unit-tested `core::idle_parking` detector
  (parking-phrase scan + last-assistant-message extraction from a Claude Code
  JSONL transcript). Registers the `SubagentStop` hook and wires the Stop/
  SubagentStop handler to tail-read the transcript, detect a parking final
  message, emit a loud structured IDLE-PARKING WARNING to stderr, and enrich the
  daemon hook payload (`idle_parking`, `idle_parking_phrase`) so the dashboard/
  errors feed can surface it. Fully fail-open and time-bounded.

Follow-up (daemon-side dashboard surfacing + auto-nudge re-injection) is filed
separately; this PR ships detection + warning per the proportionate/testable bar.

* fix(trusty-mpm): stat-guard transcript reads against FIFO/non-regular-file hangs (PR #2620 review)

Code-critic MEDIUM finding on PR #2620: `read_transcript_tail`'s caller wraps
the read in `tokio::time::timeout`, but that only bounds the `.await` — the
underlying `open()` syscall still runs to completion on a spawn_blocking
worker thread. A `transcript_path` pointing at a FIFO with no writer would
block `open()` indefinitely and leak a stuck blocking-pool thread, even though
the timeout still lets the hook process exit. `stat()` never blocks on a FIFO,
so checking the file type first and refusing anything that is not a regular
file closes the leak before `open()` is ever reached.

- `read_transcript_tail`: stat-check via `tokio::fs::metadata` before opening;
  return `None` unless `file_type().is_file()`.
- New `rejects_fifo_without_blocking` integration test (`#[cfg(unix)]`,
  mkfifo via `Command`), bounded-poll assertion so a regression fails loudly
  instead of hanging the suite.
- LOW: documented the 256 KiB tail-window tradeoff (an oversized single final
  JSONL line is an advisory false negative by design) in
  `core::idle_parking::last_assistant_text_from_transcript`.

Makes `tctl install` + `tctl start` bring up the full daemon set on a fresh
machine without any undocumented manual `<binary> service install` step, and
fixes the hard-fail where two of five launchd members shipped no service code.

#2557 — trusty-review and trusty-console were marked `ManageStrategy::Launchd`
in `stable_set()` but shipped zero launchd/plist code, so `tctl start` (which
`launchctl bootstrap`s `com.trusty.trusty-{review,console}.plist`) hard-failed
against a plist nothing ever wrote. Both binaries DO expose a real long-lived
HTTP daemon (`serve`), so — per the issue's minimal-correct rule (add plist
support where a real daemon mode exists) — this adds a `service`
install/uninstall/status/logs subcommand to each, mirroring the established
trusty-search / trusty-analyze pattern and reusing the labels already reserved
in `plist_label.rs`. The console launchd-vs-process-managed question (umbrella
#2555) stays an owner decision: this makes the EXISTING `Launchd`
classification function, it does not decide it is the right lifecycle model.

`service_bootstrap` module wires each daemon member's own `<binary> service
install` into `install_all`'s post-install hooks (search/memory/analyze +
review/console), reusing the daemon's audited launchd logic rather than
duplicating plist XML. Fail-soft (log + continue), idempotent and
non-clobbering (an existing plist is left untouched — skip-with-message, so a
re-run neither overwrites an operator-customised plist nor needlessly restarts
a healthy daemon), and opt-outable via `--no-service` / TCTL_NO_SERVICE_BOOTSTRAP.

if present, else run `service install`" for tctl-managed members.

* fix(tooling): stop /* inside line-comment prose from swallowing SLOC counts

check_line_cap.sh's SLOC-counting awk scanner looked for the next `/*`
substring unconditionally, so a `/*` appearing inside `//`/`///`/`//!`
line-comment prose (e.g. a doc comment mentioning a path glob like
`/api/v1/sessions/*`) was mistaken for a block-comment opener. Once
tripped, every line after it was silently discarded as "still inside
an unterminated block comment" for the rest of the file — reproduced
locally: a 2244-raw-line file (api.rs) counted as ~24 SLOC pre-fix.

`/*`) occurs first at each position. A `//` that occurs before any
`/*` always wins and truncates the line immediately, so `/*` inside
comment prose is never reached. Real code-context block comments
(single- and multi-line) are still fully excluded as before.

The awk program is extracted to scripts/lib/sloc_awk.sh so both
check_line_cap.sh and the new self-test share one implementation.
scripts/check_line_cap_selftest.sh exercises it against fixtures in
scripts/test-data/ (normal file, /* in doc-comment prose, real block
comments, trailing // after code).

were silently undercounted by the old scanner and are genuinely over

fix(trusty-mpm): guided-default no longer inherits an ancestor repo's project when cwd is untracked (#2535)

Bare `tm` (guided default) run from a directory that physically sits inside
another repository's working-tree span but is NOT part of that repo's tracked
tree silently resolved to the ancestor repo's project and offered its sessions.
Root cause: `find_git_root()` walks up to any ancestor `.git`, and
`derive_project()` / `fallback_protected()` then trusted that root's `origin`
remote unconditionally — never verifying `cwd` actually belongs to the repo's
tracked tree. On case-insensitive APFS an untracked notes folder `~/Duetto/cto`
case-folds onto the enclosing repo's tracked `CTO/` dir, so it has no `.git` of
its own and wrongly resolved to the ancestor repo.

Fix: when the discovered git root is a strict ancestor of `cwd`, verify
`cwd`'s relpath is part of the repo's tracked tree
(`git ls-tree -d --name-only HEAD -- <relpath>`) before trusting the ancestor's
identity. On a miss, `cwd` is treated as not inside any usable git project and
routed to the existing clean non-git fallback (live checkout untouched) with a
message explaining the situation — never the managed-clone redirect or the
ancestor-session picker. `git_root == cwd` behavior is unchanged.

The tracked-tree membership decision is factored into the pure, unit-testable
`ls_tree_reports_tracked_dir` helper; `classify_cwd_project` returns a three-way
`Usable` / `UntrackedInsideAncestor` / `NotGit` classification consumed by both
resolution paths.

Closes #2534

fix(trusty-mpm): TUI activity pane — explicit unavailable state instead of perpetual loading (#2513)

A PERSISTENT per-session /activity fetch failure while the daemon is
otherwise healthy (404 from an older daemon lacking the endpoint, a GC'd
session, a malformed body) previously left state.activity as None forever,
indistinguishable from "not fetched yet" — the Activity pane rendered
"loading live activity…" indefinitely.

Adds a consecutive-failure counter (ActivityFailureStreak, threshold 3)
tracked independently of ActivityInfo so it survives even when no fetch has
ever succeeded. Failures are classified via classify_activity_error: a
transport-class failure (connection refused/timeout — the whole daemon
looks down or is restarting) never advances the streak and keeps the
existing stale-keep behavior; a non-transport failure (HTTP status error or
an undecodable body — this session's endpoint is itself broken) does. Once
the streak crosses the threshold, the pane renders "activity unavailable
for this session" instead of "loading…". The streak resets to a fresh
count whenever a different session id is recorded (an implicit
session-switch reset) or a fetch succeeds.

The pure classification + state-transition logic (apply_activity_outcome)
is unit tested with typed inputs, no live daemon. Split poll/mod.rs's test

  whenever a trusty-mpm launchd unit is registered, mirroring

* fix(trusty-mpm): close PATCH /api/v1/projects/{name} TOCTOU race + reject blank tags

Adversarial review of #2481 found a HIGH (merge-blocking) and a MEDIUM.

HIGH — lost-update race: patch_project_registry_route called
registry.get(&name) then registry.register(project.clone()) as two SEPARATE
lock acquisitions, with nothing held across read->mutate->persist. Two
concurrent PATCHes to the same project could silently drop one caller's
update, since each builds its full replacement record from its own stale
snapshot. This is the exact bug class #2395 already fixed for
DeliverableManager::update_deliverable_with. Fix: add
ProjectRegistry::update_with(name, f: FnOnce(Project) -> Project), holding
ONE write-lock guard across the whole fetch->mutate->persist sequence;
route the PATCH handler through it. Added a negative reproduction test
(get_then_register_pattern_reproduces_lost_update_pre_fix, using the raw
two-lock primitives with a Notify-forced interleave to prove the pre-fix
hazard deterministically) and a positive regression test
(update_with_serializes_concurrent_field_edits, proving two concurrent
PATCHes to different fields both land).

MEDIUM — blank tags accepted: tags_add entries were pushed as-is with no
trim/blank rejection, unlike repo_url/default_branch. Since this endpoint
is the server-side validation surface #2120's CLI/TUI depend on, a blank
tag would persist silently with 200. Fix: trim every tags_add/tags_remove
entry and reject (400) the whole request if any entry is blank/
whitespace-only after trimming. Added patch_rejects_blank_tags_add,
patch_rejects_blank_tags_remove, and patch_trims_tags_add_whitespace.

(2869 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored — ONNX-gated), clippy --workspace
--all-targets -D warnings, fmt --check, check_line_cap.sh.

feat(trusty-search): add follow_links symlink policy to indexer (#2355)

Adds an opt-in `follow_links` control to the reindex walker so operators
can create indexes that do NOT dereference symlinks. Roots that contain
symlinks escaping the tree (a self-referential link, links into unrelated
repos — e.g. the cto-resources self-symlink) previously had every escape
link indexed because the walker hardcoded `follow_links(true)`, bloating
and corrupting the index.

Design / default semantics:
- WalkOptions.follow_links (Default false); walker uses
  `.follow_links(opts.follow_links)` instead of hardcoded true.
- New indexes created via create_index / POST /indexes default to
  follow_links = FALSE (safe do-not-follow).
- Pre-existing persisted indexes deserialize a missing field as TRUE
  (serde default), so their behaviour is unchanged on upgrade — those
  indexes were built while symlinks were followed unconditionally.
- IndexHandle.follow_links threaded through the reindex orchestrator into
  WalkOptions; preserved across handle rebuild (PATCH config), restore,
  relocate, and root_path override.
- Optional `follow_links` boolean on the MCP create_index tool + HTTP
  CreateIndexRequest; create handler resolves `unwrap_or(false)`.
- Persisted to indexes.toml with skip_serializing_if so only the
  new-index opt-out (false) is written.

Tests: walker directional tests (follows-when-enabled /
does-not-follow-by-default) and a persistence back-compat round-trip
(missing field -> true; explicit false survives save/load).

The file-based SmContextEngine is opened fresh per turn and persists by atomic
whole-file replace with NO merge, so two concurrent chat turns for the SAME
conv_id each load the state, append their round, and save — the second save
silently clobbers the first, losing a round whose reply was already returned to
the caller. Now reachable via the async coordinator/chat endpoint.

(open -> record -> save) in both `chat` and `chat_with_actions`, mirroring the
per-palace write_mutex precedent in memory_core. Turns for different conv_ids
never block; the lock registry is bounded via Weak handles + opportunistic prune.

different-conv_ids non-serialization guard.

for sm.goals.*, sm.delegate, and sm.context.get on the default build.

the default build, durable palace-backed storage under sm-memory — mirroring the
recall no-op cfg pattern. Only a degraded provider (not the missing feature) makes

fix: route install-trusty-search-signed.sh log helpers to stderr (#2351)

Root cause: the info() and section() log helpers in
scripts/install-trusty-search-signed.sh wrote to stdout instead of
stderr. detect_identity() calls info() for status messages while also
using `echo "$identity"` to return its result, and callers capture that
result via command substitution (`identity="$(detect_identity)"`). Because
info()'s log lines landed on the same stdout stream as the echoed
identity, the captured value was corrupted with log text, which was then
passed to `codesign --sign <identity>` — causing "no identity found"
even though a valid Developer ID Application certificate was present.
This left the cargo-installed binaries unsigned, silently reintroducing
the FDA-loss-on-reinstall problem (#873) the script exists to prevent.

Fix:
- Route info() and section() to stderr (warn() and error() already were).
- Audited every function in the script invoked via command substitution
  ($(...)) — detect_identity() and detect_repo_root() — to confirm only
  the intended return value reaches stdout now that all log helpers are
  stderr-only.
- Added an explicit post-sign verification step in sign_binary(): after
  each `codesign --sign`, immediately run `codesign --verify --deep
  --strict` on that binary and exit non-zero with a clear stderr message
  if it fails, so a corrupted or invalid signature can never pass
  silently before signing the next binary.
- Checked sibling scripts under scripts/ for the same copy-pasted
  info()/warn()/error() helper pattern; no other script shares it.

Reproduced live during the 2026-07-10 signed install; workaround at the
time was manually running the intended codesign invocation for both
binaries.

* fix(trusty-mpm): dedup stale duplicate session records per project in reconcile_on_boot (closes #2306)

A project could accrue two conflicting non-Decommissioned records — one
canonical (resolved workspace_path) and one adopted record permanently
stuck at cwd/workspace_path=/unknown (adopted before #2163's get_pane_cwd
resolution). reconcile_on_boot only resolved /unknown when a live pane was
found and never revisited a Stopped /unknown record, and nothing collapsed
multiple records per project — so tm kept re-attaching to the stale one.

Add a dedup pass (new session_manager/dedup.rs) invoked by reconcile_on_boot
after the main reconcile persists states and the store guard is dropped. It
groups non-Decommissioned records by source_id (fallback: workspace_path),
and for a fully-quiesced group (no live tmux among any member) keeps the best
survivor (resolved workspace_path over /unknown; tie-break most-recent
last_activity_at then created_at) and decommissions the rest via the existing
safe path (/unknown losers are workspace_owned=false → no disk removal). A
group with ANY live tmux member is left untouched. Planned losers are also
pruned from the pending auto-resume set.

The core decision is a pure function (plan_dedup) unit-tested without real
tmux (the #1790 guard); two reconcile_on_boot integration tests cover the
end-to-end collapse and the live-group skip.

* fix(trusty-mpm): narrow dedup loser eligibility to unresolved-or-dead records only (closes #2306)

Review (BLOCK) found a data-loss flaw in the first pass: source_id is
derived per-REPOSITORY (derive_source_id_for_record, adopt.rs), so ALL
worktree sessions of one repo share a dedup group — a "keep only the
newest" policy would collapse legitimate concurrent sessions. Worse: an
in-project worktree record is workspace_owned=false BY DESIGN, yet
decommission_with_root still runs `git worktree remove --force` (+ branch
delete) for such a path via is_session_worktree — so the naive policy
would destroy real, possibly-uncommitted work on a daemon restart with 2+
stopped worktree sessions of one repo.

Redesign the loser-eligibility rule instead of the grouping key (the
grouping-by-source_id/workspace_path stays as-is; the safety boundary
moves to selection time):

  - A record is loser-eligible ONLY when it is unresolved-or-dead:
    workspace_path is None, the literal "/unknown" sentinel, or a resolved
    path that no longer exists on disk (is_resolved_existing == false).
  - A record with a resolved, still-existing workspace_path is NEVER a
    loser, regardless of group size or recency — this is the fix: two (or
    more) concurrent worktree sessions of one repo now survive untouched.
  - Within a quiesced group, if ANY member is resolved-existing, every
    unresolved/dead member is superseded and decommissioned; the
    resolved-existing members themselves are left alone even if there are
    several. If NONE are resolved-existing (/unknown-only or all-dead),
    the most-recently-active/created member survives (nothing on disk to
    lose in that case).
  - Belt-and-suspenders: immediately before decommissioning a loser, the
    SAME is_resolved_existing predicate is rerun against a fresh fetch;
    a loser whose path has reappeared since planning is skipped with a
    warn!, guarding a TOCTOU race between the plan snapshot and the
    decommission call. The full plan is logged at info level before acting.
  - No feature flag was added: the narrowed rule makes losers unresolved
    or dead-path BY CONSTRUCTION, so nothing selected for decommission has
    anything left to lose on disk — the destructive scenario the review
    flagged is eliminated at the eligibility-rule level, not gated behind
    a flag.
  - Live-group guard (any live tmux member exempts the whole group) is
    unchanged — verified correct in review.

three-way test into plan_dedup_two_resolved_existing_paths_untouched (two

fix(trusty-search): dedup warm-boot entries sharing one redb corpus path (closes #2305) (#2335)

Two colocated registry entries that share a root_path resolve to the same
<root>/.trusty-search/index.redb. redb is a single-open database, so the
sequential warm-boot restore opens the file for the first entry and holds the
corpus Arc for the daemon's lifetime; every later entry sharing that file fails
its open with DatabaseAlreadyOpen (the 50ms open_corpus_with_retry can never
clear an in-process holder), and the failure recurs on every restart — the
#1870 root cause.

Fix: collapse entries resolving to one on-disk redb corpus down to a single
handle before any open is attempted. dedup_entries_by_corpus_path keys colocated
entries by their canonical root (equivalent to the redb path, no create_dir_all
side effect), keeps the most-recently-active entry per file, and drops the rest
with a warn. Non-colocated corpora are id-keyed and never collide, so only
colocated duplicates are affected. Wired into restore_indexes before the
eager/cold split so a dropped duplicate is never parked in the cold store to
re-trigger the double-open on first query.

Tests: dedup unit tests (collapse same-root, keep distinct roots, keep
non-colocated, keep most-recent) plus an open-path regression proving a
concurrently-held second open of the shared redb fails (DatabaseAlreadyOpen) and
that dedup collapses the pair to one, and a distinct-roots test proving
independent corpora still open with zero DatabaseAlreadyOpen.

fix(trusty-mpm): strip leading -- separator from tm mcp args at write and read (closes #2326) (#2329)

`tm mcp add <name> <cmd> -- <args...>` mirrors `claude mcp add`, where `--`
merely stops flag parsing. But clap's `trailing_var_arg` keeps that `--` in the
captured tail once the command positional is consumed, so it was persisted as
the FIRST stored arg (`["--", "-y", "@scope/pkg"]`). Spawned verbatim that
breaks every npx/uv-style stdio server (npm ETARGET `undefined@-y`; uv
"unexpected argument 'run' ... remove the '--'"), and the args are wrong at
rest so real Claude Code sessions consuming the config break too.

- write: `tm mcp add` drops a single leading `--` before persisting;
- read: the `mcp_test` spawn path and `tm mcp list/get` display strip a legacy
  stored leading `--`, so already-broken registries work without manual repair.
Only the leading token is stripped, once — a legitimate deeper `--` is preserved.

* fix(trusty-search): close TOCTOU in embedder in-flight guard (closes #2315)

Review caught a critical kill-mid-request race in the previous commit:
embed_via incremented in_flight AFTER releasing the state lock, so a
watchdog tick could observe in_flight==0 under its own state lock while
a request had already cloned a client_slot and was about to use it.

Fix: construct the InFlightGuard (the increment) inside the SAME
self.state critical section that idle_watchdog re-checks in_flight
under. This serializes the two sides on one mutex -- whichever
acquires it first is fully observed by the other before either
proceeds. If the watchdog wins and clears state to None, a subsequent
embed_via call observes None under the lock and respawns rather than
reusing a stale client_slot (the pre-existing guard.is_none() check
already does this correctly).

Also: replaced the AcqRel-ordering doc comment on InFlightGuard --
the safety guarantee comes from lock serialization, not atomic
ordering -- and added embed_via_defers_watchdog_eviction_while_request_in_flight,
a real-path test that drives the race through embed_via itself with an
op that blocks on a Notify past the idle deadline (the existing
hand-seeded in_flight=1 test would pass even with the old buggy
ordering, since it never exercises the lock-acquisition sequence).

fix(trusty-code): re-anchor task only once per compaction event, not every turn (closes #2302) (#2303)

Transcript::to_messages() re-appended the original seeded task message
on EVERY call once compaction had fired once, instead of only on the
turn compaction actually fired on. The engineer model read this as
"start over from scratch" repeatedly, producing 121-turn thrash cycles.

Replace the one-way `compaction_triggered: bool` flag with
`last_compaction_len: Option<usize>`, recording the entry count at the
moment maybe_compact last fired. to_messages() now replays the last
user message only when the current entry count still equals that
recorded length — true on the compaction turn itself (maybe_compact
and to_messages run back-to-back before new entries are appended), and
false on every later turn until compaction fires again.

task text appears exactly once (its seeded position) after further
turns without a new compaction event.

* fix(trusty-mpm): harden redact_oauth_token against embedded single-quote (#2256)

Re-review caught a real edge case in the #2246 token-redaction fix: the
quoted-value branch treated the FIRST `'` after the opener as the closer,
but shell_single_quote escapes an embedded literal `'` in a token as the
POSIX close-escape-reopen sequence `'\''`. A token containing an apostrophe
therefore leaked its tail in cleartext:

'\'' run as one escaped-quote unit to skip over, so only a bare `'` (not
followed by \'') is treated as the true closer. redact_oauth_token now
collapses the entire escaped value — including any embedded quotes — to a
single '<redacted>' marker.

find_quoted_value_end_skips_escaped_embedded_quote, and
redact_oauth_token_masks_value_with_embedded_single_quote (the exact

* fix(trusty-code): Bedrock backstop enforces ToolUse/ToolResult pairing (#2278)

build_converse_messages now runs enforce_tool_pairing over the fully
role-merged Converse message list before returning: orphan ToolResult
blocks (no earlier matching ToolUse) are dropped, and any ToolUse left
unanswered in its answering window gets a synthesized placeholder
ToolResult (status Error) so Bedrock's Converse API never sees an
unpaired tool block. This is the general last-resort guarantee that the
wire request is always valid, independent of whatever produced the
input history (compaction, re-delegation retries, or anything else).

message (e.g. a compaction-summary placeholder) was diverted to the

in-progress same-role batch first — silently merging content from
before and after the system entry into one message. Flush first.

* fix(trusty-code): turn-group-atomic compaction cutoff (#2278)

Transcript::maybe_compact used a raw entry-COUNT cutoff with no
tool-call awareness, so it could land between an assistant entry
carrying tool_calls and one of its answering tool-role entries,
folding the assistant into the compacted summary while the answer
survived verbatim — an orphaned tool result with no tool use.

maybe_compact now treats an assistant entry with tool_calls plus the
maximal contiguous run of answering tool entries as one atomic turn
group (naturally covering multi-tool-call turns). turn_group_start/
turn_group_end detect when the naive cutoff falls inside a group and
pull the whole group forward into the kept zone, making
keep_last_messages a soft floor rather than ever splitting a group.
Existing invariants (system/user and pinned skill-output entries never
compact; turn-boundary-only) are unchanged and their tests still pass.

Provider-agnostic; pairs with the Bedrock-specific enforce_tool_pairing
backstop landed in the previous commit.

fix(install.sh): handle GitHub API 403/rate-limit in release resolution, honor GITHUB_TOKEN (#2285) (#2288)

resolve_version() piped `curl | grep | grep | head | sed` directly into a
command substitution. POSIX sh has no pipefail, so the pipeline's exit
status was the LAST command's (sed, which succeeds on empty input) — a
curl failure such as an HTTP 403 from unauthenticated rate-limiting (60
req/hr, easily exhausted behind a shared IP/NAT/CI runner) was silently
swallowed, and the script reported the misleading "no
trusty-installer-v* release found" instead of the true cause.

trusty-installer-v0.4.0 is in fact published and the unauthenticated API
call succeeds under normal conditions (verified via `gh release list` and
a direct curl), confirming this is a rate-limit/script-bug issue, not a
missing release.

Fetch the releases body to a temp file and inspect curl's own HTTP status
via `-w '%{http_code}'` instead of relying on pipeline exit status. Retry
transient 403/429/5xx a few times with backoff, and send an
`Authorization: Bearer` header when GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN is set
(raises the limit to 5000/hr) — entirely optional, the tokenless path is
unchanged.

Closes #2285

fix(trusty-search): return doc hits for Unknown-intent queries instead of empty (Closes #2203) (#2287)

Short (1-3 word) natural-language queries classify as `Unknown` intent
(`multi_noun_re` requires >= 4 tokens to reach `Conceptual`). `SearchQuery::mode`
defaults to `SearchMode::Code`, and `CodeIndexer::search`'s intent-aware
Code->All upgrade only covered `Conceptual`/`Definition`, so `Unknown` stayed
`Code`. `apply_archive_downrank` then did a hard `retain` dropping every
non-code file when mode was `Code`, deleting BM25's correct `.md`/`.txt` hits
post-hoc and silently returning empty/irrelevant results for exactly the
queries the semantic/NL search tool exists to serve.

Two changes, both requested by the diagnosis:

1. `core/indexer/search/mod.rs` (~150-154): add `Unknown` to the intent set
   that upgrades `Code` -> `All`, alongside `Conceptual`/`Definition`. This is
   the primary fix - it lets Unknown NL queries surface doc hits.

2. `core/indexer/search/mod.rs` `apply_archive_downrank` (~283-300): as
   defense-in-depth, `Unknown` intent no longer hard-drops non-code files even
   if `mode` somehow still resolves to `Code` (e.g. a future caller path that
   bypasses the upgrade above). Instead of the hard file-type `retain`, it
   applies the existing (previously unused) `docs_penalty::doc_score_penalty`
   multiplicative down-rank to non-code chunks - a soft demotion rather than a
   deletion. Chose the existing multiplicative penalty (not a new additive
   one) because the infrastructure already existed and unused
   (`_docs_mult` was discarded), it's simplest, and it keeps prose/config
   visible-but-lower-ranked rather than invisible. Every other intent (Usage,
   BugDebt, and Conceptual/Definition that already upgrade away from Code)
   keeps the existing hard filter, so no regression for real code-shaped
   queries.

Regression tests added in a new `tests_unknown_intent.rs` (kept separate from
`tests.rs`, which is already near its frozen 1500-SLOC test-cap budget):
- `test_unknown_intent_downranks_docs_instead_of_dropping_them`: builds an
  in-memory corpus with a matching `.md` doc plus `.rs` files, runs a 2-word
  query verified to classify as `Unknown`, with `mode` left at its default
  (`Code`) to mirror a real caller. Asserts non-empty results containing the
  `.md` hit. Verified this test fails against the pre-fix code (temporarily
  reverted just `search/mod.rs`) and passes after restoring the fix - see
  verification output below.
- `test_bugdebt_intent_still_hard_filters_code_mode`: companion no-regression
  test confirming a `BugDebt`-intent query still hard-filters to source-only
  in `Code` mode.

Also updated `test_mode_filter_code_returns_only_source` in `tests.rs`: its
query previously relied on classifying as `Unknown` to exercise the
(pre-fix) hard Code-only filter; since `Unknown` is now upgraded/downranked
per this fix, the query was changed to `where is alpha_qwerty` (`Usage`
intent, not in the upgrade set) so it continues to validate the genuine
hard-filter contract for non-Unknown intents.

fix(trusty-memory): idle-to-disk palace eviction + unpin dream scheduler + configurable max-open (#2276)

Stops the dream scheduler pinning every palace's Arc<PalaceHandle> for life
(which defeated the LRU), adds idle-TTL eviction that drops drawers/HNSW/KG
for palaces idle past TRUSTY_MEMORY_IDLE_EVICT_SECS and lazily rehydrates from
the durable redb store, and wires TRUSTY_MEMORY_MAX_OPEN_PALACES. Cuts idle RSS.

Design note: eviction drops the whole Arc<PalaceHandle> at the registry level
(cold = "absent from registry") rather than nulling individual handle fields.
This reclaims the same RAM, reuses the already-tested open/reopen path for
rehydration, and is safer under redb's exclusive flock: an evict_idle guard
(strong_count == 1) plus per-palace open serialisation guarantees only one
store instance per palace ever exists, so a concurrent reopen never
double-opens the files. The field-nulling approach was infeasible anyway —
handle.kg/drawers/vector_store/closets are read directly by 40+ call sites
including introspection paths (health, TUI, console_metrics) that must not
rehydrate a cold palace on access.

* feat(trusty-code): Bedrock cachePoint prompt-caching + tool_calls-aware compaction

Two highest-leverage cost fixes from the Bedrock bake-off teardown, landed
together because they compound:

1. (#2260) Bedrock's Converse path never emitted prompt-cache breakpoints,
   re-billing the full tools+system prefix as fresh input every turn: L1
   bake-off measured tcode at 452,901 fresh input tokens / $1.67 vs
   claude-code $0.72 / opencode $0.75 (near-zero fresh input, reading
   847K-1.11M from cache). `BedrockProvider::supports_prompt_caching` now
   returns `true`; the Converse transport (new `llm::bedrock::cache` module)
   translates the SAME `agent_loop::build_request` cache markers OpenRouter's
   `anthropic/*` passthrough already sets into Bedrock-native `cachePoint`
   content blocks (`SystemContentBlock::CachePoint` / `Tool::CachePoint`),
   placed after the system prompt and after the tool schemas — mirroring
   where the OpenRouter path places its two breakpoints. Guarded by a
   1024-estimated-token minimum-cacheable-prefix floor (the Claude
   Sonnet/Opus floor) so a too-small prefix never wastes one of Bedrock's
   4-per-request checkpoint slots.

2. (#2261) The compaction estimator summed only `ChatMessage.content`,
   ignoring `tool_calls[].function.arguments` — where write_file/edit
   argument bodies (the actual file contents) live. A tool-call-only
   assistant turn has `content: None` entirely, so a real segment measured
   at 23,541 tokens never crossed the default 6,000-token threshold and
   never compacted. `estimate_total_tokens` now sums tool-call argument JSON
   alongside content, using the same chars/4 heuristic.

Closes #2260
Closes #2261

See also #2242, #2212 (the OpenRouter cache_control pattern this mirrors).

  non-system messages with an ephemeral cache_control breakpoint each turn,

  wired into build_request right after the existing system marker.

  ContentBlock::CachePoint immediately after a marked message's own content
  blocks, landing inside the correct (possibly same-role-merged) Message.

2 history breakpoints (Bedrock's per-request maximum).

fix(trusty-code): cap engineer re-delegation and stop mislabeling partial work as run_failure (#2267)

Completes the #2233 partial fix for the orchestration regression in #2265:
a recurring retryable Bedrock transport error (AgentLoopError::Llm) aborted
the delegated engineer sub-loop mid-session, and with no cap on total
re-delegations, the PM's own 8-turn budget (unchanged since #2233 raised the
engineer's max_turns to 40) became the only ceiling — blowing session turn
counts from ~40 to ~111 and reporting an opaque run_failure even when a
working solution already sat on disk.

Four fixes, all required:

1. Re-delegation cap (run_task/redelegation.rs): RedelegatingRunner wraps the
   engineer AgentRunner and internally retries a failed attempt (reuse-hint
   augmented) up to MAX_REDELEGATIONS=3 total attempts, entirely inside one
   delegate_to_agent tool dispatch. A shared RedelegationCapSignal lets
   run_task::assemble_report recognise a cap-triggered terminal state.

2. tools/delegate.rs: redelegation_hint() now returns Some(..) for
   AgentLoopError::Llm too (previously only TurnCapExceeded/Timeout/
   Cancelled), since it is the dominant bake-off failure mode and #2233's
   reuse-hint never fired for it.

3. Turn-budget asymmetry: chose the "decouple" design — every re-delegation
   retry happens inside RedelegatingRunner, never consuming the PM's own
   AgentLoopConfig::max_turns (left at its default of 8), rather than raising
   that budget.

4. run_task::assemble_report gates on TurnCapExceeded/cap-reached PLUS a
   non-empty diff to emit the new ExitCode::Partial (exit 6, status
   "partial") instead of RunFailure, purely on "was a deliverable produced"
   — genuine no-output failures still map to RunFailure unchanged.

Fix #5 (in-loop retry-with-backoff for AgentLoopError::Llm before aborting to
re-delegation) is deferred — see the TODO(#2265 follow-up) left in
agent_loop/mod.rs at the chat() call site.

fix(trusty-embedderd): bound ONNX model-init so a provider hang fails loud (#2218)

The published binary's FastEmbedder::new() model-load call had no timeout.
On Amazon Linux 2023 / glibc 2.34 hosts, the ORT CPU(no-arena) execution-
provider init deadlocks in futex_wait_queue indefinitely (0% CPU, no error,
no further log output past "registering CPU(no-arena) execution provider"),
leaving the daemon hung for hours with no HTTP/stdio/UDS listener ever bound
and search silently degraded to lexical-only.

run_with_args now races the model load against a bounded timeout
(readiness::run_bounded, default 180s via TRUSTY_EMBEDDER_INIT_TIMEOUT_SECS,
matching the existing memory_core convention). On expiry the process exits
nonzero with an actionable stderr message naming issue #1633 and the two
remediations: raise the timeout if the host is just slow, or reinstall with
--features embedder-load-dynamic + ORT_DYLIB_PATH on AL2023/older-glibc
hosts. Because every transport listener is only bound after model load
succeeds, the daemon already could not report false-positive readiness
during init — this closes the gap where a hang was unbounded and silent.

Suspected toolchain root cause (full writeup + recommended release-workflow
follow-up in the PR description): the crates.io default feature set
(embedder-bundled-ort) links a statically-bundled ONNX Runtime assuming
glibc >= 2.38; AL2023 ships glibc 2.34. cargo install always builds with
default features regardless of host glibc, so AL2023 users who cargo
install never get the load-dynamic variant the GitHub Releases build
matrix already produces for exactly this case. That distribution-channel
gap is an infra decision, deferred to the PM/user — not fixed here.

* fix: coordinate cold_park_index with the loading gate to prevent orphaning a racing cold-load

QA deterministically reproduced an orphan race: get_or_load_index registers
the freshly-loaded handle into the hot registry before it clears the id from
ColdIndexStore (mark_loaded runs after restore_fn resolves). If
cold_park_index landed in that gap, it would re-insert a cold entry and
detach the just-loaded handle, then the racing loader's mark_loaded would
delete the entry cold_park_index just added -- leaving the index in neither
store and turning the successful load into a spurious NotFound.

Fix: cold_park_index now bails out (returns false, touches nothing) whenever
the id is still a member of ColdIndexStore at call time -- that membership is
the exact tell for "a cold-load has this id claimed and hasn't settled it
yet" (a purely resident, settled id is never in cold_store.entries). Parking
is an optimization; skipping one id for one sweep tick is always safe.

Adds a deterministic (synchronization-based, not timing-based) regression
test that injects the racing park call inside get_or_load_index's restore_fn
closure, reproducing the exact interleaving on every run.

fix(trusty-search): prevent reindex from hijacking to a non-persisted root and pruning the corpus (#2183)

The #402/#1073 "colocated root moved" heuristic in the reindex runner
trusted an in-memory IndexHandle.root_path candidate purely because the
candidate directory *had* colocated `.trusty-search/` storage — not
because it was actually this index's registered root. `POST
/indexes/:id/reindex` accepts a caller-supplied `root_path` override
(issue #63) that is swapped into the in-memory registry entry but is
never written to `indexes.toml`, so the in-memory root can silently
diverge from the durably persisted source of truth.

In the live incident, `reindex -i cto` ran while an unrelated
trusty-tools git worktree session was active. The CLI's bare `reindex`
command always derives its `root_path` override from the CWD-detected
project (crates/trusty-search/src/commands/reindex.rs), regardless of
which index was targeted by `-i`. The heuristic accepted the worktree
as cto's "moved" root (it also has colocated storage — this workspace
self-indexes), walked it, and the post-loop prune pass then deleted
every one of the real corpus's 369,568 chunks that weren't seen in that
2,506-file walk. indexes.toml's root_path was correct throughout; only
the in-memory handle drifted.

Fix: before trusting any detected root move enough to walk or prune the
corpus against it, cross-check the candidate against the durably
persisted indexes.toml entry for that index
(validate::root_move_is_trusted). A move is trusted only when there is
no persisted entry to check (fresh/test index) or the candidate matches

feat(trusty-search): re-view idle promoted HNSW stores back to mmap (#2174)

The #709 mmap-view optimization opens warm-booted HNSW snapshots via
Index::view (low RSS), but any write promotes the index to a full
heap copy via ensure_mutable()/promote_view_to_mutable() and there was
no path back. Live measurement on a 77-index daemon found mmap-resident
was only ~80 KB total, i.e. nearly every index had been promoted at
least once and stayed heap-resident forever afterward — the largest
reclaimable chunk of a ~13 GB footprint.

Adds UsearchStore::try_demote_to_view(), the counterpart to
promote_view_to_mutable(): re-opens the same Index handle via
Index::view when the store is currently mutable, idle, and clean (no
unpersisted writes). A new `dirty` flag is the correctness gate — set
by every graph-mutating path (upsert/remove/upsert_batch) while still
holding the HNSW write lock, cleared by save() once the snapshot is
flushed. Demotion re-checks is_view/dirty under the same write lock
used by search/ensure_mutable/save, so it can never race a concurrent
reader or writer, and it refuses to demote whenever there is any doubt
(no source path, non-UTF8 path, unpersisted writes) rather than risk
losing vectors.

Wired into the existing idle sweep (spawn_idle_chunk_eviction_ticker /
CodeIndexer::demote_vector_store_if_idle) added by #2162, rather than a
competing ticker. Gated by TRUSTY_HNSW_REVIEW_IDLE (default on) so the
chunk/BM25/entity eviction path stays unaffected if this needs to be
disabled independently.

Closes #2164

* fix: rehydrate entities in rebuild_symbol_graph to prevent KG-edge loss after eviction

QA found that rebuild_symbol_graph() read self.chunks/self.entities
directly with no rehydration guard, relying on callers to rehydrate
first. Four production call paths do not: remove_file (reconcile.rs,
delete HTTP handler), remove_chunk (FSEvents watcher hot path),
rebuild_symbol_graph_for_reindex (prune-only reindex), and the
contrib-graph ingest endpoint. When bm25_entities_evicted is true and
any of these fire, the graph gets rebuilt from an empty entities
snapshot, silently dropping every entity-derived KG edge (TestedBy,
CoOccursInTest, Documents, ReferencesConcept) for the whole corpus —
and the impoverished graph is then persisted to redb, so the loss
survives a restart. The 300s->60s TTL retune made this state far
easier to hit.

Fix: guard at the single choke point every caller funnels through —
the top of rebuild_symbol_graph() itself — with
ensure_chunks_loaded() + ensure_bm25_entities_loaded(). Both are fast
no-ops when nothing was evicted.

Added a regression test (tests_idle_evict.rs) that builds a graph with
a Documents edge, force-evicts BM25/entities, then calls remove_file
on an unrelated file (the same vulnerable call path) and asserts the
untouched Documents edge survives. Verified the test fails without the
fix (empty edge list) and passes with it.

fix: correct trusty-search rss_mb to true physical footprint (#2168)

Closes #2165

On macOS, sysinfo::Process::memory() reads PROC_PIDTASKINFO's
pti_resident_size, the same getrusage-style figure ru_maxrss reports.
That figure excludes pages the memory compressor currently holds, so a
daemon with several GB compressed can self-report tens of MB of RSS
while vmmap/footprint/Activity Monitor see the true multi-GB physical
footprint. The TRUSTY_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB guardrail keyed off the
under-counted figure could never trip.

libproc's proc_pid_rusage(RUSAGE_INFO_V0).ri_phys_footprint — the same
counter vmmap/footprint report — via libc (already a workspace
dependency, no new crate needed). Wire it into SysMetrics::sample()
(feeds /health's rss_mb) and trusty-search's memguard::current_rss_mb
(feeds the reindex-pipeline guardrail), both falling back to the
existing sysinfo reading on non-macOS platforms or if the libproc call
fails. current_rss_mb() now delegates to current_rss_mb_for_pid() to
remove a near-duplicate sysinfo sampling path.

fix(trusty-mpm): pm_guard exempts native delegated sub-agent edits; retire global UNRESTRICTED bypass (#2107)

Closes #2014

The PreToolUse guard denied Edit/Write from native Claude Code Task/Agent
sub-agents because its only sub-agent exemption keyed on the legacy
CLAUDE_MPM_SUB_AGENT env var, which trusty-mpm stamps on its own nested
process spawns but which a native Task-tool dispatch never sets. This
forced operators to fall back to the all-or-nothing
TRUSTY_MPM_PM_UNRESTRICTED=1 bypass just to unblock ordinary delegated
work, disabling enforcement entirely rather than only for the dispatched
sub-agent.

Claude Code's PreToolUse hook payload documents `agent_id` as present
"only when the hook fires inside a subagent call" specifically so hooks
can distinguish subagent calls from main-thread calls (confirmed against
the live hooks reference). pm_guard now checks for a non-empty
`agent_id` in the payload and allows the call before running the
tool/Bash-verb classification, so delegated sub-agent edits work without
any bypass while the PM's own direct Edit/Write and forbidden Bash verbs
remain denied.

`TRUSTY_MPM_PM_UNRESTRICTED` is kept as a manual, opt-in operator
override (verified: no session-launch or spawn code in this repo ever
sets it), but is no longer needed for normal delegated work now that
native sub-agent dispatches are exempted directly.

feat(trusty-search): idle watcher suspension — stop watching inactive projects (#2077)

A live index's FSEvents watcher previously ran from warm-boot/registration
until the index was deleted, so a host tracking hundreds of registered projects
kept hundreds of live OS watches regardless of use — a standing CPU / fseventsd
cost (the same load that, combined with orphan accumulation, pinned fseventsd
at 8 GB). This adds runtime suspend/resume:

- New `spawn_watcher_idle_suspend_ticker`: every 60s, releases the watcher of
  any index whose in-memory `idle_duration()` exceeds
  TRUSTY_WATCH_IDLE_SUSPEND_SECS (default 900s; 0 disables). Sits above the 300s
  chunk-eviction window, so an idle index sheds heap first, then its watcher.
- Query-wake path in `search_handler`: an index served without a live watcher
  (idle-suspended, or lazily cold-restored — which never spawned one) has its
  watcher re-established via the idempotent `spawn_for_index`, and — only when a
  watcher is actually (re)established — a background reconcile is kicked to catch
  edits missed while unwatched. The query itself serves current in-memory state;
  the reconcile converges subsequent queries. No-op under TRUSTY_DISABLE_WATCHER=1.
- Side fix: lazily cold-restored indexes (issue #993) previously never started a
  watcher; the wake path now gives them one.

To make reconcile callable from the library query path (it was boot-only in the
binary-only `commands` tree), `commands/start/reconcile.rs` moves to

feat(trusty-search): self-managed orphan reaping — stop leaking dead index registrations (#2047)

* feat(trusty-search): self-managed orphan reaping — daemon no longer leaks dead registrations

The daemon previously never removed orphaned index registrations. An ephemeral
MPM worktree (`.worktrees/<uuid>/`) registered and then deleted left a dead
entry in `indexes.toml` forever: warm-boot *detected* the missing `root_path`,
logged "run prune-orphans", and skipped it — but nothing ever removed it. Over
a long-lived daemon these accumulated without bound (a real machine reached 485
dead registrations over 26 days), each holding an idle FSEvents watch that
pinned macOS `fseventsd` at ~100% CPU / 8 GB RSS.

Three complementary mechanisms now keep the registry self-healing:

- Boot self-heal: `heal_boot_orphans` runs at warm-boot start and drops legacy
  (non-colocated) registrations whose root_path was deleted, so they stop being
  re-read every boot. Colocated entries are left for the relocation scan.
- Runtime reaper ticker: an hourly background sweep unregisters live indexes
  whose root vanished mid-run. Cadence via TRUSTY_ORPHAN_REAP_SECS (0 disables).
- Ephemeral-dir ignore: auto-discovery and the colocated rescan skip the
  `.worktrees/` component, so throwaway worktrees are never auto-registered (or
  FSEvents-watched) in the first place. Explicit `index <path>` is unaffected.

Safety:
- Reaping fires only when a root_path is missing AND its immediate parent still
  exists (a deleted worktree leaves `.worktrees/` behind; an unmounted volume
  takes the parent with it). External `/Volumes/…` mounts are excluded outright,
  before any syscall, so a mounted-but-TCC-blocked volume (issues #723/#873) is
  never auto-reaped and stat can never hang the sweep.
- The automatic reaper never deletes on-disk index data, only the registration,
  so a false-positive is always recoverable by re-registering. The interactive
  DELETE /indexes/:id still removes data (via the extracted unregister_index,
  delete_data=true).

fix(trusty-mpm): correct env arg order in managed spawn (-u before CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) (#2009)

POSIX env's grammar is `env [OPTION]... [NAME=VALUE]... [COMMAND]...` — option
flags like `-u NAME` must precede any `NAME=VALUE` assignment. env_bin_prefix
built `env CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY <claude_bin>`, putting
the assignment before the option. Because env stops parsing options at the
first NAME=VALUE token, it then tried to exec `-u` as a command, producing
`env: -u: No such file or directory` and killing every managed session spawn
that resolved a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (i.e. nearly all of them).

Reorder to `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> <claude_bin>` so
the option precedes the assignment. Updates the doc-comment examples and all
hardcoded test assertions to the corrected order, and adds
env_bin_prefix_orders_unset_flag_before_config_dir_assignment as an explicit
regression guard asserting `-u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` appears before
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=` in the built command.

fix(trusty-console): eliminate proxy 500/502 after upstream daemon restart (closes #1984) (#2007)

* fix(trusty-console): eliminate proxy 500/502 after upstream daemon restart (closes #1984)

`tm session new` intermittently failed with a 500/502 from the console
gateway (`:7788/api/mpm/api/v1/sessions/managed`) while a DIRECT POST to
the mpm daemon (`:7880/...`) returned 201. Root cause: the reverse proxy's
shared reqwest::Client kept a default keep-alive connection pool. After the
mpm daemon restarted on its stable port 7880, the first proxied request
reused a STALE pooled connection to the dead process; reqwest does not
retry a non-idempotent POST on a broken pooled connection, so it surfaced
as a proxy error. A graceful bootout (SIGTERM drain → FIN) evicts the
connection cleanly, which is why the failure looked intermittent and only
appeared after hard restarts / crash races.

Fix (entirely in trusty-console, root-cause):
  - server.rs: build the proxy client with pool_max_idle_per_host(0) so no
    idle keep-alive connection is ever retained — every proxied request
    opens a fresh connection to whoever currently owns the port. Loopback
    connect cost is negligible.
  - proxy/routes.rs: send_with_connect_retry() retries EXACTLY once (300ms
    backoff) on an is_connect() error — which, with pooling disabled, proves
    the request was never transmitted, so it is safe for the non-idempotent
    POST (no duplicate-spawn risk). Absorbs the ~1s window where a restarting
    daemon is not yet listening.

Tests: test_connect_retry_recovers (port bound after 120ms → retry succeeds),
test_connect_retry_gives_up (permanently-unbound → one extra attempt, no hang).

cargo clippy -p trusty-console --all-targets -D warnings (clean);
scripts/check_line_cap.sh (0 violations).

* fix(trusty-mpm): fix sudo/env flag-argument bug in orchestrator-exclusion matching (PR #1968)

A fourth trusty-review pass found a genuine bug (confirmed by manual
trace, not a false positive): `sudo -u root make build` resolved the
token after `sudo` (`-u`) as if it were the program name, producing the
bogus tool name `"-u root"` instead of recognising `make`. Because
`is_orchestrator_command` shares this same prefix-stripping logic via
`first_command_token`, the practical effect was that a `make`/`sam`/etc.
invocation wrapped in `sudo -u <user>` (or `env -i`/`env --flag`) would
silently skip the orchestrator-exclusion safety net this whole module
exists to provide — the exact class of incident (an unconditionally
wrapped build orchestrator breaking) the design doc built this
exclusion list to prevent.

Fix: `first_command_token` and `effective_tool_name` now return
`None`/empty (respectively) when the token immediately after `sudo`/
`env` is itself flag-shaped, rather than guessing. `is_orchestrator_
command` now treats that "can't confidently resolve" `None` as
conservatively `true` (assume orchestrator-like, don't rewrite) instead
of `false` — a fail-open-to-fail-closed polarity flip for a check whose

fix(trusty-memory): decouple recall/remember from embedder warm-up (closes #1970) (#1972)

Root cause: memory_recall/memory_recall_deep/memory_recall_all/memory_remember/
memory_note/task_add all called AppState::readiness_check() as a hard preflight
that returned MCP error -32603 ("trusty-memory is warming up...") whenever the
embedder was still cold-initialising (issues #910/#911/#914). trusty-search's
staged pipeline, by contrast, treats the lexical (BM25) lane as independent of
the semantic (vector) lane and never blocks reads/writes on embedder state.

Fix: remove the hard-error preflight and make trusty-memory behave like
trusty-search architecturally:

- Reads (memory_recall/_deep/_all): while AppState::readiness() is Warming,
  skip the vector lane entirely and return retrieve_l0_l1() + BM25 results
  (BM25-only hits are now hydrated from the in-memory drawer table via the
  new bm25_hits_to_recall_results() helper, since fuse_bm25_into_recall() only
  boosts existing vector hits). Once Ready, behavior is unchanged.

- Writes (memory_remember/memory_note/task_add): a new RememberOptions::
  defer_embedding flag lets PalaceHandle::remember_with_options() skip the
  synchronous embed+vector-upsert step and instead spawn a background task
  (spawn_deferred_embed) that awaits the shared embedder and backfills the
  vector once it resolves. KG/redb/BM25 indexing remains fully synchronous,
  so writes are durable and searchable via BM25 immediately; only the vector
  lane trails behind.

AppState::readiness_check() and its only call sites are removed as dead code
now that no handler hard-blocks on embedder state.

Tests: replaced the four "must return warming-up error" tests with tests
asserting the graceful-degradation behavior (writes succeed + defer embedding,
reads return without erroring), added a dedicated backfill test that polls
the vector store until the deferred embed completes, and added a focused unit
test for the new BM25 hydration helper.

fix(trusty-mpm): register provisioned native sessions so session_list finds them (closes #1946) (#1949)

The MCP `session_list` tool read ONLY the legacy `DaemonState.sessions`
registry (native-process discovery, hook auto-register, `POST /sessions`
bookkeeping). Sessions provisioned via the managed path — `session_new` /
`spawn_managed` / the in-project worktree spawn, i.e. exactly how tm
provisions day-to-day sessions — live in the separate `SessionManager`
store and were never surfaced.

Meanwhile the sibling tools `session_stop`/`session_resume`/
`session_decommission`/`session_activity`/`session_send` all target the
`SessionManager` store by id. So a provisioned session could be stopped by
id but its id could never be discovered through `session_list` — the exact
"can't stop the session I'm in from the CLI" gap in #1946.

Fix: `StateBackend::session_list` now unions the legacy registry (tagged
`kind: "legacy"`) with every `SessionManager` record (tagged
`kind: "managed"`, serialized via the shared `record_to_json` so callers
get the managed id + workspace_path/cwd used to target `session_stop`).

Regression coverage: `session_list_includes_managed_sessions` seeds a
managed session the way the real path does and asserts it appears in
`session_list`; `session_list_returns_registered_sessions` is hardened to
an isolated managed store (#1790) since session_list now reads it.

fix(trusty-mpm): reconcile manifest drift, scope roster by project language, fix catalog sync (closes #1940, closes #1941, closes #1947) (#1950)

Three tightly-coupled fixes sharing one root cause: manifest/catalog
source-of-truth gaps.

#1940 — catalog-status false-positive drift. `detect_staleness` keyed
drift on the checksum manifest alone, so a bundled agent absent from the
manifest was reported `new` even when already deployed on disk (the live
manifest tracked 5 of 55 files). New `classify_drift` reconciles the
manifest against the file ACTUALLY on disk under the deployed dir: a
deployed-but-unmanifested file that already matches the catalog content is
no longer drift, and user-owned / user-modified files `apply` would skip
are not reported. A fully-deployed roster now reports 0 changes.

#1941 — full polyglot roster deployed to Rust-only workspaces. New
`project_lang` module auto-detects a project's language(s) from root
marker files (Cargo.toml -> Rust, package.json -> JS/TS family,
pyproject.toml -> Python, go.mod, pom.xml, Gemfile, composer.json,
pubspec.yaml, mix.exs, tauri.conf.json, ...) and produces an agent scope
that excludes foreign-language engineers while keeping BASE-*/agnostic
agents. Wired as the lowest override layer in `resolve_manifest` (below
catalog/user/project), so launch, `catalog status`, and `catalog apply`
all agree. Unknown project types are unscoped (deploy-everything, zero
regression).

#1947 — catalog sync fetches 0 agents. Root cause confirmed: upstream
claude-mpm moved agents to `src/claude_mpm/agents/` as JSON templates, so
`repo/.claude/agents/` is empty and the format is incompatible with
trusty-mpm's composable `.md` agents. Bundled assets are the de-facto
source of truth. Made that honest: `CatalogSyncResult::agents_empty()`,
a `warn!` on a zero-agent fetch, and a clear operator warning from
`tm catalog sync` instead of silently presenting "0 agents" as success.

keep `catalog_sync.rs` under the 500-SLOC cap. Regression tests added for

* fix(trusty-memory): stop console_metrics force-opening every palace on poll (closes #1924)

sustained multi-GB RSS on machines with dozens of palaces (observed: ~82

fix(trusty-mpm): prevent orphan-GC from killing legitimate sessions across daemon restart (closes #1918) (#1921)

DaemonState.sessions is never persisted to disk, so it is always empty
immediately after a daemon restart, while a legacy session's .pid file
(and its still-alive claude process) persists on disk. classify_pidfile
then treats that pidfile as an orphan on the very first post-restart
sweep and the orphan-GC SIGTERMs a perfectly legitimate, actively-used
session.

Add PidOrphanGc, a two-pass debounce for the PID-file sweep modeled on
the existing OrphanGc debounce already used by the tmux-name orphan-GC
for the same class of mid-spawn race. A Terminate verdict is only acted
on once a session-id has been seen as a candidate on two consecutive
sweeps, giving a freshly-restarted daemon one full GC interval (60s
default) to re-learn a session before any SIGTERM is sent. Dead-PID and
PID-reused removals are unaffected — deleting a stale file can never
harm a live process.

Separately (not fixed here, flagged for follow-up): managed sessions
never register with the PID registry at all (only the legacy /sessions
route does via spawn_pid_capture), so they have zero orphan-process
protection in either direction.

feat(trusty-mpm): unify session start with protected-path routing, rename sessions->session, bare tm shortcut (closes #1916) (#1920)

`tm session start` previously bypassed protected-path/managed-clone
segregation entirely: it ran `prepare_session` and a hand-rolled
`POST /sessions` + raw tmux spawn directly on the given/cwd directory,
even when that directory was a live, non-tm-managed GitHub-backed git
checkout (issue #1916). `tm session new` already routed correctly
through `ManagedNew` -> `spawn_managed` -> `spawn_managed_inproject`
(the #1913 protected-worktree fix).

`session start` now detects project/source info from the resolved

guided default already uses) and, when it IS a recognized GitHub-backed

request through `managed_route::run` -- the exact `spawn_managed`/
`spawn_managed_inproject` code path `session new` uses -- rather than
duplicating the routing logic. A directory that is NOT a recognized git
repo has no live source tree to protect (mirrors what `tm connect`
already documents as a supported case), so the original in-place

for that case.
