fix(trusty-mpm): correct launchd plist detection in guided autostart (#1901)

* fix(trusty-mpm): correct launchd plist detection in guided autostart (closes #1900)

`ensure_daemon_started` (guided-default autostart path) checked for the
launchd plist `com.trusty.mpm.supervisor` (label `com.trusty.mpm.supervisor`)
to decide whether the daemon was launchd-managed. That is the WRONG service.

Determination: the supervisor is a real, intentionally-separate OPTIONAL
service (#1206) — its plist (deploy/supervisor/com.trusty.mpm.supervisor.plist,
also emitted by trusty-installer) runs `tm supervisor`, a passive
auto-resume/observer bound to :7881. The MAIN session-manager daemon that bare
`tm` actually talks to registers under a DIFFERENT label, `com.trusty.mpm`
(its plist runs `trusty-mpm daemon --addr 127.0.0.1:7880`). So `.supervisor`
was not a typo; the code was conflating "is the supervisor installed" with
"is the main daemon launchd-managed".

Because the lookup always missed the real main-daemon plist,
`try_launchctl_start` always returned `Unavailable` and every autostart fell
through to a raw detached `Command::new(exe).arg("daemon").spawn()` instead of
nudging the managed daemon via `launchctl bootstrap`. When this raced a
transient health-check miss while the real daemon was running, it spawned a
second daemon that lost the port, bound a random ephemeral port, and became an
orphaned, untracked stray (observed: PID 13944 on :50541).

Fix:
- Replace SUPERVISOR_PLIST_LABEL/supervisor_plist_path with the main-daemon
  label `com.trusty.mpm` and a pure, home-injectable path helper
  (`plist_path_in`) plus a pure decision gate
  (`main_daemon_managed_by_launchd_in`) so the launchd-vs-spawn branch is
  unit-testable with temp dirs (no touching real ~/Library/LaunchAgents).
- `ensure_daemon_started` now routes through `launchctl bootstrap` when the
  real main-daemon plist is installed, and only raw-spawns when launchd
  genuinely cannot help.

Hardening (#1900 optional): the raw fallback spawn now records the child PID
in a discoverable pidfile (`~/.trusty-mpm/autostart-daemon.pid`) so a
raced/orphaned autostart daemon is trackable/killable rather than invisible;
`daemon::cleanup_lock_file` (the stop path) removes it, mirroring the existing
lock-file cleanup.

Tests: main_daemon_plist_path_uses_main_label, main_daemon_managed_by_launchd,
main_daemon_managed_ignores_supervisor_only_home (direct #1900 regression
guard), autostart_pidfile_roundtrip.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(trusty-mpm): clean up stale autostart pidfile on health-check failure

The #1900 hardening records the fallback-spawn child PID in a discoverable
pidfile (`autostart-daemon.pid`) via `write_autostart_pidfile`, but only the
`daemon stop` path (`cleanup_lock_file`) ever removed it. If the post-spawn
`/health` poll in `ensure_daemon_started` timed out (all 10 iterations fail),
the function `bail!`ed without removing the pidfile it had just written.

Precise failure mode: the pidfile stores exactly one PID and is overwritten on
each spawn, so it does NOT accumulate entries. Instead, a failed/unreachable
autostart leaves the pidfile pointing at a stale/wrong PID — a child that never
became reachable (may have exited immediately or bound an unreachable address).
Between a failed autostart and the next spawn, `tm`'s own tooling would read
that pidfile and probe a PID that no longer corresponds to a healthy daemon.

Fix: track the framework root when the fallback spawn happens and, in the
health-poll timeout branch, call `remove_autostart_pidfile()` before bailing so
a failed autostart leaves no misleading pidfile (mirrors the stop-path cleanup).
Only a pidfile written by this same call is removed — the launchd path leaves it
untouched.

Also add a one-line comment at the child-handle drop site noting the drop is
intentional (the daemon is meant to outlive this process; on Unix it re-parents
to init on our exit).

fix(trusty-mpm): auto-transition sessions to stopped when runtime process exits (closes #1814) (#1894)

Managed-clone sessions (`tm launch` / agent delegation) run `claude` inside a
tmux pane. When that inner process EXITS but the tmux session stays alive, the
pane falls back to a bare login shell with no client attached. The existing
reapers all missed this case:

- `reap_dead_managed_sessions` (#1744) only transitions a record to `Stopped`
  when its whole tmux *session* has disappeared.
- The orphan-GC deliberately KEEPS any session tracked by the store (gate 2 of
  `classify_session`), so a tracked `Active` record is never touched.

Result: a runtime-exited managed session stayed marked `active` forever — 30+
phantom sessions accumulated for a single project on 2026-06-29. Per the SESSION
LIFECYCLE principle (session != process), such a session must transition
`active` -> `stopped` (resumable; workspace + record intact), NOT decommissioned.

Mechanism: a new `daemon::runtime_reap` module, wired into the existing 60s
`reap_loop`. Each tick it enumerates live managed panes (name +
`pane_current_command` + shell PID via `TmuxDriver::list_managed_panes`) and, for
every `Active` record whose pane is present but has dropped to a bare shell,
routes it through the EXISTING `SessionManager::stop` path (kills the leftover
shell, marks `Stopped`). Detection reuses the orphan-GC's fail-closed primitives
`is_idle_shell` (shell allowlist) and the `ChildLivenessProbe` belt-and-braces
gate (spares a `claude` that is mid-spawn under the shell). Sessions whose tmux
session is entirely gone are left to the #1744 reaper — the two never double-act.

Detection and transition are unit-tested end-to-end against a `FakeNoopTmuxDriver`
(no real tmux): `stop_runtime_exited_transitions_active_to_stopped` asserts an
Active session whose pane reports `zsh` becomes `Stopped`, while
`stop_runtime_exited_keeps_running_session` asserts a `claude` pane stays Active.

fix(trusty-review): unify grade computation so outer and embedded grade never diverge (closes #1886) (#1891)

Root cause: `ReviewResult` exposes the letter grade in two observable places.
The top-level `grade` field is the authoritative value the pipeline computes
once (severity floor → #1486 post-verification clamp → #1877 shallow-review
cap). But in the unified single-pass path `review_body` stores the RAW LLM
response verbatim, which embeds the model's OWN self-assessed `"grade"` in its
JSON output block. Those two were never reconciled, so any late-stage
adjustment that lowered the top-level grade below the model's self-assessment
left the embedded grade stale and HIGHER — the outer field read harsher than
the grade printed inside `review_body` (issue #1886: outer "C"/"C+" vs embedded
"B+" across PRs #1879/#1883/#1884). This is not a second grading computation;
it is one computed value plus one un-reconciled raw model value.

Fix: keep the single source of truth (top-level `result.grade`) and propagate
it into the embedded JSON so the two can never disagree — no grading logic is
duplicated. New `pipeline::grade_reconcile::reconcile_review_body_grade` rewrites
every JSON `"grade": "…"` value in `review_body` to the final grade; it is a
conservative, dependency-free string rewrite that preserves all surrounding
prose/fences, ignores `"grade_justification"`, is byte-safe amid UTF-8, and
no-ops on prose-only bodies and on an un-reviewable UNKNOWN (grade `None`, #1474).
It is called after the grade is fully settled and before the footer is appended,
in BOTH the single-pass (`runner.rs`) and map-reduce (`runner_mapreduce.rs`)
finalisation paths.

Tests: `grade_reconcile_tests.rs` pins the rewrite across direct-JSON, fenced
block, prose-only, multi-occurrence, whitespace, non-string, UTF-8, and
truncated-tail cases. New end-to-end `run_review_outer_and_embedded_grade_agree_after_shallow_cap`
drives a model self-grade of "A+" through the #1877 shallow cap and asserts the
grade re-parsed from `review_body` equals the top-level grade (and is no longer
the stale "A+").

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(trusty-review): aggregate token counts across map-reduce for shallow-review heuristic (closes #1885) (#1890)

The shallow_clean_review heuristic (#1877) flags a suspiciously cheap clean
APPROVE by comparing output_tokens against a floor proportional to the diff
size. It was wired only into the unified single-call path. On the map-reduce
path (used for the LARGEST diffs) result.output_tokens stayed 0 because per-call
token telemetry was never aggregated onto the result, so the heuristic silently
never fired on exactly the highest-risk reviews.

Fix: thread aggregate token/cost telemetry through the map-reduce stages and
apply the SAME heuristic uniformly.

- Add `TokenUsage` (saturating accumulator) to mapreduce::outcome; carry it on
  `MapOutcome::Reviewed` and `ReducedReview`.
- map stage: capture each chunk call's input/output tokens + cost.
- reduce stage: sum `TokenUsage` across every reviewed chunk.
- synthesis stage: fold the synthesis call's usage onto the map-stage total
  (preserved unchanged on the disabled/fail-safe fall-back paths).
- runner_mapreduce: set result.input_tokens/output_tokens/cost_estimate_usd
  from the aggregate, then run is_shallow_clean_review / cap_shallow_review_grade
  in fold_reduced_into_result using filtered_byte_size as the diff-length analog

fix(trusty-mpm): output-style resolution + test-isolation hygiene (#1860, #1863, #1858)

* fix(trusty-mpm): thread FrameworkPaths through deploy to stop ~/.claude test leak (#1860)

prepare_session's output-style deploy step called dirs::home_dir() directly,
ignoring the injected FrameworkPaths base. Under test isolation
(FrameworkPaths::under(tempdir)) this silently wrote to the real
~/.claude/output-styles/trusty-mpm.md instead of the test-scoped temp dir,
leaking state between test runs.

Add FrameworkPaths::claude_home_dir(), which recovers the exact base a
FrameworkPaths was resolved against (real home for default(), temp dir for
under()), and route the output-style deploy through it instead of
re-resolving dirs::home_dir() at the call site.

* fix(trusty-mpm): resolve effective outputStyle across project+global scopes (#1863)

check_output_style previously stopped looking at project settings as soon as
the project .claude/settings.json file existed, even when that file had no
outputStyle key. Since project settings only override keys they actually
set, a project file silent on outputStyle must fall through to the global
~/.claude/settings.json value — the old logic instead silently reported Warn
("no outputStyle key") and never inspected the bad global value, which is
the exact DOC-28 R4 incident condition this probe exists to catch.

Rewrite the resolution as: read the project settings file first (when
project_dir is given); if it is silent (missing file or missing key), fall
back to the global settings file. Malformed/unreadable settings at either
scope still Fail immediately. The report now names which scope ("project"
vs "global") supplied the resolved value.

Add regression tests for the incident condition (project settings present
but silent, and project settings absent entirely) plus a test asserting the
Ok message names the resolved scope.

* fix(trusty-mpm): inject color mode into shade_image to stop banner test race (#1858)

image_shading_emits_truecolor in two_panel.rs raced every sibling test in the
same file: shade_image() read the process-global colored::control override
internally, and ~13 tests in that file flip that same global via
set_override(true/false) with no synchronization across parallel test
threads.

Make shade_image(art, use_color) take the color decision as an explicit
parameter instead of probing the global. load_and_shade_banner() — the one
legitimate production call site — still probes colored::control once and
threads the result down, preserving live behavior (NO_COLOR / non-TTY
detection via NoColorGuard). Every call site (production and tests, across
two_panel.rs and bin/tm/tests.rs) now passes an explicit bool, so the
color-sensitive tests are pure and deterministic and no longer need
set_override/unset_override or the COLOR_LOCK mutex.

Verified with 10 back-to-back full runs of the banner test module under
default parallel threading: 49/49 passing every time.

extraction in `format_daemon_row` uses `rfind(':')` which works on both forms).

fix(trusty-mpm): RAII guard kills leaked tmux sessions after test/error (#1815) (#1821)

`launch()` and `connect()` in `commands/launch.rs` create detached tmux
sessions via `tmux new-session -d` but — before this fix — had no cleanup
path for any failure between session creation and a successful
`attach-session`.  In integration tests that run without a TTY,
`attach-session` always fails with "not a terminal", so every test that
called `fallback_protected` → `launch()` orphaned a `tmpm-*` session.
Over many test runs the host accumulated dozens of leaked sessions.

Fix: introduce `LaunchSessionGuard` — a minimal RAII struct whose `Drop`
impl calls `tmux kill-session -t <name>` best-effort.  The guard is created
immediately after step 12 (`new-session` succeeds) in both `launch()` and
`connect()`, and is disarmed only after step 14 (`attach-session`) returns
successfully (i.e. the user detached normally).  Any error path — including
the no-TTY case that always fires in tests — therefore reaps the session.

`connect()` special-case: when the session was already running
(`already_running = true`), no guard is created so an attach failure on an
existing user-owned session never accidentally kills it.

Verified: isolated test run of `tests_behavior_c::guided_fallback_does_not_
refuse_github_ssh_alias_remote` (the worst offender) shows BEFORE=42,
AFTER=42 tmpm-* sessions — zero net leaks.

  preventing the lazy initialiser from ever touching real tmux.  Includes
  a hard panic guard if the caller accidentally passes `~/.trusty-mpm`.

  from `DaemonState::with_root(...)` to `with_root_isolated_managed(...)`.

* fix(trusty-mpm): prevent double-daemon spawn on EALREADY, strip port from github_host

Two defects found in code review (PR #1776):

HIGH — double-daemon spawn on EALREADY:
`try_launchctl_start` previously returned bool, treating launchctl exit 37
(EALREADY — service already bootstrapped) the same as "plist absent". This
caused `ensure_daemon_started` to delete the lock file and spawn a second
daemon even when launchd already owned the service, creating a race for the
port.

Fix: replace the bool return with a `LaunchctlOutcome` tri-state enum:
- `Launched`      — launchctl exit 0 (newly started)
- `AlreadyLoaded` — exit 37 / EALREADY or matching stderr message
- `Unavailable`   — plist absent, id -u failed, or unknown error

`ensure_daemon_started` only enters the lock-delete+spawn path on `Unavailable`;
on `Launched` or `AlreadyLoaded` it skips straight to the health-poll loop.

MEDIUM — github_host port regression:
The scheme-URL branch returned "github.com:443" for `https://github.com:443/…`,
causing `is_github_remote` to return false — a regression vs the prior
substring-match. Fix: strip a trailing `:<port>` suffix (all-ASCII-digit after
the colon) from the host token before returning.

Also adds regression tests:
- `github_host_strips_port_from_https_url` (in guided_autostart.rs tests)
- `is_github_remote_accepts_github_com_https_with_port` (in tests_behavior_c_tests.rs)

Note: `test_mcp_config_review_no_home_write` failure seen in full-suite runs is
a pre-existing test-isolation race on origin/main: the test passes 15/15 in
isolation (`cargo test -- global_config`) and global_config.rs is byte-identical
to origin/main (diff = 0). The failure is caused by parallel tests mutating HOME
without serial-test guards, not by this branch.

fix(trusty-installer): detect unwritable self-update target, report actual install dir (#1770)

* fix(trusty-installer): detect unwritable self-update target and report actual install dir (SPEC-INSTALLER-01)

Before this change, `trusty-installer self-update` would:
1. Call try_install_prebuilt into current_exe().parent() (e.g. /usr/local/bin)
2. If the atomic rename failed due to insufficient permissions, fall through
   to the cargo fallback which installed to ~/.cargo/bin instead
3. Print "updated via cargo. Restart to apply." — a misleading success when
   the binary on PATH at /usr/local/bin was never replaced

This commit fixes both failure modes:

(a) Up-front writability probe: is_dir_writable() creates and removes a temp
file in the resolved install dir before any download attempt. On failure it
prints an actionable error naming the dir and exits 1 immediately — no download
is started, no misleading success is possible.

(b) Truthful cargo-fallback message: cargo_updated_message() compares the cargo
install dir (~/.cargo/bin) with the original binary's dir. When they differ it
emits a WARNING naming both paths and stating "was NOT replaced".

New unit tests cover: writable temp dir passes, read-only dir fails (unix),
error message names path, cargo-fallback warns on divergent dirs, same dir no
warning, None dir no warning, cargo install dir ends in bin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(trusty-installer): only abort self-update on permission-denied target, fall through on transient probe errors

The previous commit added an up-front writability probe but used a bool return
from is_dir_writable(), which treated ANY tempfile failure (ENOSPC, NotFound,
races) as "not writable" — hard-aborting the self-update for errors where the
existing prebuilt-attempt + cargo-fallback path could have still succeeded.
This was a behavioral regression removing a previously-working code path.

Fix: Replace the bool probe with a WriteProbe tri-state enum:
  - WriteProbe::Writable       → proceed with self-update
  - WriteProbe::PermissionDenied → abort up-front with actionable error (the real bug)
  - WriteProbe::Other(e)       → log tracing::warn!, fall through to prebuilt/cargo

probe_install_dir() inspects io::Error::kind() to distinguish PermissionDenied
from all other error kinds. is_dir_writable() (the bool version) is removed.

New tests:
  - probe_writable_temp_dir: Writable on a user-owned temp dir
  - probe_nonwritable_dir_is_permission_denied (unix): 0o555 dir → PermissionDenied
  - probe_nonexistent_dir_is_other_not_permission_denied: /nonexistent/... → Other,
    proving transient errors do NOT abort the self-update

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(trusty-installer): abort self-update early on storage-full / read-only target, fall through only on transient probe errors

StorageFull (ENOSPC) and ReadOnlyFilesystem (EROFS) both predict that the
subsequent prebuilt-binary write and cargo install into the SAME directory will
also fail. Falling through on these errors wastes network/CPU time and then
fails anyway — worse, it could install to a different directory (cargo fallback
to ~/.cargo/bin) while the target dir issue is left silent.

Changes:
- WriteProbe gains two new abort variants: StorageFull and ReadOnlyFilesystem
- classify_probe_error() is extracted as a pure helper that maps io::ErrorKind
  to the right WriteProbe variant — testable without OS side-effects
- probe_install_dir() now delegates to classify_probe_error()
- run() matches all three abort variants, each with a distinct actionable message
- storage_full_error() and read_only_fs_error() join unwritable_dir_error()
  as pure message helpers for the three abort cases
- WriteProbe::Other (the fall-through arm) is now reserved for genuinely
  transient/inconclusive kinds (Interrupted, NotFound, races, etc.)

Uses ErrorKind::StorageFull and ErrorKind::ReadOnlyFilesystem — both stabilized
in Rust 1.83, well within the MSRV of 1.91.

New tests (6 added, all pure/no disk-filling):
  - classify_permission_denied_aborts
  - classify_storage_full_aborts
  - classify_read_only_filesystem_aborts
  - classify_interrupted_is_other
  - storage_full_error_names_path
  - read_only_fs_error_names_path

* feat(trusty-installer): prebuilt-binary download layer + prebuilt-first install (closes #1760)

Phase 2 of trusty-installer (#1760): add a prebuilt-binary download layer and
wire it as the default install/upgrade path on Tier-1 platforms, with automatic
cargo fallback on unsupported targets or any download/verify/extract failure.

## New module: crates/trusty-installer/src/download/

Three focused submodules, each under the 500 SLOC cap:

- `platform.rs`: Tier-1 target detection via `std::env::consts`. Recognises
  `aarch64-apple-darwin` (macOS arm64) and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` (Linux
  x86_64). All other targets (Intel Mac, Linux arm64, Windows) return `None`
  and fall back to cargo install.

- `release.rs`: GitHub Releases API queries. Fetches all releases, filters by
  `<crate>-v*` tag prefix, selects the highest stable semver (skips prerelease
  API flags AND semver pre-release identifiers), and constructs deterministic
  asset + SHA-256 URLs. Honours GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN for rate-limit avoidance
  in CI.

- `fetch.rs`: HTTP download (streaming reqwest), SHA-256 verification (sha2),
  tar.gz extraction (flate2 + tar), and atomic binary placement. Downloads into
  a temp dir; verifies checksum before trusting any bytes; extracts ALL regular
  files from the archive (so multi-binary crates like trusty-search ship all
  their binaries); atomically renames each binary into the install dir.

- `mod.rs`: Public orchestrator (`try_install_prebuilt`) + `Outcome` enum
  (`Installed` / `Fallback`). Returns `Fallback` with a human-readable reason
  on any failure (non-Tier-1, API 404, SHA mismatch, I/O). Default install dir
  is `~/.local/bin` (mirrors install.sh); falls back to `~/.cargo/bin`.

## Wire-up: install.rs + upgrade.rs

- `install_one` now calls `try_install_prebuilt` first; on `Outcome::Fallback`
  verifies cargo is on PATH before delegating to `perform_upgrade`.
- `upgrade_one` (new helper) does the same for upgrade candidates; daemons still
  go through `upgrade_and_restart` for the connection-safe restart step.
- Both paths verify with `verify_installed_binary` after success.

## New workspace dependencies

- `flate2 = "1"` — gzip decompression for tarballs
- `tar = "0.4"` — tar archive extraction
- `semver = { version = "1", features = ["serde"] }` — release tag comparison
- `tempfile` moved from dev-dependencies to dependencies in trusty-installer
  (production code uses it for the atomic temp-dir staging)

## Tests (all offline, no real network calls)

- Platform: `is_tier1_target` predicate, `current_target` host probe
- Release: semver selection (max wins, pre-releases skipped, other crates
  ignored), URL construction pinned to expected shapes
- Fetch: SHA-256 parse (bare hex + shasum format, invalid rejected),
  digest mismatch detection, multi-binary extraction, directory-prefix
  stripping, atomic placement, optional binary skipping
- Orchestrator: fallback decision logic, `Outcome` variant field access,
  default install dir resolution

3 live-network tests are tagged `#[ignore]` and run with `--include-ignored`.

## What is NOT included (later phases)

- Self-update (trusty-installer upgrading itself)
- Interactive component picker UI
- claude-mpm bridge

* fix(trusty-mpm): idempotent catalog sync — update existing checkout, recover corrupt (closes #1751)

Previously `CatalogSync::sync` called `git clone` unconditionally after
`create_dir_all`, so a second sync failed with:
  "fatal: destination path '…/catalog/repo' already exists and is not an empty directory."

Root cause: `catalog_sync.rs` line 216-220 (before this fix) — `create_dir_all`
created the target dir, then `clone_repo` was always called regardless.

Fix: add `is_git_repo`, `remote_url`, and `fetch_and_reset` to the `GitBackend`
trait, implemented for both `RealGitBackend` (shells out to git) and
`FakeGitBackend` (reads/writes minimal `.git/config`). Replace the unconditional
clone with `ensure_repo`, a three-branch decision function:
  1. dir absent → fresh clone
  2. valid git repo with matching origin → fetch + hard-reset (update in place)
  3. non-git dir, wrong remote, or corrupt → guard_remove + re-clone

The `guard_remove` safety guard refuses to remove any path outside the catalog
directory. URL normalisation (`urls_match`) handles trailing slashes and `.git`
suffixes so equivalent URL forms don't trigger spurious re-clones.

Tests:
- `catalog_sync_second_sync_succeeds` — second forced sync succeeds (the bug)
- `catalog_sync_corrupt_dir_reclones` — non-git dir recovered via re-clone
- `catalog_sync_wrong_remote_reclones` — wrong remote triggers re-clone

* fix(trusty-review): decouple AppState build from MCP initialize handshake (closes #1739)

`trusty-review serve --stdio` previously called `build_app_state()`
synchronously before starting the MCP stdio loop. `build_app_state`
includes `enforce_verifier_liveness()` which makes a real Bedrock Converse
API call — on a host with broken/unreachable credentials this retries 3×
and takes ~7.4 s. Claude Code sends `initialize` immediately on spawn with
a ~1.5 s deadline, so the server was consistently marked DEGRADED.

feed the result through a `watch::Sender<DeferredStateValue>` channel.
Start the MCP stdio loop immediately via the new `mcp::run_deferred(rx)` entry
point. `dispatch_deferred` answers `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`,
and `tools/list` without touching the channel (zero network calls). Tool
calls await `state_rx.wait_for()` with a 30 s timeout, returning a graceful
JSON-RPC INTERNAL_ERROR on timeout or build failure. HTTP mode is unchanged.

Adds 6 unit tests: initialize/tools/list/notification without state, tool call
with ready/failed/dropped-sender states.

* fix(trusty-mpm): robust daemon URL resolution — probe stale TRUSTY_MPM_URL (closes #1731)

Root cause: `resolve_daemon_url` treated any explicit non-default URL
(e.g. `TRUSTY_MPM_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7881`) as unconditionally
winning, skipping the lock-file read entirely.  When the daemon
restarts on a different port the stale env var permanently points `tm`
at a dead address, causing the guided-default path to fall into the
protected fallback instead of showing the session picker.

The daemon already writes `~/.trusty-mpm/daemon.lock` at startup with
the actual bound URL (daemon_run.rs); the bug was purely in the client-
side resolution logic.

Changes:
- Add `resolve_daemon_url_probing(client, explicit)` async fn to
  `core/discovery.rs` (and export from `core/mod.rs`).  Same three-step
  precedence as the sync variant, but the explicit override is accepted
  only after a 500 ms GET /health probe; on failure the function falls
  through to the lock file then DEFAULT_DAEMON_URL.  Reachable explicit
  URLs (including `--url http://…:9999`) still win immediately.
- Wire `resolve_daemon_url_probing` into `bin/tm/main.rs` for the
  primary URL resolution (line 195) so all `tm` subcommands benefit.
- Add two unit tests in `core/discovery.rs`:
  - `probing_resolver_falls_back_when_explicit_unreachable`: port 1
    (reserved, always refused) must NOT be returned; result must be a
    valid HTTP URL.
  - `probing_resolver_wins_when_explicit_reachable`: a minimal TCP
    listener (tokio) responding HTTP 200 must be returned verbatim.

* fix(trusty-mpm): trim trailing slash before /health probe (refs #1731)

`probe_url` concatenated `url + "/health"` without first stripping a
trailing slash, so a base URL of `http://127.0.0.1:7880/` produced
the path `//health`.  Strict HTTP servers return 404 for double-slash
paths, making a live daemon appear unreachable and causing
`resolve_daemon_url_probing` to fall through to the lock file or default
even when the daemon was listening.

Changes:
- `probe_url`: call `url.trim_end_matches('/')` before `format!("{base}/health")`.
- Add `probe_url_trims_trailing_slash` unit test: binds a TCP listener,
  captures the HTTP request line, asserts it is "GET /health …" (no `//`).

fix(trusty-search): HNSW data-loss guard — refuse empty-over-populated save (closes #1711) (#1716)

* fix(trusty-search): defensive HNSW overwrite guard + regression tests (closes #1711)

Add a data-loss guard in UsearchStore::save() that refuses to overwrite
an on-disk HNSW snapshot larger than 100 KB when the in-memory index has
0 vectors.  The shutdown flush path introduced in PR #1671 (commit
fe4c0b28) via reconcile_stale_indexes() created a race: a newly promoted
but not-yet-populated UsearchStore could race SIGTERM and persist 0
vectors on top of a fully-populated snapshot.  The guard fires, logs a
tracing::error!, and returns Ok(()) preserving the on-disk state.

Three regression tests added to core/store/tests.rs:
  - test_save_refuses_to_overwrite_populated_snapshot_with_empty_index
  - test_save_does_not_block_first_time_creation
  - test_save_populated_index_writes_correctly (happy-path guard)

Quality bar: cargo check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test (all pass),
cargo fmt --check, check_line_cap.sh — all green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(trusty-search): make #1711 shutdown guard test real, fix TOCTOU, bump 0.29.1

- Promote POPULATED_SNAPSHOT_THRESHOLD_BYTES to pub(super) module-level
  const near INITIAL_CAPACITY so tests can reference it without magic
  literals (items 1, 3).

- Fix TOCTOU (HIGH-2): move the 0-vector data-loss guard UNDER the same
  write-lock scope that owns the usearch save() call. Previously the
  guard acquired a separate read-lock to call index.size(), then released
  it before the write-lock — leaving a window where the size could change
  between check and save. Now: acquire write-lock once, check index.size()
  under it, conditionally refuse and return Ok(()), or proceed with save.
  No window between check and save.

- Rewrite the vacuous regression test (HIGH-1):
  test_save_refuses_to_overwrite_populated_snapshot_with_empty_index
  previously saved 5 real vectors (far under 100 KB) so the guard never
  fired and the test asserted nothing meaningful. Rewritten to write a
  filler file of POPULATED_SNAPSHOT_THRESHOLD_BYTES+1 bytes at the HNSW
  path, then call save() on a fresh empty store, then assert byte-for-byte
  identity — proving the guard fired and the snapshot was preserved.

- Add residual-risk comment referencing follow-up issue #1717: the guard
  catches only the exact-0-vector case; a non-zero but catastrophically-
  partial in-memory index (e.g. mid-reindex) is not caught; root-cause
  race (reconcile_stale_indexes / fe4c0b28) tracked separately.

feat(trusty-review): #1618 accept & use caller-supplied PR context for reviewer + verifier (#1623)

trusty-review previously reviewed from the diff alone on the local-diff path
(no GitHub fetch), so a caller (CI/editor/MCP) could not hand it the PR
description, the human review/issue discussion (author rationale), or related
source the diff depends on. This adds OPTIONAL, backward-compatible caller
context and threads it to BOTH the reviewer and the adversarial verifier.

Contract — new OPTIONAL fields on ReviewRequest (service/handlers.rs), serde
Option + #[serde(default)] so existing callers are unaffected:
  - pr_description:  Option<String>  // PR body/description prose
  - pr_discussion:   Option<String>  // concatenated human review/issue comments
  - referenced_code: Option<String>  // caller-supplied referenced/related code

Implementation (generic, provider-agnostic — no Duetto-specific logic):
- New CallerContext carrier on ReviewInput (default = all None ⇒ one-line at the
  5 non-HTTP construction sites). handle_review populates it from ReviewRequest.
- Reviewer: ReviewContext gains the 3 fields; build_user_message renders each as
  a labelled section ("## PR Description", "## PR Discussion / Author Rationale",
  "## Referenced Code") ONLY when present/non-empty (no empty sections). Populated
  on BOTH the GitHub-fetch and local_diff_text paths (runner injects from input).
- Verifier: build_author_rationale folds description+discussion into one block,
  threaded maybe_verify → run_verification_round → build_verify_request and
  rendered in the verifier user message. verifier_system_prompt gains generic
  guidance: when the author has explicitly verified external-system state, treat
  it as plausible and respond REFUTED if the only remaining doubt is unverifiable
  speculation about external systems the author claims to have checked. The
  diff-grounding rules are unchanged (a diff-demonstrated problem stays CONFIRMED).

Calibration adjacency (capping diff-visible-but-unverifiable-external-data
findings to advisory): DEFERRED — not a small in-area change. It needs a new
materiality signal on Finding plumbed from the LLM JSON (parser.rs) into
grade.rs::severity_floor + a reviewer-prompt schema field; tracked separately to

fix(trusty-common): accept key=value secret-filter tokens with slash-path values (closes #1676) (#1678)

The `=` branch in `is_structural_token` was evaluated AFTER the `/` branch.
Tokens containing both `=` and `/` (e.g. `reviewer_model=openrouter/openai/gpt-5.4-mini-20260317`)
were routed to the slash-path check first, where the first `/`-segment
(`reviewer_model=openrouter`) contains `=`, which is not in `is_word_segment`'s
allowed charset, so it failed the check and fell through to the entropy heuristics
— incorrectly flagged as a credential.

in the `=` branch: LHS must be a word segment AND the RHS must be either a word
segment or a slash-path (all `/`-separated segments are word-like). This allows
`key=provider/model/version` while keeping high-entropy opaque blobs non-structural.
Base64 blobs with `+` in the encoded form still fail the early `+` guard before
reaching the reordered `=` check.

fix(embedder): pin ORT intra-op to 1 + disable spinning to break CUDA deferred-embed deadlock (#1668)

The deferred-embed background pass deadlocks inside ORT's intra-op thread
pool (libonnxruntime 1.24.2, CUDA provider): a couple of workers busy-spin
at ~70% CPU while the rest block forever in condition_variable::wait on an
ORT barrier, producing 0 embeddings and an empty 112-byte HNSW index
(code-intelligence #1542).

Root cause: fastembed-rs (5.13.4) hardcodes
`Session::builder()?.with_intra_threads(available_parallelism())` on every
session it creates and exposes no hook to override it. So the single shared
FastEmbedder ORT session spins up one intra-op thread per logical CPU (8 on
the GPU instance), and that multi-threaded intra-op barrier deadlocks. The
"workers: 2" vs "8 ORT threads" mismatch is two orthogonal pools: the
trusty-search EmbedPool runs 2 worker threads that all funnel through ONE
Arc<dyn Embedder> (one ORT session), and that one session's intra-op pool is
sized to the CPU count — not 2x4.

Fix: commit an ORT *global* thread pool before any fastembed session is
created. ort 2.0.0-rc.12's commit path calls DisablePerSessionThreads when a
global pool exists, so fastembed's per-session with_intra_threads(N) is
overridden by the global pool's settings:
- intra-op threads = 1 (default): removes the barrier — no sibling worker to
  wait on, so the pass can never deadlock.
- inter-op threads = 1 (default): keeps total ORT threads deterministic.
- spin control off (default): kills the busy-wait half of the deadlock.

Knobs are configurable via TRUSTY_ORT_INTRA_THREADS / TRUSTY_ORT_INTER_THREADS
/ TRUSTY_ORT_ALLOW_SPINNING but default to the safe single-threaded, no-spin
profile. resolve_ort_threading_options() is a pure, unit-tested resolver
(mirrors resolve_cuda_options); init_ort_runtime() commits the global pool
once via OnceLock.

A from-source CUDA rebuild on the AL2023 GPU host is still required before
this can be validated on the GPU (separate ops step).

chore(trusty-agents): make ETXTBSY backoff shift overflow-safe (closes #1642) (#1645)

The ETXTBSY spawn-retry backoff computed `BACKOFF_MS * (1 << attempt)`. The
`1 << attempt` shift is safe at the current MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, but is a latent
overflow hazard if MAX_ATTEMPTS is ever raised. Make the shift explicit
(`1u64 << attempt`) and use a saturating multiply so the computation stays
overflow-safe for any reasonable MAX_ATTEMPTS. Behavior is unchanged for the
current value (5ms, 10ms, 20ms).

matrix is unit-tested against a fake probe and a tempfile dir — no real process
is ever signalled in tests. 15 pid_registry + 4 process tests pass.

Behavior:
- `post-commit`: calls `add`/`remove` for changed/deleted files after each commit

- Hooks are wrapped in `# >>> trusty-search >>> ... # <<< trusty-search <<<`
  marker blocks — append-safe, coexists with other tools in the same hook file
- `install` is idempotent: re-running replaces the existing block in-place
- `uninstall` removes only the trusty-search block, preserves all other content
- Files are written atomically (tmp + rename) and chmod +x

fix(trusty-memory): serialize env-mutating cwd_palace_slug_at tests to stop CI flake (#1624)

The three pin-file tests (`cwd_palace_slug_at_prefers_pin_file`,
`cwd_palace_slug_at_reads_pin_from_subdir`, and
`cwd_palace_slug_at_pin_read_does_not_create_pin_file`) were missing
`#[serial_test::serial]` and an `EnvGuard::clear` call, making them
vulnerable to env-var leakage from the sibling test
`cwd_palace_slug_at_env_override_wins`.

The resolution order in `cwd_palace_slug_at` is:
  1. `TRUSTY_MEMORY_PALACE` env override (highest precedence)
  2. Pin file (`.trusty-tools/trusty-memory.yaml`)
  3. git-derived slug

When the env-setting test ran concurrently with the pin-file tests, the
leaked env var fired step 1 and returned "my-override" before the pin
file at step 2 was ever reached — causing the pin-file tests to fail
intermittently on `main` and therefore on every PR.

Fix: add `#[serial_test::serial]` and `let _guard = EnvGuard::clear(...)`
to all three pin-file tests. This places them in the same serial token
group as the env-setting test, preventing concurrent execution and
guaranteeing the env var is absent for the duration of each pin-file test.
Updated test doc comments explain the isolation contract.

fix(trusty-review): envelope verdict/grade derive from review_body (#1486) + expose calibration thresholds via env (#1597) (#1603)

* fix(trusty-review): envelope verdict/grade derive from post-verification review_body (closes #1486)

Root cause: clamp_grade_to_verdict(F, APPROVE) is a no-op because F implies
BLOCK (ordinal 3), which is already strictly stricter than APPROVE (ordinal 0),
so the clamp condition (is_at_least_as_strict(BLOCK, APPROVE) = true) left the
grade unchanged at F even after verification relaxed the verdict to APPROVE.

Fix: thread the original LLM grade (pre-floor) through apply_grade_and_floor as
a third return value.  After verification re-derives the verdict, clamp the
*original LLM grade* (e.g. B-) to the post-verification verdict instead of the
floor-escalated grade (e.g. F).  clamp_grade_to_verdict(B-, APPROVE) = B-
(correct: APPROVE is consistent with B-), while clamp_grade_to_verdict(B-,
BLOCK) = F (correct: BLOCK's only consistent grade is F).

Adds two regression tests in runner_tests.rs:
- envelope_grade_tracks_verdict_after_verification_relaxation_1486: high finding
  is REFUTED → verdict relaxes to APPROVE → envelope must show APPROVE + B-

  is CONFIRMED → verdict remains BLOCK → envelope shows BLOCK + F

feat(trusty-mpm): WI-1 isolation regression-guard with version capture (closes #1582, refs #1548) (#1583)

Add two new serial tests to `standalone_isolation.rs` that form the WI-1
regression guard:

- `regression_guard_version_capture_and_isolation_invariant`: detects the
  installed Claude Code version via `claude --version`, emits it to the CI
  log, then runs the full config-assembly pipeline with HOME redirected to
  a fresh temp dir and asserts zero writes to `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json`,
  and `~/.config/claude*` (the extended path set added by WI-1).

- `regression_guard_config_write_paths_never_escape_to_home`: a focused
  negative-only variant that runs the same pipeline and checks that no
  write leaks to the real home. Kept separate so failure messages are
  precisely targeted.

Both tests call `detect_claude_version()` first: when `claude` is not on
PATH (CI without Claude Code installed), they skip with a clear log line
rather than failing — CI stays green on machines without Claude Code.

Version capture is done via `detect_claude_version()` which shells out to
`claude --version` and returns `None` on any failure (not found, non-zero
exit, empty output). The version string appears in `println!` output so it
is visible in `cargo test -- --nocapture` and in CI logs, making version
drift detectable without any persistent state file.

Design: guard lives as CI tests only (no launch-time check). A launch-time
check would block or slow attended interactive sessions; the test harness is
the correct home for a non-fatal advisory check that runs on every CI push.

The extended `assert_no_managed_driver_writes_to_home` helper adds a
`~/.config/claude*` scan on top of the existing two-path
`assert_no_real_claude_writes` check from WI-7.

Validated: 11/11 tests pass (9 WI-7 + 2 WI-1), cargo clippy clean,
cargo fmt clean, line-cap OK. Graceful-skip demonstrated via `None` path
in `detect_claude_version()` when claude is absent.

* fix(trusty-voice): correct ElevenLabs ≥1.x API + asyncio loop + audio stream close + debug-log redaction (refs #1561)

Four correctness fixes identified in code review of PR #1569:

FINDING 1 (HIGH — core TTS broken):
tts.py used the pre-1.0 elevenlabs module-level helpers (generate, set_api_key)
which are REMOVED in elevenlabs ≥1.0 (pinned ≥1.16.0).  Replaced with:
  from elevenlabs.client import AsyncElevenLabs
  client.text_to_speech.stream(voice_id=..., text=..., model_id=...,
                                output_format="pcm_22050") → AsyncIterator[bytes]
PCM chunks are now fed directly to pyaudio without a decoder (pcm_22050
output format matches the 22 050 Hz / 16-bit / mono pyaudio stream).
Added _client injection point so the speak() path is fully testable without
touching audio hardware or making network calls.

Real-SDK regression guard added in tests/test_tts.py:
  test_elevenlabs_real_sdk_import — imports AsyncElevenLabs from the ACTUAL
  installed package (no mocking) and asserts .text_to_speech.stream is callable.
  If the SDK API changes again this test fails loudly at test time, not runtime.
  test_elevenlabs_speaker_construction_uses_real_sdk — verifies _get_el_client()
  returns an AsyncElevenLabs instance.
Plus 8 new mock-based tests covering speak(), stream error recovery, close().

FINDING 2 (MEDIUM — asyncio deprecation):
pipeline.py: asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor() → asyncio.get_running_loop().
get_event_loop() is deprecated inside async functions on Python 3.10+ and can
raise DeprecationWarning / RuntimeError on 3.12+.

FINDING 3 (MEDIUM — use-after-close race):
audio.py record_blocking(): stream.stop_stream() / stream.close() were called
immediately after recording.clear() + thread.join(timeout=2.0), but a short
join timeout meant the capture thread could still be mid-stream.read() when
close() executed.  Fixed by: (a) the capture loop checks recording.is_set()
before each read, (b) close() is called strictly AFTER join() completes,
(c) timeout extended to 3.0 s (one CHUNK at 16 kHz ≈ 64 ms — generous margin).

FINDING 4 (LOW — privacy / PII):
daemon_client.py: debug log was printing the full payload dict including the
user's speech text.  Replaced with keys-only + message-length logging:
  payload_keys=[…] msg_len=N
User speech is never written to logs at any level.

Verify output: 54 passed in 0.16s, ruff check clean, ruff format clean.

* fix(trusty-mpm): correct --root/env/config precedence + panic-safe test env guard (refs #1566)

Finding 1 (precedence bug): removed `env = "TRUSTY_MPM_ROOT"` from the clap
`#[arg]` on all 6 standalone subcommands. The env attribute caused clap to
populate `root` from `TRUSTY_MPM_ROOT` at parse time, which then reached
`resolve_managed_paths(root.as_deref())` as a Some value — effectively promoting
env (tier 2) to CLI-flag (tier 1) and silently skipping the config.toml tier
whenever TRUSTY_MPM_ROOT was set. Now `root` is only Some when the user explicitly
passes `--root`, and `resolve_root` reads `TRUSTY_MPM_ROOT` explicitly at tier 2,
preserving the required precedence: flag > env > config.toml > default.

with a RAII `CleanEnvGuard` struct whose `Drop` impl restores `TRUSTY_MPM_ROOT`
and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` unconditionally — even when the test body panics — so a
failing test can no longer poison `ENV_LOCK` or leave env vars dirty for
subsequent tests.

New test `test_env_and_config_file_independent_tiers` proves the precedence is
exactly flag > env > config.toml > default: branch A confirms env wins when set;
branch B confirms config.toml is consulted when env is absent.

fix(trusty-search): restore non-empty file walk when root path contains a skip-dir name (closes #1554) (#1568)

Issue #1554: trusty-search 0.26.1 returned walk_complete total_files=0 for all
223 repos on an AL2023/g4dn host where 0.24.4 had walked 1665 files.

Root cause: the #1372 commit (3683d655) added DEFAULT_EXTRA_SKIP_DIRS
("data", "exports", "output", "reports", "snapshots", "results") and
checked them against EVERY component of the emitted absolute path — not
just the components relative to the walk root. Any repo stored under a
path containing one of those directory names (e.g. /data/repos/myproject)
had all its files pruned before they reached the indexer, producing
total_files=0 in the walk_complete SSE event.

The pre-1372 code (0.24.4) only had the hardcoded SKIP_DIRS list
(target, node_modules, .git, etc.) which never appear as host-level
mount-point names. The new "data" entry in extra_skip_dirs is a standard
Linux filesystem path component / EBS mount point name, so it silently
zeroed out entire deployments.

Fix: strip the canonical root prefix before checking path components
against SKIP_DIRS and extra_skip_dirs so only relative path segments
(those UNDER the root) are evaluated. A data/ subdir WITHIN a project
is still correctly pruned; the root path prefix is never matched.

Regression test: test_walk_root_containing_skip_dir_name_still_indexes_files
creates a project at <tmp>/data/repos/myproject, walks from the project
root, and asserts the walk finds files. It also asserts that a data/
SUBDIR *within* the project is still pruned.

fix(trusty-mpm): atomic confirm_pair_code with crash-safe claim cleanup (closes #1506) (#1547)

* Fix atomic read-then-delete in confirm_pair_code (#1506)

* fix(trusty-mpm): harden atomic pairing claim — unique temp name + startup stale-claim cleanup + stronger tests (closes #1506)

Builds on @aniruthramidi's rename-based atomic claim from #1507. The
contributor's core approach (OS rename as cross-process lock) is correct
and preserved unchanged.

Hardening added in this commit:

1. Unique claim temp name: replace `.claim.<pid>` with
   `.claim.<pid>.<nanos>.<uuid-prefix>` so a PID-reuse collision (new
   process reusing the PID of a previous crashed one) cannot accidentally
   "win" an outstanding claim against a stale orphan file.

2. Startup stale-claim cleanup: add `cleanup_stale_claims(root)` which
   removes orphan `pending_pair.json.claim.*` files older than 60 s left
   by a process that crashed between the rename and the delete. Wire it
   into `DaemonState::new()` and `DaemonState::with_paths()` so every
   daemon startup reclaims the pairing surface after a crash without
   operator intervention.

3. Stronger concurrent test: the existing `concurrent_pairing_confirms`
   test now uses `Arc<DaemonState>` so each thread has full ownership;
   asserts not only that exactly one confirm wins (the original XOR
   assertion) but also that the WINNER has its `chat_id` stored in state
   and the LOSER does not, and that the shared pending code file is
   absent after a winning confirm.

4. New stale-claim tests: four deterministic tests for
   `cleanup_stale_claims` cover fresh-file preservation, unrelated-file
   safety, no-op on a missing root, and orphan-with-known-mtime
   detection.

* fix(trusty-mpm): restore-on-failure in claim_pending, safe cleanup default, real stale-removal test (refs #1506)

Finding 1 (MEDIUM): claim_pending previously deleted the temp file before
checking the read/parse result, permanently losing the pending code on any
transient I/O error or malformed file. Now: read succeeds → parse succeeds
→ remove temp and return Some; read fails → rename temp back to pending_pair.json
(best-effort restore) and return None; parse fails → same restore+None. The
winning-process atomicity guarantee is unchanged.

Finding 2 (LOW): claim_path used d.subsec_nanos() (sub-second component only),
which wraps at 1 second and loses monotonicity. Changed to d.as_nanos() for a
total nanosecond count monotonic across second boundaries.

failures, treating files with unreadable metadata as stale and deleting them —
racing against live claims. Changed to .unwrap_or(false): if age is
undeterminable, conservatively keep the file. Updated inline comment to explain
the conservative choice.

Finding 4 (MEDIUM): the only stale-removal test admitted it couldn't backdate
mtime and only re-checked the fresh-preserve case, leaving the remove_file branch
at zero coverage. Introduced cleanup_stale_claims_with_threshold(root, max_age)
containing the full scan logic; cleanup_stale_claims now delegates to it with the

passes Duration::ZERO so every file is "stale", directly exercises remove_file.

* fix(trusty-search): make publish.sh monorepo- and redb2-aware (closes #1539)

The old publish.sh was written for the pre-monorepo multi-repo layout and
was broken in five ways:
  - cloned trusty-common from a standalone repo (/tmp/trusty-common-publish)
    that no longer exists;
  - stripped a [patch."https://github.com/bobmatnyc/trusty-common"] block,
    but the monorepo uses [patch.crates-io];
  - edited crates/trusty-search/Cargo.toml instead of the workspace-root
    Cargo.toml where the patch table actually lives;
  - computed WORKSPACE_ROOT as the crate dir, not the repo root;
  - had no awareness of the redb2 alias (redb 2.6 alongside redb 4 for the
    migrate-redb subcommand).

Rewrite (Option A) to the real monorepo flow:
  - compute repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`;
  - drop the obsolete trusty-common clone entirely;
  - strip the [patch.crates-io] block (both the in-tree path patches AND any
    future redb/redb2 entries) from the WORKSPACE-ROOT Cargo.toml before
    `cargo publish -p trusty-search`, then restore it;
  - trap-based restore of BOTH Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock on ANY exit
    (success, failure, Ctrl-C) so the workspace is never left mutated;
  - add a `--dry-run` mode that needs no crates.io token, plus `--help`;
  - `--allow-dirty` (transient strip) and no `--locked` (the strip
    legitimately re-resolves in-tree libs from the registry).

redb2 itself is a plain `package = "redb"` rename pinned to 2.6 and resolves
from crates.io directly — no patch entry needed.

Verified: `bash crates/trusty-search/publish.sh --dry-run` packages + verifies
trusty-search 0.26.1 (redb/redb2/trusty-common all resolve from crates.io) and
restores the root Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock; `git status` shows only publish.sh.

* fix(trusty-search): harden publish.sh patch-strip regex + lock/usage robustness (refs #1539)

Address code-review findings on PR #1544:

- Finding 1 (regex): the patch-strip prefix `(?:^#.*\n)*` only allowed comment
  lines before `[patch.crates-io]`, so a blank line between the comment banner
  and the header (a common Cargo.toml layout) broke the match and left the
  block in place — `cargo publish` then failed or tried to publish a
  path-patched manifest. Widen the prefix to `(?:^(?:#.*)?\n)*` (comment OR
  blank). Also add a FAIL-LOUD guard: if the header is present but the strip
  matched nothing (n==0), exit non-zero instead of warning-and-continuing, so a
  silent no-strip can never let a publish proceed.

- Finding 2 (Cargo.lock): track whether Cargo.lock existed before the run. If it
  did NOT exist but `cargo publish` created one during resolution, the EXIT trap
  now removes it, leaving the worktree exactly as found (previously a stray
  untracked lockfile could remain).

- Finding 3 (usage): replace the fragile `sed -n '2,40p'` header slice — which
  would leak raw bash if the header grew — with a self-contained heredoc.

Verified: bash -n OK; dry-run drives `cargo publish -p trusty-search --dry-run`
to success with redb/redb2 resolved from crates.io and exit 0; git status clean
afterward (root Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock restored, no leftovers); line-cap OK.

fix(trusty-agents): split camelCase in context indexer tokenizer for BM25 recall (closes #1542) (#1545)

The context indexer's `tokenize()` only lowercased and split on non-alphanumeric
characters, so `getUserProfile` was indexed as the single opaque token
`getuserprofile`. A BM25 query for `get user` or `user profile` would therefore
miss the document entirely.

Add `split_camel_case_indexer()` (private helper mirroring the algorithm in
`trusty_common::bm25`) and integrate it into `tokenize()`: for each
alphanumeric run, emit both the raw lowercased token *and* any camelCase /
PascalCase sub-parts that are longer than 2 chars. Tokens are deduplicated and
sorted before returning so the BM25 term list is stable.

The existing short-token filter (`len > 2`) is preserved on all emission paths,
so the `tokenize_lowers_and_drops_short` test continues to pass unchanged.

New test `tokenize_splits_camel_case` asserts:
- raw token `getuserprofile` is still emitted (exact-identifier match wins)
- sub-parts `get`, `user`, `profile` are also emitted
- no token of ≤ 2 chars leaks through
- PascalCase (`GetUserProfile`) splits identically

  writable handle is still open on Linux.
- `spawn_script`: constructs a fresh `tokio::process::Command` per attempt
  (Command is not Clone) and retries up to 3 times with 5 ms exponential
  back-off on `ErrorKind::ExecutableFileBusy` as belt-and-suspenders.

fix(trusty-mpm): stop dropping tokio Runtime in async test context (closes #1521) (#1522)

`reqwest::blocking::Client::builder().build()` internally creates its own
`tokio::Runtime`. When `LlmOverseer::new()` was called from `DaemonState::new()`
(which was called from `DaemonState::shared()` in every `#[tokio::test]`), this
construction happened inside the test's ambient tokio runtime, causing a panic:

    Cannot drop a runtime in a context where blocking is not allowed.
    This happens when a runtime is dropped from within an asynchronous context.

Fix: change `LlmOverseer.client` from an eagerly-built `reqwest::blocking::Client`
to a `std::sync::OnceLock<reqwest::blocking::Client>` initialised lazily on the
first call to `evaluate()`. The `evaluate()` method is always invoked from a
synchronous, non-async context via the `Overseer` trait (sync methods), so the
blocking client is never constructed inside an async runtime in normal operation
or in tests. The async `chat_client` is unaffected — it is still built eagerly
as it has no restrictions on async context construction.

fix(trusty-mpm): HTML-escape Telegram command replies (closes #1514) (#1515)

* fix(trusty-mpm): HTML-escape Telegram command replies under ParseMode::Html (closes #1514)

Root cause: `TelegramFormatter::format` returned `text.clone()` for
`CommandResult::Help`, passing the raw `help_text()` string — which contains
lines like `/status <id> — Session status` — directly to teloxide with
`ParseMode::Html`. Telegram rejects `<id>` as an unsupported HTML start tag
and silently drops the update.

Fix: change the `CommandResult::Help` arm to `html_escape(text)` so `<`, `>`,
and `&` in the help body are escaped to their HTML entities before sending.
This is consistent with every other arm that interpolates dynamic/user-sourced
content (snapshots, managed session names, doctor reports, etc.), all of which
already call `html_escape`.

Intentional structural tags (`<b>`, `<code>`, `<pre>`) written literally by
other arms are unaffected — only `Help` text is escaped, and Help text
contains no intentional HTML.

Tests added in `telegram/formatter/tests.rs`:
- `help_escapes_angle_bracket_placeholders` — verifies `<id>` → `<id>`
- `intentional_html_tags_are_preserved_in_other_variants` — verifies `<b>`
  tags in Sessions output are NOT double-escaped

* fix(trusty-mpm): supervise Telegram bot + share pairing-code store (#1499, #1500)

#1499 — daemon's internal Telegram bot died silently on a startup port/long-poll
conflict (e.g. a 409 from a duplicate getUpdates consumer): the bare
`tokio::spawn` body logged once and ended, leaving the Telegram surface dark
until a full daemon restart. Add `telegram::supervisor` — a restart-on-exit
supervisor with bounded exponential backoff (500ms→…→30s cap), per-restart and
give-up logging, transient-vs-permanent error classification (a permanent
misconfiguration backs off to the cap and gives up after a small budget instead
of tight-looping), and cancellation-safety (a `CancellationToken` ends the loop
and interrupts an in-flight backoff so it never blocks graceful shutdown).
`telegram::run_supervised` adapts `run()` into the supervisor; `daemon_run.rs`
spawns it and cancels it from the shutdown handler.

#1500 — the live pairing CODE lived only in the daemon's in-memory `pair_code`
mutex, so a code minted on one daemon instance (e.g. the silent ephemeral-port
duplicate from #1499) was rejected as "invalid/expired" when confirmed against
another instance's empty store — the reason operators pre-seeded pairing.json.
Persist the pending code+issue-time to a single canonical
`<framework_root>/pending_pair.json` (`PendingPairCode`, save/load/clear with a
process-portable epoch-ms TTL). `generate_pair_code` writes it; `confirm_pair_code`
validates against the shared store (memory fallback) and consumes it from both;
`clear_pairing` drops it too. Codes minted by any surface rooted at the same
framework root now validate against one source of truth — no pre-seed needed.

Tests: supervisor restart-after-transient, exponential growth + cap, give-up at
the permanent budget, transient-resets-permanent-counter, pre-cancel no-op, and
backoff-sleep cancellation; pairing pending-store round-trip / expiry / clear and
the cross-instance `pairing_confirms_shared_disk_code` regression guard. fmt,

* fix(trusty-mpm): add Origin guard to action-capable chat endpoint for web surface CSRF (review #1503)

The new GET /web browser surface drives the state-mutating, action-capable
POST /api/v1/sessions/chat (actions:true), which can spawn/stop/mutate
managed sessions. Without an origin check a malicious cross-origin page could
trigger session actions if the daemon is reachable from a browser on a
non-loopback interface.

Add a lightweight, testable Origin guard (origin_guard::origin_allowed):
- No Origin header -> allowed. Server-side callers (Telegram/TUI via reqwest
  on localhost, curl) send no Origin, so all current behavior is preserved.
- Loopback Origin (127.0.0.1 / localhost / ::1, any port) -> allowed.
- Same-origin (Origin authority matches request Host) -> allowed.
- Any other (cross-origin) Origin, opaque "null", or present-Origin-without-
  Host -> rejected with 403.

The guard is applied ONLY to the actions:true path, so read-only/text-only
and non-browser actions:false callers are untouched. Adds a DaemonError::
Forbidden variant (maps to 403). Documents the threat model on the /web
route handler (daemon binds loopback by default; the Origin guard is the
CSRF mitigation for the browser surface).

(allowed) and cross-origin/null/no-Host (rejected); error_status_codes_map
covers the new 403 mapping. The pre-existing SM handler tests that build a

test env regardless of this change and are out of scope.

fix(trusty-memory): open daemon palace redb as Writer — fail-loud, no silent read-only (closes #1487) (#1488)

* fix(trusty-memory): open daemon palace redb as Writer (fail-loud, no silent read-only) (closes #1487)

The HTTP daemon is the sole palace writer but opened palace redb files with
`OpenIntent::ReadOnlyClient`, so a second instance opening the same store
silently fell back to `OpenMode::Snapshot` (read-only) and rejected every
write for its lifetime — effectively silent data loss when an MCP client
routed `memory_remember` to the rogue listener.

Fix: thread an `OpenIntent` parameter through the open chain
(`KgStoreRedb::open_with_intent`, `UsearchStore::new_with_intent`,
`KnowledgeGraph::open_with_intent`, `PalaceHandle::open_with_intent`,
`PalaceRegistry::with_writer_intent`). Existing zero-arg `open`/`new`
signatures default to `ReadOnlyClient`, preserving the issue-#59 snapshot
read-fallback for CLI / stdio-proxy / test callers. The HTTP-daemon path
(`run_serve` → `AppState::with_writer_intent`) passes `Writer`, so a second
live daemon fails loud (Err / non-zero exit) instead of degrading.

Restart-handoff: a naive fail-loud would flap launchd during a graceful
`bootout`→`bootstrap` overlap (the old daemon may still hold the flock for a
few hundred ms). The Writer path now retries `Database::create` with bounded
exponential backoff (`WRITER_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=5`, `WRITER_RETRY_SLEEP_MS`
=50/100/400/1000, ~1.55s total) inside `try_open_or_snapshot`, and only then
fails loud with an actionable error naming the conflict — never degrading to
snapshot mode. The per-store TOCTOU loops pass a single attempt for `Writer`
so the window is not multiplied.

stdio proxy (#1152) and CLI/read paths are unchanged (still `ReadOnlyClient`
/ pure proxy). No advisory data-dir flock added (fix option c left for a
follow-up).

- concurrent_open: writer_intent_fails_on_locked_file (persistent conflict

fix(trusty-search): surface silent reindex failures with logged cause (closes #1428) (#1449)

* fix(trusty-search): surface silent reindex failure + capture producer-task panic (closes #1428)

A full reindex of a large corpus could end in status=error with duration=None
and NO error logged by the daemon. Root cause of the *silent* symptom: the
reindex pipeline had three error/early-exit paths that set status=Failed (or
left the run incomplete) without ever logging the underlying cause to stderr:

1. ReindexTerminationGuard::drop (guard.rs) — fired on any panic/cancellation
   of the runner future, set status=Failed and broadcast a *generic* SSE error,
   but logged nothing to stderr and carried no real cause.
2. The parse/embed producer task's JoinHandle result was discarded
   (`let _ = producer.await`), so a panic inside parse/embed (e.g. an embedder
   fault under GPU OOM / sidecar stall) unwound silently and the consumer loop
   fell through to a "successful" finish.
3. emit_batch_error (batch.rs) surfaced a failed batch ONLY as an SSE frame —
   a GPU-OOM Err from embed_batch never reached the daemon log.

Hardening (in-scope to trusty-search; the actual ~1665-chunk halt is a CUDA
BFCArena VRAM-pressure stall whose mitigations — #600 gpu_mem_limit bounding,
#763 CUDA-hang fix, #907 30s call timeout — already shipped in 0.24.4):

- guard.rs: Drop now ALWAYS logs at error! to stderr (issue #1428), stamps the
  index id, and surfaces a captured failure reason via a shared FailureReasonSlot
  instead of a fixed generic string. SSE frame now carries index_id + fatal:true.
- runner.rs: capture the producer JoinError — log panic/cancellation at error!
  and record the cause in the guard's failure slot. Added RUST_LOG=debug tracing
  around batch flush (producer) and commit (consumer) to pinpoint a mid-run halt.
- batch.rs: emit_batch_error now logs the anyhow cause chain at error! to stderr.

Tests: 3 guard tests (captured reason, fatal-by-default fallback, index-id in
frame); full suite green (932 lib + integration). clippy/fmt/line-cap clean.

Add the runtime execution layer: an in-process AgentRunner that the PM's
delegate_to_agent tool dispatches to. For each call it loads the sub-agent's

the model and assembled system prompt (BASE preamble + agent prompt + project
context), drives the multi-turn AgentLoop to completion, and returns the
sub-agent's AgentOutput — including accrued token usage — back to the PM on the

  the DI seam, so #1030's orchestrator wires it via DelegateToAgentTool::new).

  how each sub-agent's tools are assembled; the runner owns allowlist gating.
- ToolRegistry::gated(allowed) narrows a registry to an agent's tools.allowed —
  the AgentLoop dispatches with no per-call allowlist, so gating happens before
  the loop runs by handing it a registry that omits denied tools.
- RunnerKind::InProcess is now the real default backend; SubProcess/ClaudeCode
  retained as future variants.
- RunnerError (thiserror): UnknownAgent / ConfigLoad / Loop. No unwrap() in lib.

engineer's own loop on its own slug and returns AgentOutput to the PM;

  Error: GitError ... "could not find repository at

  stat: cannot statx 'RELEASE_NOTES.md': No such file or directory

→ RELEASE_NOTES.md was never written and the GitHub Release was never created,

tag-range walking. Ordering is now: checkout → download artifacts →

fix(trusty-review): reconcile structured verdict/grade with review_body, ignore refuted/low-confidence findings (closes #1343) (#1350)

The structured `verdict`/`grade` returned by `review_pr`/`review_diff` could
systematically contradict the model's own `review_body` JSON verdict/grade and
harden to REQUEST_CHANGES/D+ even as the reviewed code improved.

Root cause: `derive_verdict`/`severity_floor` (pipeline/grade.rs) applied a
count-based severity FLOOR as `max(model_proposed, floor)`. The floor could only
escalate, so a model APPROVE/B+ was overridden to REQUEST_CHANGES whenever the
raw findings looked severe by count — and it fed ALL findings into the floor,
including verifier-refuted findings (demoted to confidence 0.10) and raw
`confidence:0.1` speculation. `clamp_grade_to_verdict` then dropped B+ to D+.

Fix (pipeline/grade.rs):
- Exclude non-substantive findings from ALL floor logic via `is_substantive`:
  any refutation variant (Refuted/ErrorRefuted/TruncationRefuted) or
  confidence < 0.50 (FLOOR_COUNT_MIN_CONFIDENCE) is noise, never evidence.
- Source-of-truth reconciliation: when the model's own verdict is a clean
  APPROVE, a count-based REQUEST_CHANGES floor (>=2 Medium findings) is capped at
  APPROVE* — it must not contradict an APPROVE review_body. A High-effort
  (critical) finding is exempt and still floors to BLOCK (grounded evidence).
- Grade stays consistent with the reconciled verdict (no spurious B+ -> D+).

Regression tests (grade_tests.rs) model the PR #1342 evidence shape (APPROVE/B+
inner verdict with refuted + confidence:0.1 findings) and assert the structured
output does not surface REQUEST_CHANGES/D+, while a genuine REQUEST_CHANGES
review_body and a substantive High finding still escalate correctly.

fix(trusty-search): resolve dashboard API base to daemon origin, not /ui/ baseURI (closes #1329) (#1336)

The dashboard SPA is mounted at the daemon's `/ui/` route while the JSON API
endpoints (/health, /indexes, search, SSE) are siblings at the daemon ROOT,
one level above `ui/`. computeBase() in ui/src/lib/base.js (from PR #996)
derived the API base straight from document.baseURI, which at `…/ui/` is the
`/ui/` directory itself — so `/health` resolved to `…/ui/health`, which the
daemon answers with the SPA index.html (text/html) instead of JSON. That
produced the offline badge + empty index list reported in #1329.

Fix: strip a trailing `ui/` path segment (in addition to the existing
`index.html` strip) so the base points at the API root that is the parent of
the SPA mount. This preserves PR #996's reverse-proxy intent: the trusty-console
proxy mounts `/proxy/{daemon}/{*path}` and forwards `{*path}` verbatim to the
daemon root, so a SPA opened at `<prefix>/ui/` collapses to API base `<prefix>/`
and `/health` reaches `<prefix>/health`. Both direct and proxied cases obey one
rule: API base = document.baseURI with its trailing `ui/` segment removed
(confirmed against crates/trusty-search/src/service/server/mod.rs and
crates/trusty-console/src/proxy/routes.rs).

Sibling dashboards synced (KEEP IN SYNC contract): trusty-analyze has the
same `/ui/` mount and the same bug — fixed identically. trusty-memory serves
its SPA at the ROOT via a fallback handler (API under /api/v1 and /health), so
it does NOT have this bug; the `ui/` strip is a harmless no-op there but is
applied for symmetry and documented as such.

Regression test: added a JS unit test harness (vitest + jsdom) to the search UI
and crates/trusty-search/ui/src/lib/base.test.js, asserting that at `…/ui/` the
computed URLs for /health and /indexes are `<origin>/health` / `<origin>/indexes`
(no `/ui/` segment), that the bare `/` case is unchanged, and that the proxy case
`<prefix>/ui/` yields `<prefix>/health`. 6 tests pass.

Bundles rebuilt: all three shipped artifacts regenerated so the fix actually
ships — crates/trusty-search/ui-dist/ (via `make release-prep`),
crates/trusty-analyze/ui/dist/ and crates/trusty-memory/ui/dist/ (vite build).
Each rebuilt index-*.js now contains the `.replace(/(^|\/)ui\/$/,"$1")` strip;
only the JS asset hash changed (CSS unchanged), confirming a logic-only diff.

fix(ci): skip binary-release workflow gracefully for library-only crate tags (#1335)

The Binary Release workflow fires on every `<crate>-v<version>` tag. Its
`setup.config` step had an explicit binary-crate table, a two-crate
green-skip branch (trusty-bm25-daemon, trusty-embedderd), and a fatal
`else → exit 1` for everything else. As a result, pushing a tag for a
library-only crate that publishes to crates.io but produces NO standalone
binary (e.g. `trusty-common-v0.15.3`) turned the whole release run RED even
though there was simply nothing to build or upload.

Invert the default: treat the binary-crate branches as a strict ALLOWLIST
and default every other crate to a graceful green-skip (emit bundled=true,
exit 0) instead of erroring. This subsumes the old two-crate special case
and makes new library crates "just work" — they green-skip with no workflow
edit. The build / release / homebrew-bump jobs are already guarded on
`bundled != 'true'`, so they skip cleanly.

Library-only crates that now green-skip include: trusty-common,
trusty-bm25-daemon, trusty-embedderd (sidecar binaries shipped inside their
host crate per #1318), trusty-progress, the internal trusty-agents* libs,
and any future library-only workspace crate.

Caveat documented inline: because the default is skip, a NEW binary-producing
crate also green-skips until an explicit config branch is added. Notably
`trusty-controller` (bin `tctl`, #1316) is a real binary crate with no config
branch yet, so its tags currently green-skip — flagged in a comment so it is
wired into the allowlist before tctl releases are relied upon.

YAML validated with `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"`.

fix(trusty-search): cursor-based deep pagination + timeout relief for get_chunks (closes #1325) (#1331)

* fix(trusty-search): cursor-based deep pagination + timeout relief for get_chunks (closes #1325)

Deep offset pagination on GET /indexes/{id}/chunks (e.g. offset=304000 on a
300k-chunk index) timed out and surfaced as a 502 Bad Gateway after ~120s. The
offset path materialized the entire corpus and re-sorted it on every page
request (O(N log N) per page), so bulk enumeration (trusty-analyze PR-review
context) could never complete. Chat/search were unaffected.

Root cause: CodeIndexer::enumerate_chunks loads all chunks from the in-memory
map (rehydrating the whole corpus from redb after idle eviction) and sorts the
full collection per call, then slices [offset..end].

Fix (cursor-based pagination — the structural fix):
- CorpusStore::chunks_after(after, limit): indexed redb B-tree seek over the
  chunk_id-keyed CHUNKS_TABLE via range(Excluded(after)..). O(log N) seek +
  O(page) read instead of O(offset) scan.
- CodeIndexer::enumerate_chunks_after: durable path uses the seek; BM25-only /
  test indexers fall back to an id-ordered in-memory page with the same cursor
  semantics. Returns (total, page, next_cursor).
- GET /indexes/{id}/chunks gains an additive, non-breaking `after` query param
  (empty = from first chunk) and returns `next_cursor`. Legacy offset/limit is
  unchanged (next_cursor always null — offset and cursor use different stable
  orderings, so a cursor walk must not be seeded from an offset page).
- list_chunks MCP tool gains a matching `after` arg (URL-encoded via reqwest
  .query through a new McpServer::get_query helper).

Timeout relief: the cursor path makes each page O(page) regardless of depth, so
legacy 502s no longer occur; the chunks route stays on the unbounded bulk lane
(no 30s interactive deadline that would cut off a legitimate large page).

Tests: corpus chunks_after seek/paging; indexer cursor paging over both redb
and in-memory fallback; server endpoint cursor full-coverage, offset back-compat
+ next_cursor=null, and 404. Version bump 0.24.7 -> 0.24.8 + CHANGELOG.

docs(spec): record harness-agnostic design principles — canonical-context preservation + no-drop-in-required (#1320) (#1323)

Add section 3.3 to SESSION_MANAGER_MVP.md documenting three core principles for
pluggable harness support:

1. **Canonical-Context Preservation**: MPM assembles instructions once; each harness
   implementation projects that context into its native format. Agents, skills, and
   configuration have one source of truth.

2. **No-Drop-In-Required**: Users never need to drop into a harness UI to make progress.
   All observation and control happen through MPM interfaces (CLI, TUI, HTTP, chat).
   Harness attachment is optional, not required.

3. **Transport-Agnostic Core**: session_manager, runtime, activity, and provisioner
   modules contain no HTTP/CLI/tmux-specific logic. They're reusable across any transport.

This forward-looking spec establishes the design contract for adding trusty-code and
future harness implementations without architectural rework.

feat(trusty-mpm): SM-8 SM↔session delegation loop with verification gate + prohibition enforcement (#1292) (#1311)

* feat(trusty-mpm): SM-8 SM<->session delegation loop with verification gate + prohibition enforcement (#1292)

Implements the SM-8 capstone (DOC-14 §3.4): the 6-phase SM↔session delegation
loop (intake → decompose → launch → observe → verify → report+persist) that
brings the Session Manager to life. SM-1..SM-7 + SM-STDIO built the parts; this
wires them into the prime directive (§3.1): the SM does NO work itself — every
unit of real work becomes a launched t-mpm session it observes and verifies.

Decision protocol: the SM provider is text-only (`complete()`, no tool-calling),
so the loop uses a structured-text (ReAct-style) protocol — the SM emits ONE JSON
action block at DECOMPOSE which `parse_decision` turns into a typed `SmDecision`;
the engine then mechanically executes launch→observe→verify. Observation and
evidence interpretation are deterministic pane heuristics (no LLM), per §3.4.

- Relocate the `SessionControl` trait + `LaunchParams`/`SessionControlError` to a
  shared `core::sm::control` so the agent-side loop can depend on it; `sm_stdio`
  re-exports them unchanged and keeps the production `DaemonSessionControl`.
- Add `agent::delegate` (split under the 500-SLOC cap): `decision` (action
  protocol + lenient JSON parser), `observe` (pane interpretation + evidence
  scanner), `verify` (the SP redirect), and `mod` (the orchestrator
  `delegate_goal`).
- Verification gate (§3.5, BLOCKING): a link reaches `Verified` ONLY with observed
  evidence (PR URL / test-pass output / diff); the goal closes only when SM-6's
  gate confirms every linked task is Verified.
- Prohibitions (§3.2 SP1–SP7): enforced structurally (the loop has only
  session-control + goals + memory — no edit/read/build/test tools) plus a guard
  that refuses + redirects a direct-work `do_work` decision to "launch a session".
- Task delivery (#1299): after launch the loop `sessions.send`s the task prompt to
  the spawned session so it isn't left idle.
- Reachable over SM-STDIO via a new `sm.delegate` method (the §1A.2 step-1 flow),
  feature-gated like `sm.goals.*`.
- Concurrency (#1309): goal-store mutations stay atomic/serialized; the loop adds
  no new last-write-wins race and leaves a TODO(#1309) per-goal seam.

Tests (hermetic — mock provider + mock SessionControl + in-memory goal store, no
network/spawn/ONNX): decision-parser variants, deterministic observe/evidence,
launch+link, task delivery, observe→progress, the gate (blocks without evidence,
closes with), the prohibition redirect, multi-session fan-out, degraded mode, and
an end-to-end `sm.delegate` over the dispatcher (launch→observe→verify→close).

* fix(trusty-mpm): SM-5 review — convergent compaction, recompute estimate on load, unique temp file, single system message (#1288)

Address four medium advisory findings from the trusty-review APPROVE pass on
PR #1306 (SM-5, issue #1288):

1. Compaction non-convergence for a single oversized round: the eviction loop
   keeps >=1 verbatim round, so a lone over-budget round left should_compact()
   true with no further re-summarisation. Add a bounded post-loop convergence
   pass (converge_within_budget) that re-summarises the compressed block and
   folds the lone retained round into it until within budget or no further
   reduction is possible, with a no-progress guard to guarantee termination.

2. token_estimate stale on load: SmContextEngine::open now recomputes the
   estimate from loaded content so a stale/heuristic-drifted on-disk cache can
   never trigger a spurious compaction on the first record.

3. Temp-file PID uniquifier collision: the atomic-write temp name is now unique
   per call (pid + wall-clock nanos + a process monotonic counter), so two
   concurrent saves for the same conv_id cannot share a temp path. No new deps.

4. Multiple system-role messages: assemble_working_prompt now consolidates the
   base system prompt, compressed-context block, and memory-recall block into a
   single system message (in §7.5 order, each omitted if empty), so providers
   that reject >1 system message accept the prompt.

New/updated tests: single_oversized_round_converges_within_budget,
convergence_terminates_when_summariser_cannot_shrink,
open_recomputes_stale_token_estimate,
loaded_stale_estimate_does_not_spuriously_compact,
concurrent_saves_use_distinct_temp_paths,
concurrent_saves_same_conv_id_do_not_corrupt,
assembly_emits_single_system_message, and assembly_order_is_exact updated to

(/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin) that omits Homebrew (/opt/homebrew/bin → tmux)
and ~/.local/bin (claude). Managed-session spawns therefore 500'd before

      (idempotent; an explicit caller PATH wins).
    - deploy/supervisor/com.trusty.mpm.supervisor.plist + README now ship a full
      PATH covering Homebrew, ~/.local/bin, ~/.cargo/bin, and system dirs.

(b) Defense-in-depth runtime resolution:
    - TmuxDriver::discover() resolves tmux via bin_resolve::resolve_binary
      (live PATH first, then well-known dirs) instead of bare `which tmux`.
    - ClaudeCodeAdapter resolves claude to an ABSOLUTE path and sends that to the
      tmux pane, so the pane (which inherits the daemon's minimal PATH) launches
      claude regardless of its own PATH.

resolver fallback + absolute-path), launchd with_daemon_path_seeds_full_path /
preserves_explicit_path, claude_code spawn_command_uses_resolved_binary.

schema's findings.items object omitted both, so OpenAI rejected the request and
