VerifyJudgment) already use #[serde(default)] on the now-always-emitted fields,
so both lenient (Bedrock/Anthropic, Gemini) and strict (OpenAI) responses

fix(trusty-mpm): reload-on-read so daemon reflects supervisor's out-of-process session writes (closes #1219) (#1227)

* fix(trusty-mpm): reload-on-read so daemon reflects supervisor's out-of-process writes (closes #1219)

The `tm supervisor` process and the `trusty-mpm` daemon each own an
independent `SessionManager` over the same on-disk `sessions.json`. The
daemon loads its store once (via OnceCell) and never re-reads the file, so a
state transition written by the supervisor (e.g. auto-resume flipping
`stopped` -> `active`) was never observed: `GET /sessions/managed/{id}`
served stale state indefinitely.

Fix (Option A — mtime/len-aware reload-on-read; the file stays the single
source of truth, no coupling between the two processes):

- SessionStore tracks a (mtime, len) freshness fingerprint of the backing
  file. `reload_if_changed` re-reads from disk when the fingerprint moves;
  a matching fingerprint is a one-stat no-op.
- `get`/`all` reload-on-read before answering, so cross-process writes are
  reflected within one read.
- `upsert`/`remove` reload-before-write so a single-record mutation is
  applied on top of the freshest disk state and never clobbers a concurrent
  out-of-process write to a different record.
- `save` is now atomic (temp file + rename) so a cross-process reader never
  observes a torn, unparseable file.

Manager `get`/`list` upgrade from a read lock to a write lock since the
reload mutates the in-memory map; their public signatures are unchanged.

Tests:
- session_manager::tests::manager_get_reflects_out_of_process_write — two
  managers over one data dir; a resume via manager B (the supervisor) is
  observed by manager A's (the daemon's) `get`/`list`.
- store::tests::store_reload_picks_up_external_write,
  store_reload_noop_when_unchanged, store_upsert_preserves_concurrent_write.

  reload-on-read fails. A transient I/O error (e.g. NFS hiccup, momentarily
  unreadable/corrupt file) previously made GET /api/v1/sessions/managed
  report ZERO sessions despite the comment claiming "last-known set",

feat(trusty-memory): derive default palace ID from project identity (#1217) (#1224)

The default palace ID was derived from the bare directory basename, so two
checkouts/worktrees of the same repo under different names produced unrelated
palaces and a GitHub project was not addressable by its `owner/repo` slug.

Introduce a pure, fully unit-tested derivation core (`palace_id_derive`) with
the precedence **override > pin file > git owner/repo > parent/dir**, and wire
it into the default-palace resolution path (`cwd_palace_slug_at`).

Derivation core (`palace_id_derive.rs`, pure — no FS/git/env I/O):
- `owner_repo_from_git_remote`: parses SSH (`git@github.com:owner/repo.git`)
  and HTTPS (`https://github.com/owner/repo(.git)`) forms, non-GitHub hosts,
  nested groups, trailing slashes, `.git` suffix, owner-less paths.
- `parent_dir_slug`: last two path components joined (`Projects/trusty-tools`
  → `projects-trusty-tools`).
- `derive_palace_id`: applies the precedence; returns `None` only when every
  source is exhausted.
- `owner/repo` and `parent/dir` collapse the separator to `-` for storage
  safety (a palace ID is also a dir name and a Unix-socket filename).

Override mechanism: `TRUSTY_MEMORY_PALACE` env var (slugified) — the
"specifyable" default override; documented in the env-var reference. Per-command
`--palace` flags still win at their call sites.

Backward compatibility: a committed `.trusty-tools/trusty-memory.yaml` pin file
always wins over the new git/dir derivation (new `pinned_slug_at` helper returns
`Some` strictly when a pin exists, never the basename). The new derivation
applies only when no pin exists, so existing palaces are never orphaned.

* fix(trusty-mpm): isolate prepare_session tests from shared ~/.claude/agents race

The 6 session_launch unit tests that called prepare_session() with
FrameworkPaths::default() shared the real ~/.claude/agents and
~/.claude/skills directories at runtime. Under parallel test execution,
atomic_write() uses a single .tmp sidecar name per target path, so two
concurrent manifest writes to the same ~/.claude/agents/manifest.json.tmp

would fail with ENOENT ("No such file or directory").

FrameworkPaths::under(tmp_home.path()) instead of ::default(). This routes
claude_agents_dir and claude_skills_dir into per-test temp directories,
eliminating the shared-path race entirely without requiring --test-threads=1.

fix(trusty-memory): LRU palace-handle cache + health sentinel hardening + doc fixes (#1198)

* feat(trusty-memory): LRU palace-handle cache (closes #463)

Replace the unbounded DashMap in PalaceRegistry with an
LruCache<PalaceId, Arc<PalaceHandle>> bounded by DEFAULT_MAX_OPEN_PALACES
(64). Each open palace holds ~3 redb file descriptors; with many palaces the
daemon could exhaust the OS fd limit (EMFILE). The LRU strategy closes handles
for idle palaces automatically so the resident fd count stays bounded
regardless of palace count.

Changes:
- Add `dep:lru` to the `memory-core` feature in trusty-common/Cargo.toml
- Replace `Arc<DashMap<PalaceId, Arc<PalaceHandle>>>` with
  `Arc<Mutex<LruCache<PalaceId, Arc<PalaceHandle>>>>` in PalaceRegistry
- Add `PalaceRegistry::with_max_open(n)` constructor and
  `DEFAULT_MAX_OPEN_PALACES = 64` constant
- Add `register_arc`, `peek`, `remove` helpers; update `register`/`get`/`list`
  to use LruCache semantics
- Evicted handles drop outside the lock so redb close() never runs under Mutex
- Add four regression tests:
  `lru_evicts_least_recently_used`, `lru_get_promotes_to_mru`,
  `lru_evicted_handle_reopens`, `registry_remove_clears_cached_handle`

fix(trusty-console): release outer state lock before tools/list I/O in ensure_connected (closes #1164) (#1187)

The tools/list probe added in PR #1161 called list_tools().await while still
holding the outer Mutex<(Option<HandleState>, SpawnBackoff)>, blocking any
concurrent poll_metrics / route handler for the full network round-trip.

Fix: mirror the existing call_tool lock discipline. After a successful
initialize, wrap the client in Arc<Mutex<>> (so it outlives the outer guard),
drop the outer guard, call list_tools().await on the inner arc, then
re-acquire the outer guard to record the Connected/Degraded outcome.
Structured via a phase-1 scoped block (synchronous state transitions) and a
phase-2 block (tools/list I/O outside the outer lock). The maybe_probe tuple
now carries (client_arc, daemon_version) to thread server_info through the
drop/re-acquire boundary while retaining full capability-gating tool_names.

  mapping to ServiceHealth::Error (was silently falling through to Degraded)

  tools_list_has_four_tools (the assertion already checked 4)
- trusty-console/server.rs: add clarifying comment to apply_handle_overrides
  that Available handles return None from degraded_hint (skipping only Absent
  is safe)

New tests:
- outer_lock_not_held_during_probe_outer_lock_remains_acquirable: verifies both
  Connected/Degraded/Absent outcomes resolve correctly; documents concurrency
  invariant enforced by the drop/re-acquire structure

fix(trusty-search): forward explicit --data-dir to background daemon self-spawn (closes #1182) (#1186)

Before this fix, `handle_start` only stamped TRUSTY_DATA_DIR into the process
environment when it was not already set. The background self-spawn path then
relied on child env inheritance. This meant `trusty-search start --data-dir
/new/path` with a pre-existing TRUSTY_DATA_DIR=/old/path would silently make
the spawned child use /old/path — the explicit CLI flag was lost.

Fix: pass `--data-dir <dir>` as an explicit CLI arg to the child Command in
`commands::start::daemon.rs` (the split location in post-#1180 code) when
data_dir is Some, so the flag always wins over any inherited env var. The
foreground path continues to respect TRUSTY_DATA_DIR (env) > --data-dir (CLI)
for backward-compat with launchd/systemd units that set it in the service file.

- spawn_args_omit_data_dir_when_none (no-flag baseline)

fix(trusty-search): clamp XML chunker depth at zero on malformed input (closes #1181) (#1185)

The `chunk_xml` depth tracker used a bare `i32` with no lower bound.
On malformed XML (orphaned closing tags, more closes than opens) depth
went negative, making the emit guard `depth <= 1 && prev_depth >= 1`
fire spuriously and produce garbage chunks.

Fix: add `depth = depth.max(0)` immediately after the subtraction so
depth never goes below zero. Well-formed input is unaffected because
the clamp is a no-op when depth is already non-negative.

Added three unit tests covering the bug:
- test_chunk_xml_malformed_leading_close (file starts with </root>)
- test_chunk_xml_malformed_extra_closes (more closes than opens)
- test_chunk_xml_well_formed_unchanged (regression guard)

Before this fix a failed `CorpusStore::open` (incompatible redb page format,
corrupted file, or any I/O error at the path) was silently swallowed in
`build_indexer_from_entry`: the error was logged at ERROR level but execution
continued with no corpus store wired. `chunk_count` therefore fell through to
`unwrap_or(0)`, and `derive_warm_boot_stages` emitted `InProgress` — identical
to a freshly-created empty index. The failure was invisible to callers and to
the health/status endpoints.

Changes:
- `CodeIndexer`: add `corpus_open_failed: bool` field (false by default).
- `persistence_loader::build_indexer_from_entry`: set `corpus_open_failed = true`

fix(trusty-memory): robust MCP transport — compat shim + hardened serve --stdio proxy (closes #1141) (#1143)

* fix(trusty-memory): robust MCP transport — compat shim + hardened serve --stdio proxy (closes #1141)

ROOT-CAUSE VERDICT:

**The "UDS listener bound" disappearance was INTENTIONAL**, caused solely by
commit ba60e0c3 (#914 PR3, 2026-06-08). That commit deliberately deleted:
- `src/bin/mcp_bridge.rs` (the byte-pipe bridge binary)
- `src/transport/uds.rs` (the entire UDS transport)
- `spawn_uds_listener` call site + function in `src/lib.rs`
- The `[[bin]] trusty-memory-mcp-bridge` entry from `Cargo.toml`

This was the intended design: PR1 (#919) introduced `serve --stdio` as the
canonical MCP path; PR2 (#931) repointed all `.mcp.json` configs to it; PR3
(#933/ba60e0c3) deleted the dead bridge+UDS code.

Commit 9a3c5434 (`fix TOCTOU, prefer libc::kill`, 2026-06-09) touched
`daemon_lock.rs` / `lib.rs` ONLY — it correctly hardened the PID lock file
and is NOT involved in the UDS listener disappearance. There are TWO different
sockets:
- The UDS **MCP transport socket** (bound by the daemon in `transport/uds.rs`,
  deleted by ba60e0c3) — this is what emitted "UDS listener bound at …".
- The PID **lock file** (`daemon.lock`, managed by `daemon_lock.rs`) — this
  is what 9a3c5434 hardened, and it is not a UDS socket at all.

The user's MCP client gets -32000 because their `.mcp.json` still references
the now-deleted `trusty-memory-mcp-bridge` binary; that binary is absent
from `cargo install trusty-memory >= 0.15.2` outputs.

CHANGES:
A) COMPAT SHIM: re-adds `trusty-memory-mcp-bridge` as a thin deprecated `[[bin]]`
   (src/bin/mcp_bridge.rs, ~70 lines, no library deps beyond std). On Unix it
   re-execs `trusty-memory serve --stdio` so no extra process stays alive; on
   non-Unix it spawns a child and forwards stdio. Emits a one-line deprecation
   warning to stderr only (stdout stays clean for JSON-RPC framing). Bundled
   by single-install convention so `cargo install trusty-memory` produces it.

B) HARDENED serve --stdio proxy: already landed (serve_stdio_bridge.rs +
   serve_stdio.rs with daemon-bridge architecture, ensure_daemon_up with
   bounded retry/backoff, reconnect-on-error, JSON-RPC errors on transport
   failure instead of crashing the loop). No further changes needed here.

C) No single-instance locking regression found. Commit 9a3c5434 correctly
   hardened daemon_lock.rs with O_EXCL create and libc::kill. The lock file
   and the UDS socket are entirely separate concerns. No fix required.

D) DOCS: README.md updated — removes stale UDS/bridge references, documents
   `serve --stdio` as the canonical integration and the deprecated shim path.
   CLAUDE.md updated — connection-safe daemon restart note updated to reference
   `serve --stdio` proxy instead of the deleted `mcp_bridge` binary.

Smoke test evidence:
- Zero bytes written to stdout by the shim (MCP channel stays clean)
- Deprecation warning emits to stderr as required
- JSON-RPC initialize round-trip through shim returns valid response:

feat(trusty-search): contributed-graph overlay — kg_contrib store, POST /indexes/{id}/graph, graph/neighbors traversal (ADR-0009, refs #819) (#1129)

Implements the accepted ADR-0009 ingest contract: external extractors
(T-SQL/C# cross-tier scanners and future producers) contribute relationship
graphs into a durable per-index overlay that survives restarts AND reindex,
merged into the in-RAM petgraph at every graph-construction seam.

Storage (core/corpus_contrib.rs, child module of corpus):
- New `kg_contrib` redb table: one row per producer holding the complete
  serialized contribution + envelope metadata (producerVersion, gitSha —
  the #819 staleness refinement; no timestamps, preserving producer
  byte-determinism).
- Replace-per-producer semantics (the #819 deletion-correctness
  refinement): each ingest atomically replaces that producer's prior
  contribution — removed procs/tables never leave stale edges.
- Pre-upgrade DBs tolerated (missing table = empty), reopen-safe.

Merge (core/symbol_graph/contrib.rs):
- `SymbolGraph::merge_contrib`: idempotent fold — extractor-minted
  self-contained identity, first-kind-wins nodes, (from,to,kind) edge
  dedup, dangling/unknown-kind accounting (extends the #816 counter).
- Edge-kind resolution: coarse wire vocabulary (reads/writes/references/
  calls_function/calls_proc/accesses_resource) onto the #817 first-class
  variants, falling back to EdgeKind::from_tag (Option H: custom:* always
  round-trips).
- Both seams covered: warm-boot `load_from_corpus` merges after derived
  load; rebuild path runs `save_then_merge_contrib` (derived tables are
  persisted PRE-merge so they never absorb contributed rows).
- `SymbolNode` gains an in-RAM-only `kind: Option<String>` (table/proc/
  view/csharp_method for contributed nodes; None for code symbols).

HTTP (service/server/contrib_graph.rs):
- `POST /indexes/{id}/graph` (bulk lane, 256 MB body limit): validates,
  stores, rebuilds the serving graph; responds with replace flag +
  post-merge totals + unknown-tag drop count. 404/400/503 error contract.
- `GET /indexes/{id}/graph/neighbors?node=&direction=in|out|both&
  edge_kinds=&max_hops=`: the single ADR-0009 traversal primitive —
  direction-aware, kind-filtered BFS (hops clamped 1..=4), answering
  "what writes table X", "what does this method transitively touch",
  "callers of a deprecated proc".

(SipHash), which is not guaranteed stable across Rust toolchain versions or
process restarts. This silently invalidated persisted KG entity IDs on

formats are unchanged in structure. Only the hash values change.

  body in `fact_hash_str` with `Sha256::digest` (sha2 was already a dep via
  the `symgraph` feature). Update Why/What/Test docs. Add three new unit tests:
  `fact_hash_str_is_deterministic` (updated), `fact_hash_str_output_shape`
  (exact 8-char shape assertion), `fact_hash_str_pinned_values` (algorithm-pin
  with known SHA-256 expected hex outputs).
- `crates/trusty-common/Cargo.toml`: bump version 0.14.4 → 0.15.0 (minor bump;
  persisted-data contract change).
- `Cargo.toml`, `crates/trusty-search/Cargo.toml`, `crates/trusty-memory/Cargo.toml`,
  `crates/trusty-gworkspace/Cargo.toml`: update trusty-common version pins to 0.15.0.

fix(trusty-search): mark cold index failed on restore failure (closes #1106) (#1125)

* fix(trusty-search): mark cold index failed on restore failure so health metrics stay honest (closes #1106)

When `restore_fn` returns `false` (blocked volume, missing root_path),
`get_or_load_index` previously returned `LazyLoadError::Loading` without
removing the entry from `ColdIndexStore.entries`. This meant:

- The same expensive restore was re-attempted on every subsequent query
  (every query 503'd in a tight loop).
- `indexes_lazy` in `GET /health` never decreased, misleading operators
  and the trusty-console metrics view into thinking the index was still
  pending a routine lazy load.

Fix:
- Add `failed_entries: Arc<DashMap<IndexId, ()>>` to `ColdIndexStore`.
- Add `mark_failed(id)`: evicts from `entries` + `loading_gates`, inserts
  into `failed_entries`. After this call `contains()` returns `false`
  (so `indexes_lazy` decreases) and `is_failed()` returns `true`.
- Add `failed_len()`: reported as `indexes_failed` in `WarmBootSummary` on
  `GET /health` — distinct from `indexes_lazy` (pending) so operators can
  see at a glance that some indexes need intervention (daemon restart or
  re-registration) rather than assuming they are merely pending.
- Add `LazyLoadError::RestoreFailed` variant (permanent, distinct from
  `Loading` which is transient timeout).
- On `restore_fn == false`: call `cold_store.mark_failed(id)` then return
  `LazyLoadError::RestoreFailed`.
- In `search_handler`: add `is_failed` guard before the existing `contains`
  guard — permanently-failed indexes return 503 `index_restore_failed` with
  a clear operator message (not 404 "unknown index").

Retry/eviction policy: failure is permanent for the daemon's lifetime (no

chore(line-cap): count code lines (SLOC), not raw lines (#1123)

* chore(line-cap): count code lines (SLOC) not raw lines; regenerate allowlist

Replace the per-file `wc -l` raw-line count with a SLOC counter implemented
in awk. A line counts only when it contains non-whitespace source code after
all comment matter is stripped. Excluded from the count:
  - blank / whitespace-only lines
  - // line comments (including /// doc and //! inner-doc variants)
  - /* ... */ block comments, including multi-line spans — every line inside
    an open block is excluded
  - lines that are entirely a closing */
A line with code followed by a trailing // comment still counts.

The SLOC counter is centralised in a single SLOC_AWK variable; both the
snapshot-building pass and the update/check modes use the same logic so
counts are always consistent.

Lenient-heuristic note: edge cases where // or /* appear inside a string
literal or raw string may cause the counter to undercount SLOC (treating
code as a comment). The counter is designed to err toward leniency — it
may undercount code lines but will never over-count, so the gate will
never falsely fail a legitimate file.

Cap value stays 500 (now interpreted as 500 SLOC).

Allowlist regenerated with --update (SLOC counts are lower than raw-line
budgets, so --update accepted every entry without growing). Result:
169 entries -> 95 entries (74 files now fall under 500 SLOC and were
removed from the allowlist entirely).

  crates/trusty-search/src/service/reindex/mod.rs: 2975 raw -> 1658 SLOC

CI (.github/workflows/line-cap.yml) and pre-commit hook (.pre-commit-config.yaml)
unchanged — both just invoke `bash scripts/check_line_cap.sh`; the script
interface is identical.

state the cap counts SLOC, list the exclusion rules, and note the
lenient-heuristic caveat.

* fix(trusty-console): fix double-wrapping bug + use correct mcp subcommand args

Three bugs surfaced during E2E runtime proof for PR #1112:

1. Double-wrapping (root cause of parse_report failure): `handle_console_metrics`
   was calling `serialise_report(&report)` which emits a content[0].text envelope,
   then `wrap_tool_result` in the MCP dispatcher wrapped that Value AGAIN into
   another content[0].text envelope. `parse_report` in trusty-console extracts
   content[0].text and tried to deserialise the inner envelope as ConsoleMetricsReport
   (wrong type), always failing. Fix: return `serde_json::to_value(&report)` so
   `wrap_tool_result` provides the single correct wrapping layer.

2. Wrong spawn args: `McpServiceHandle::new("trusty-analyze", ["serve", "--mcp"])`
   was spawning `trusty-analyze serve --mcp`, which requires trusty-search on
   port 7878, opens the redb facts store (already locked by the running daemon),
   and starts a conflicting HTTP server. Fix: use `["mcp"]` — the lightweight

* fix(trusty-search): address 4 confirmed PR #1103 review findings

Finding 1 (BUG — relocate drops LRU timestamps):
  indexes_relocate.rs was setting last_queried_unix / last_indexed_unix to None
  even though the comment said "preserve them". Load the on-disk entry once
  (combining the existing colocated read) and copy both timestamp fields so a
  PATCH /indexes/:id never silently zeroes the LRU sort key for a heavily-used
  index.  Test: relocate_preserves_lru_timestamps.

Finding 2 (BUG — TOCTOU race in get_or_load_index):
  Between the cold-store check (step 2) and loading_gate(id) (step 3), a
  concurrent mark_loaded can remove the entry, causing loading_gate to return
  None.  Previously this returned LazyLoadError::NotFound — a spurious 404 for
  an index that just became hot.  Fix: when loading_gate returns None, re-check
  the hot registry; return the handle if present, otherwise genuine NotFound.
  Test: get_or_load_index_gate_none_but_index_just_became_hot.

Finding 3 (PERF — sync disk read on hot path):
  search_handler called persistence::read_last_queried_unix (opens + parses
  indexes.toml) synchronously on the async handler for every warm query.
  Replace with an in-memory DashMap<IndexId, u64> (last_queried_write_cache) on
  SearchAppState.  Hot path consults the map (zero disk I/O); the background
  write task updates the map immediately (before tokio::spawn) so concurrent
  queries within the rate-limit window don't all race to spawn a write.
  Rate-limit semantics are fully preserved.
  Test: last_queried_cache_rate_limits_disk_writes.

  global_search_handler used registry.list() (hot only), so with a warm-boot cap
  POST /search silently returned partial results.  Add cold_indexes_skipped to
  the response (global fan-out: cold_store.len(); restricted fan-out: count of
  requested cold IDs).  Also adds ColdIndexStore::count_matching helper to avoid
  exposing DashMap internals to callers.  Lazy-loading all cold indexes during
  fan-out is deliberately NOT done (too expensive); a follow-up issue should

* fix(trusty-search): remove root from roots.toml on index delete to prevent warm-boot resurrection (closes #1090)

`delete_index_handler` removed the index from `indexes.toml` and the
in-memory registry, but left its root path in `roots.toml`. On the next
daemon restart the colocated warm-boot scan re-read `roots.toml`, found
the orphaned `.trusty-search/` directory, and re-registered the deleted
index — effectively resurrecting data the user had explicitly removed.

Fix: capture `root_path` from the in-memory registry handle BEFORE
unregistering, then call `roots_registry::remove_root()` after the
unregister. A `warn!` log is emitted if the roots.toml write fails
(with a note that warm-boot may still rediscover the root) so the
failure is visible without being fatal to the delete operation.

`indexes_skipped_timeout` but never reflected that in `warm_boot_degraded`.

the HTTP daemon's exclusive write lock. Writes failed with "palace is
read-only"; reads fell back to a stale snapshot.

Fix: `serve_stdio_bridge.rs` — a new module that:
1. Auto-starts the daemon if not running (`serve --foreground --http
   127.0.0.1:0` so the OS assigns a free port, avoiding EADDRINUSE when the
   real daemon holds :7070 — critical for test isolation).
2. Polls the `http_addr` file each iteration to discover the daemon's real
   dynamic port.
3. Hard-errors if the daemon doesn't start within 30 s — no silent fallback.
4. Forwards every non-notification request to `{base}/rpc`; suppresses
   notifications per MCP spec §4.1 (no response for requests with no id).

Key decisions:
- `serve --foreground --http 127.0.0.1:0`: port=0 → OS-assigned; --foreground
  bypasses the self-spawn shortcut that `serve --http` (bare) would trigger.
- `/health` probe (not `/api/v1/health`, which returns 404).
- `TRUSTY_DATA_DIR_OVERRIDE` is inherited by the spawned daemon so tests
  are hermetically isolated from the user's real palace.

Tests:
- `serve_stdio_e2e.rs`: 4 tests (tools/list, remember+recall, recall_all,
  stdout-only JSON) — previously timed out in 30 s, now pass in < 3 s.
- `serve_stdio_concurrent_e2e.rs`: rewritten for bridge architecture; two
  independent bridge clients each with their own isolated daemon.

  simplification) = net +348 lines.

ci: pre-seed/cache fastembed ONNX model to stop HF 429 test flake (closes #865) (#1057)

trusty-memory tests initialise FastEmbedder which downloads the AllMiniLML6V2Q
ONNX model (~22 MB) from HuggingFace on cold CI runners. Concurrent downloads
hit HF's HTTP 429 rate-limit, causing ~31 tests to fail spuriously and forcing
manual `gh run rerun` to recover.

Fix: two-stage approach in the test job:

1. actions/cache restores ~/.cache/fastembed keyed on Cargo.lock hash + model
   repo IDs. On a warm cache hit the runner never contacts HuggingFace at all.
2. On a cache miss, a pre-seed step downloads the model before cargo test runs,
   using a retried curl with 5×exponential backoff (5 → 10 → 20 → 40 s).
   One controlled download is far more reliable than N concurrent in-test fetches.

The FASTEMBED_CACHE_DIR env var is set to /home/runner/.cache/fastembed at the
job level so fastembed-rs, hf-hub, and the resolve_fastembed_cache_dir() helper
in trusty-common all agree on the same writable path. The pre-seed script writes
files directly into the hf-hub snapshot layout (refs/main pointer + snapshot dir
with tokenizer files + onnx/model_quantized.onnx), which hf-hub's cache.get()
recognises as a cache hit and skips the network call entirely.

Steady-state CI runs hit the action cache (no HF contact). Cold runs download
once with retry rather than failing on a single 429.

fix(trusty-search): isolate embed-pool sidecar calls from the async executor to prevent accept-loop starvation (closes #1017) (#1054)

Move EmbedPool worker tasks from tokio::spawn (HTTP runtime) onto dedicated
OS threads with per-worker single-thread Tokio runtimes.

Problem: worker tasks awaiting a 30 s CoreML/ANE sidecar stall occupied the
main Tokio runtime's thread pool, starving the axum accept loop and /health
endpoint under heavy embed load (issue #1017). PR #1016's worker-floor bump
(min 16 threads) was a probabilistic mitigation, not a root-cause fix.

Fix: each embed worker is now a std::thread::spawn'd OS thread that builds
its own new_current_thread() runtime and blocks on worker_loop. Tokio
mpsc/oneshot channels are runtime-agnostic, so callers on the HTTP runtime
send requests and await replies identically to before. A 30 s sidecar stall
now blocks only the embed worker's own OS thread — the HTTP runtime's threads
remain fully available for the accept loop and /health regardless of how many
workers are stalled.

The PR #1016 worker-floor bump becomes belt-and-suspenders rather than
load-bearing with this change in place.

- crates/trusty-search/src/service/embed_pool.rs: replace tokio::spawn
  with std::thread::Builder::spawn + current_thread runtime; hold JoinHandles
  in _worker_threads so threads are joined on pool drop; split tests to
  embed_pool_tests.rs to maintain 500-line cap; update module doc with
  isolation rationale; make EmbedRequest/EmbedPool fields pub(crate) for
  test access.
- crates/trusty-search/src/service/embed_pool_tests.rs: new sibling test

fix(trusty-analyze): resolve CALLS edge targets via qualified node-id scheme across all 13 adapters (closes #913) (#1056)

Root cause: adapters emitted call-edge targets as
`{lang}:{kind}:{caller_file}:{bare_callee}`, which never matched the
class-qualified node IDs (`{lang}:{Kind}:{file}:{Class}:{Method}`) used
when nodes are created.  Resolution rate was ~4.8% (only same-file
free-function calls hit by accident).

Fix (two-pass approach):
1. All 13 adapters now emit unresolved sentinel targets via the shared
   `lang::call_target::build_call_target()` helper, which produces
   `{lang}:{kind}::{callee}` (double-colon signals "unresolved").
2. A new `core::call_resolver::resolve_calls()` pass runs after
   `linker::link()` deduplication.  It builds a
   `(language, bare_name) → Vec<&KgNode>` index over the canonical node
   set and rewrites sentinel targets to real node IDs:
   - Unique match → resolved unconditionally.
   - Multiple candidates → same-file match preferred; cross-file
     ambiguous cases preserved as sentinel (no wrong-guess resolution).
   - No candidates → external call, sentinel preserved.

New files:
  crates/trusty-analyze/src/lang/call_target.rs  — shared sentinel builder/parser
  crates/trusty-analyze/src/core/call_resolver.rs — resolution pass + 6 tests

* fix(trusty-analyze): restore per-file scratch isolation + harden setsid in pre_exec (PR #967 review, closes #976)

Finding 1 — basename collision in run_diagnostics_blocking_with_registry
(regression introduced by PR #967's dispatch restructuring):

commit 16cd8eac (closes #976) fixed run_diagnostics_blocking in
handlers/analysis.rs by writing each file to a unique numeric subdir
(scratch/<idx>/<name>) instead of scratch/<name>. PR #967 extracted the
dispatch into diagnostics_dispatch.rs and introduced a new
run_diagnostics_blocking_with_registry function that did NOT carry the
isolation forward — two files with the same basename (src/a/Main.cs and
src/b/Main.cs) in the same language bucket would collide: the second
fs::write overwrote the first, silently dropping its diagnostics.

Fix: restore the per-file subdir pattern using enumerate() in the
file-scoped tool loop — mirrors the 16cd8eac fix exactly.

Test: add run_diagnostics_blocking_with_registry_two_files_same_basename
which injects a FakeFileScopedTool (no external linter required) that
records the (path, content) it receives. The test asserts:
  (a) the tool was called twice (not once, which is what the old code did),
  (b) the two scratch paths are distinct,
  (c) both index-relative paths appear in the output vec.
This test FAILS against scratch.path().join(&name) and PASSES with the
scratch/<idx>/<name> fix.

Finding 2 — setsid() return value silently discarded in pre_exec:

The pre_exec closure called libc::setsid() but ignored its return value.
If setsid() fails with EPERM (caller already a process-group leader —
possible in some container / test-harness setups) the child would NOT be
in a new session; the timeout-path kill(-pgid, SIGKILL) would then target
the parent's process group, potentially killing the service or test runner.

Fix: check the return value and propagate failure as Err, which causes
spawn() to return an error cleanly rather than proceeding with an unsafe
kill target. Updated the docstring to document the setsid failure path.

fix(search): prune stale chunks for changed files on non-force reindex (closes #855) (#1001)

Without this fix, a non-force incremental reindex of a file that produces
fewer chunks than the previous version leaves orphan chunk IDs in every
store (redb, HNSW, BM25, in-memory).  The staging corpus is seeded by
`copy_all_from` (which carries ALL prior rows), and `commit_parsed_batch`
uses INSERT-OR-OVERWRITE semantics — it never removes the old IDs when a
file shrinks.  A deleted function's chunk survives in staging, is promoted
to the live corpus, and is returned by search until the next `--force`
reindex.

Fix: add `changed_corpus_paths: Vec<String>` to `BatchPayload` and
`ParsedReadyBatch` to carry the corpus-relative paths of every file being
re-indexed.  In `commit_parsed_and_finalize`, inside the same write-lock
window as the subsequent `commit_parsed_batch` call, iterate the changed
paths and call `remove_file_no_kg_rebuild` for each.  This gives
delete-then-insert atomicity: concurrent readers on the read lock either
see the full old chunk set or the full new chunk set, never a mix.

Brand-new files (not previously in the corpus) return 0 removed chunks
and are unaffected.  The KG is not rebuilt per-file (matching the existing
`remove_file_no_kg_rebuild` contract); Phase 3 rebuilds it once for the
whole reindex as before.

Regression test added in `prune_tests.rs`:
- PRE-FIX model verifies upsert-only leaves 3 chunks (1 new + 2 orphans)
- POST-FIX model verifies delete-then-insert leaves exactly 1 chunk
- Runs as part of `cargo test -p trusty-search` (no daemon, no ONNX model)

remove continue-on-error to promote it to a hard gate.

fix(review): propagate reqwest client-build errors instead of panicking in constructors (#973)

Closes #953

Eight production constructors previously called `.expect()` on
`reqwest::Client::builder().build()`, panicking on TLS init failure at
daemon startup. This commit hardens them to return `Result` and propagates
the error to callers.

Changed constructors (now return Result):
- `HttpSearchClient::new` / `from_config`  → `Result<Self, SearchClientError>`
- `HttpAnalyzeClient::new` / `from_config` → `Result<Self, AnalyzeClientError>`
- `SubprocessAnalyzeClient::new` / `from_config` → `Result<Self, AnalyzeClientError>`
- `GithubClient::new` / `with_timeout`     → `Result<Self, GithubError>`
- `ReqwestConfluenceTransport::new`        → `Result<Self, ContextSourceError>`
- `ReqwestJiraTransport::new`              → `Result<Self, ContextSourceError>`
- `ReqwestIssueSearch::new`               → `Result<Self, ContextSourceError>`

Caller update strategy:
- Binary / command callers (run, serve, compare, mcp/mod) propagate with
  `.map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(...))? ` into their existing `anyhow::Result`.
- Pipeline callers (diff.rs, post.rs, runner.rs) propagate with `?` into
  their existing `GithubError` return types.
- MCP tools.rs maps to `ToolError::InvalidParams`.
- reporter.rs degrades gracefully: logs a warning and returns `None`.
- Context-source `from_config` methods (Confluence, Jira, GitHub Issues)
  keep their infallible `Self` return type but build permanently-disabled
  sentinel sources with no-op trait impls when TLS init fails, so the
  orchestrator's `is_enabled()` skip path handles them safely.
- `Default` impls kept as-is (panicking) with clear doc explaining that
  production code should use `new()`.

Also splits `analyze_client.rs` and `jira.rs` test sections into sibling

feat(trusty-search): DEFER-EMBED indexing — fast lexical+KG pass, deferred semantic (#923) (#928)

* feat(trusty-search): DEFER-EMBED indexing — fast lexical+KG pass, deferred semantic (closes #923)

Indexes become searchable via BM25/KG within seconds of creation. The
synchronous fast pass (walk → chunk → BM25 → KG) marks lexical and graph
stages Ready immediately; HNSW vector embedding is deferred to a background
job that runs after the fast pass completes and marks semantic Ready when done.

C1 — Fast pass: `BatchCtx.defer_embed=true` routes through `parse_files_only`
  instead of `parse_and_embed_files`, skipping the embedder during the main
  reindex loop. `validate::reindex_outcome` accepts zero vectors when
  `defer_embed=true` so the #601 gate does not fire.

C2 — Background embed: `spawn_deferred_embed_pass` acquires the background
  semaphore, calls `CodeIndexer::embed_deferred_chunks` (new public method
  that snapshots all corpus RawChunks, embeds in batches via the existing
  `embed_chunks_in_batches`, upserts to HNSW, and warms the embedding cache),
  forces an HNSW snapshot, then writes `StageStatus::Ready` on the semantic
  stage. Idempotent: HNSW upsert_batch is idempotent; re-running re-embeds all
  chunks. Spawned only when `has_embedder() == true` to avoid no-op noise on
  BM25-only/test handles.

Wire-up: `defer_embed: bool` (default `true`) added to `IndexHandle`,
  `PersistedIndex`, `CreateIndexRequest`, `IndexConfig`, and `RegisterFilters`.
  Persistence: only `defer_embed = false` is written to `indexes.toml` (the
  default `true` is omitted to avoid churn on existing config files).
  YAML config: `defer_embed: false` in `trusty-search.yaml` opts a named index
  into synchronous full indexing.

* fix(memory): isolate data-dir override — no legacy dotfile write or real-env pin-scan (closes #880)

When TRUSTY_DATA_DIR_OVERRIDE is set, the daemon previously leaked into
the real environment in two ways:
1. It wrote ~/.trusty-memory/http_addr with the isolated instance's
   throwaway address, overwriting the real production daemon's discovery
   dotfile.
2. The startup pin-scan walked ~/Projects, ~/Developer, etc. and imported
   palaces from the live system into the isolated data root.

Fixes:
- Add `is_data_dir_override_active()` (public) — single predicate for
  both guards, keyed on TRUSTY_DATA_DIR_OVERRIDE being non-empty.
- `dotfile_http_addr_path()` now returns None when the override is active,
  so the dotfile write is skipped entirely for isolated instances.
- `spawn_startup_tasks` in main.rs passes an empty search list to
  `scan_pin_map` when the override is active, making the pin scan a no-op.
  Default (production) path unchanged.

Tests added (tests/isolation_override.rs):
- `is_data_dir_override_active_when_set` — true when env var is set
- `is_data_dir_override_inactive_when_unset` — false when unset

fix(search): reject empty/whitespace search queries with 400 (closes #882) (#886)

* fix(search): reject empty/whitespace search queries with 400 (closes #882)

HTTP handlers for all search lanes (hybrid, lexical, semantic, grep) now
return 400 with {"error":"query must not be empty"} when the trimmed query
text (or grep pattern) is empty. The MCP post() helper maps HTTP 400 to
DispatchError::InvalidParams so LLM agents receive an actionable error
message instead of an opaque transport failure.

Root-cause: no internal caller legitimately sends empty queries. The Svelte
admin UI guards against them client-side. The most likely real-world source
is external/manual callers: CLI with `trusty-search query ""`, direct API
calls, or LLM-generated MCP tool invocations with an empty string argument.
Previously an empty query fell through to the Unknown intent classifier and
performed a pure k-NN vector similarity search that returned arbitrary
top-k results — expensive and semantically useless.

Issue #878: `GET /indexes/:id/status` returned `last_indexed: null` after a
fresh reindex because `index_disk_and_mtime()` only probes the legacy global
data dir and misses colocated `.trusty-search/` storage and newly-created
indexes. Fix: add `last_indexed_at: Arc<RwLock<Option<String>>>` to
`IndexHandle`, stamped with `now_rfc3339()` in the `Complete` branch of
`spawn_reindex_with_cleanup()`. The status handler prefers this in-memory
value over the disk-mtime fallback.

Issue #879: `stages.lexical.chunks` reported 0 on a no-change incremental
reindex because `ReindexProgress::total_chunks` is a per-run counter that
reads 0 when all files are hash-skipped. Fix: compute the corpus total from
`corpus_arc().chunk_count()` (durable redb count), falling back to the
in-memory chunk map and finally the per-run counter. This keeps
`stages.lexical.chunks` consistent with the top-level `chunk_count` regardless
of whether any new chunks were committed in the most recent pass.

fix(trusty-search): prune deleted files on non-force reindex (closes #848) (#854)

* fix(trusty-search): prune deleted files on non-force reindex (closes #848)

After the #839 carryover fix, `copy_all_from` seeds the staging corpus
with ALL live rows before the batch loop.  A file deleted from disk is
never walked → never re-indexed → its rows survive in staging and are
promoted to live on success.  Search then returns results from files that
no longer exist on disk.

Fix: add a prune pass immediately after the producer finishes and before
the staging corpus is promoted.  The pass computes:

  deleted_files = list_indexed_files(staging) − walked_set

and for each deleted file removes data from all stores:
  1. staging redb — chunk rows, entity row, file-hash entry
  2. in-memory — HNSW, BM25, chunk map, embedding LRU
     (via `remove_file_no_kg_rebuild`; KG is rebuilt once in Phase 3)
  3. in-process file-hash DashMap (prevents false-skip on next reindex)

The prune pass is a no-op when no files were deleted and is gated to the
non-force incremental path only (`corpus_swap_tmp.is_some() && !force &&
!memory_aborted`).  Per-file errors are logged at WARN and swallowed
(best-effort; a miss is caught by the next reindex).

New helpers in `CorpusStore`:
  - `list_indexed_files()` — distinct file paths across CHUNKS_TABLE
  - `delete_file_hash_entries()` — idempotent FILE_HASHES_TABLE removal

New method on `CodeIndexer`:
  - `remove_file_no_kg_rebuild()` — removes a file from all in-memory +
    redb stores without triggering an O(N) KG rebuild per file

to keep `reindex/mod.rs` within its allowlist budget (4214 → 4214 lines
after split; allowlist ratcheted down from 4623 peak).

  normalisation used by BOTH `prepare_batch_payload` (chunk writer) and
  `prune_deleted_files_from_staging` (set-difference builder). Previously
  each site had its own inline `strip_prefix(...).unwrap_or(...).display()`
  expression; a future divergence (e.g. an `unwrap_or` returning an absolute
  path on one side but not the other) would make the set-difference classify
  live files as "deleted" and wipe the staging corpus.

  per-file prune, reconstruct the absolute path (`canonical_root.join(relative)`)
  and verify it does NOT exist on disk via `Path::exists()`. If the file is
  still present, it is a false positive from a path-normalisation mismatch —
  the prune is skipped and a `warn!` is emitted. Only files confirmed absent
  from disk are ever removed. This makes mass-deletion from a normalisation
  bug structurally impossible.

* fix(trusty-search): open durable redb corpus at warm-boot so post-restart reindex skips unchanged files (refs #840)

Root cause: `build_indexer_from_entry` called `CorpusStore::open` once and
on any failure (most commonly `DatabaseAlreadyOpen` from a stale OS-level
file lock on a fast daemon restart) silently continued without a corpus store.
With no corpus store, `load_into_cache` returned 0 hashes and every
post-restart reindex cold-started (Skipped 0, full re-embed).

Changes:
- `persistence_loader.rs`: add `open_corpus_with_retry` that retries once
  after 50 ms on `DatabaseAlreadyOpen`; upgrade corpus-open failure log from
  WARN to ERROR with actionable message (refs #840 Part 1)
- `reindex/hash_cache.rs`: change `load_into_cache` return type from `()`
  to `usize` (count of hashes loaded from redb); add regression test
  `warm_boot_hash_load_after_simulated_restart` that simulates persist →
  drop → reopen → assert count > 0 (refs #840 Part 1)
- `reindex/mod.rs`: move hash loading BEFORE SSE `start` event emission so
  the count is available; include `hashes_loaded: N` in the `start` event
  payload for operator observability without daemon log grep (refs #840 Part 2)

Part 3 (LRU reuse in embed_chunks_in_batches): deferred. File-hash skip
already handles the primary hot path (unchanged files never reach the
embedder). Consulting the LRU inside the batch loop would add per-chunk
lock overhead with near-zero hit rate on changed/new files.

fix(trusty-search): carry unchanged chunks into staging corpus on incremental reindex (closes #839) (#844)

* fix(trusty-search): carry unchanged chunks into staging corpus on incremental reindex — no durable data loss on restart (closes #839)

Root cause: `begin_force_corpus_swap` opened a FRESH EMPTY `index.redb.tmp` for
every non-force reindex. Hash-skipped (unchanged) files were `continue`d in the
batch loop and never written to the staging store. On `commit_force_corpus_swap`
the staging was atomically promoted over the live `index.redb`, producing a corpus
that contained ONLY the re-embedded files. The next daemon restart (reopen from
disk) loaded only those files — silently losing all unchanged files' chunks.

Fix: add `CorpusStore::copy_all_from(source) -> Result<()>` that bulk-copies
chunks, entities, file hashes, and _meta from the live corpus into the fresh
staging store before any batch writes. The batch loop then upserts (overwrites)
changed files' rows; unchanged files survive because their rows were pre-copied.
KG tables are intentionally excluded — they are rebuilt from scratch at the end of
every reindex via `rebuild_symbol_graph_for_reindex`. If `copy_all_from` fails
(e.g. I/O error), the reindex degrades gracefully to the old behaviour with a
`warn` rather than blocking the entire reindex.

Tests added:
- `copy_all_from_seeds_staging_corpus` — unit test in `corpus::tests` verifying
  the bulk copy semantics (chunks, entities, hashes, _meta, idempotency, empty source)
- `incremental_reindex_no_durable_data_loss` — regression test in
  `service::reindex::tests` directly modelling the pre-fix (data loss) and
  post-fix (carryover) staging behaviour using CorpusStore primitives

* fix(trusty-search): abort incremental reindex on carryover failure — keep live corpus intact (refs #839)

fix(tga): cover all accessible repos in PR reviewer ingestion (closes #752) (#808)

Switch store_pull_requests in both the GitHub and Bitbucket clients from
INSERT OR REPLACE to INSERT … ON CONFLICT(provider,repository,pr_number)
DO UPDATE SET, which preserves the existing `id` primary key on
re-collection.

Root cause: INSERT OR REPLACE deletes the conflicting row then reinserts
it, assigning a new `id`. The pr_reviewers table has a foreign key on
pull_requests.id with ON DELETE CASCADE, so every tga-collect run that
touched an already-stored PR silently cascade-deleted its reviewer rows.
On a 159-repo org the reviewer ingestion pass had to re-fetch all 36 K+
PRs from scratch on every run, exhausting the GitHub API rate limit after
roughly 2 repos worth of data.

The ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE path leaves `id` unchanged, so reviewer rows
accumulated across runs and the per-repo reviewer pass only fetches new
or updated PRs.

* fix(trusty-search): normalize watcher Removed-arm + dual-root strip for deleted files (refs #804)

The original fix (issue #402) normalized WatchEvent::Modified paths via
watcher_relative_path but left WatchEvent::Removed using the absolute
event path. Deleted files therefore never matched the relative key stored
by handle_modified, so stale chunks silently lingered in the HNSW + BM25
index after any file deletion.

Additional complication: when a file is already gone, std::fs::canonicalize
on the event path fails. On macOS notify may deliver the path under the raw
root (e.g. /var/folders/…) while canonical_root is /private/var/folders/…
(or vice versa), so a single strip_prefix attempt could still return an
absolute key.

- spawn_watch_loop now captures both raw_root and canonical_root and passes
  both to handle_modified and handle_removed.
- watcher_relative_path(canonical_root, raw_root, event_path) gains a third
  parameter. Fast path (file exists): canonicalize + strip canonical_root as
  before. Slow path (file deleted, canonicalize fails): attempt strip_prefix
  against canonical_root first, then raw_root — the dual-root strip ensures
  the macOS /var↔/private/var mismatch still yields a relative key.
- handle_removed now calls watcher_relative_path to compute the same key
  that handle_modified stored, and performs the IndexedFiles lookup by that
  relative key.
- handle_modified records with the relative key (PathBuf::from(&path_str))

  form notify delivers for each event type.

fix(trusty-memory): correct pid_alive liveness check on Linux via libc::kill with pid guards (fixes red main; refs #797) (#803)

The /bin/kill -0 shell-out had two Linux-specific bugs:
- kill(0, 0) probes the caller's process GROUP (returns 0 = alive),
  so pid_alive(0) returned true on Linux, triggering the false-positive
  that blocked stale-lock reclaim.
- u32::MAX cast to pid_t becomes -1, giving broadcast semantics
  (kill(-1, 0) returns success), so the acquire_lock_reclaims_stale_pid
  test always saw u32::MAX as "alive" on Linux CI.

Fix: replace the subprocess with libc::kill(pid, 0) guarded by explicit
range checks (pid == 0 || pid > i32::MAX → false immediately). For valid
pids: rc==0 → alive; ESRCH → dead; EPERM → exists-no-permission → alive.

Also replace u32::MAX as the "dead" PID in acquire_lock_reclaims_stale_pid
with a real spawned-and-reaped child — its PID is guaranteed dead by the
kernel after wait() returns, on all Unix variants.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(trusty-memory): guard pid_alive against out-of-range PIDs (closes #801) (#802)

The shell `kill` binary on Linux parses its PID argument as a signed
32-bit integer. Passing u32::MAX (4,294,967,295) overflows to -1, so
`kill -0 -1` broadcasts signal 0 to every process the caller may signal
— always succeeding — making `pid_alive` return `true` for a PID that
cannot exist. PID 0 has the same broadcast semantics.

Fix: add an upfront range guard in `pid_alive` that returns `false`
immediately for pid == 0 or pid > i32::MAX without calling `kill`.
Normal valid PIDs (1..=i32::MAX) continue to use `kill -0` as before.

Failing tests (now pass):
- commands::daemon_lock::tests::pid_alive_returns_false_for_pid_zero
- commands::daemon_lock::tests::acquire_lock_reclaims_stale_pid

Also extends `pid_alive_returns_false_for_pid_zero` to assert both
`pid_alive(u32::MAX)` and `pid_alive(0)` return false, and updates
the Why/What/Test docstring to document the signed-overflow mechanism.

fix(trusty-memory): serve --foreground owns lock + http_addr files, abort on port collision (closes #787) (#793)

Three bugs caused launchd `serve --foreground` instances and `start` (fork-and-detach)
invocations to pile up as orphan processes on ports 7070–7079:

Fix A — PID lock file ownership: `serve --foreground` now acquires `daemon.lock`
before binding. The RAII `DaemonLock` guard removes the file on any exit path
(graceful shutdown, panic, SIGTERM). Stale locks (dead PID) are reclaimed
transparently; a live lock returns Err so launchd logs the error and applies
ThrottleInterval instead of hot-looping.

Fix B — http_addr guarantee: `run_http_on` (called by `run_http_foreground`)
writes both the OS-standard http_addr file and the legacy dotfile path
immediately after binding, before accepting the first request. Both files are
removed on clean shutdown. A new `run_http_foreground` entry point makes this
guarantee explicit and separates the supervised path from ad-hoc invocations.

Fix C — abort on port collision: `bind_foreground_port` binds exactly
127.0.0.1:7070 and returns Err with a clear message on EADDRINUSE instead of
silently walking 7070→7071→…→7079→OS-assigned. The port-walking behaviour
is preserved in `run_http_dynamic` for ad-hoc CLI invocations.

New files:
- `src/commands/daemon_lock.rs` — DaemonLock RAII guard, acquire_lock,
  read_lock_pid, pid_alive; 10 unit tests (stale-lock reclaim, live-lock
  refusal, write/remove cycle); all tests use temp dirs.
- `src/foreground.rs` — bind_foreground_port, run_http_foreground, and
  bind_foreground_port_refuses_collision test; extracted from lib.rs to
  keep that file within its 500-line-cap allowlist budget (2796 lines).

which appends `--model <id>` before `--append-system-prompt-file`.

## Design gap note (#390)

Claude Code's `PreToolUse` hook receives the tool input as a read-only
JSON payload — the hook protocol does not allow mutation of the tool
arguments, so a hook cannot rewrite an `Agent` tool call's model field
at dispatch time. The implemented approach (injecting `--model` at
session-launch time via `build_claude_command`) is the correct seam: the
PM session Claude Code instance inherits the model from the CLI flag, and
all agent delegations from that PM session inherit the same model unless
overridden. A future `tm agent launch --model` subcommand could extend
this for per-delegation overrides, but the session-level injection covers
the primary use case in #390.

Three root-cause fixes for the 0.23.6 CUDA embedder stall/hang/zero-vectors regression on large (~44k-file) workloads:

permanently killed the task; all subsequent embed_batch calls hung forever on

forwarded raw to sidecar ORT sessions. With INFLIGHT=2 that saturated the T4
BFCArena. Extended sidecar_batch_size() with is_cuda + cuda_cap parameters;

[1,512]). trusty-search do_spawn() now resolves is_cuda and passes cuda_cap.

emits tracing::error! instead of warn!, with a clear message and remediation

* fix(trusty-common): correlate embedder responses by id to prevent stale-frame misattribution after timeout (#763)

Replace the FIFO VecDeque pending queue with a HashMap<u64, PendingRequest>
keyed by JSON-RPC request id. On timeout, only the stalled entry (by oldest
id) is removed and errored; the reader continues. When the sidecar eventually
delivers the stale response, the id-lookup finds no entry and discards the
frame — it can never be misattributed to a new request.

The previous fix (continue instead of return) kept the reader task alive but
left the FIFO misattribution hazard: a stale late-arriving response for
request A would be popped and dispatched to request B, silently injecting
wrong embeddings into the HNSW index. This commit closes that gap.

Wire protocol: trusty-embedderd already echoes the request id verbatim in
every RpcResponse. The client already sent a monotonic u64 id per request
but discarded the echoed id (marked #[allow(dead_code)]). This change uses it.

  is directly testable without ONNX; refactor the guard call site; add exact
  == 0.0 rationale comment; fix tracing::error! duplicate positional arg.
- supervisor.rs: document OnceLock process-scope caching caveat for test authors.
- stdio_tests.rs: extend misattribution test to prove stale frame is discarded
  and request B receives its own correct embeddings (fails on old FIFO impl).

fix(trusty-review): fix silent mid-file hunk truncation in render_for_prompt (#761)

The inner `break` in the hunk loop of `FilteredDiff::render_for_prompt`
only exited the inner hunk loop, not the outer file loop.  This allowed
subsequent files to be rendered after a half-rendered file whose hunks
overflowed the char budget — with no marker indicating the drop.

The reviewer LLM would see File A (partial: N of M hunks), then File B,
File C … in full, with no signal that File A was incomplete.  This is a
form of silent diff truncation distinct from the already-fixed raw-diff
cap (MAX_DIFF_CHARS, #624).

Fix:
- Use a labeled loop `'files:` and `break 'files` from the inner hunk
  budget check so the outer loop is exited when the budget is hit.
- Track `budget_exceeded: bool`; when set, append a loud
  `[RENDER TRUNCATED — char budget (N) reached …]` marker before the
  noise summary so the LLM cannot miss that content was omitted.
- Reserve `TRUNC_MARKER_RESERVE = 120` chars in the budget check so the
  marker itself never causes a large overshoot.
- Split tests into a sibling `models_tests.rs` (models.rs was 613 lines
  after the new tests; now 360+278, both under the 500-line cap).

New tests:
  render_for_prompt_mid_file_hunk_overflow_loud_not_silent — regression
    guard for the inner-break bug.
  render_for_prompt_no_truncation_marker_when_fits — no false-positive.
  render_for_prompt_marker_does_not_cause_large_overflow — overhead bound.

Closes: #622 (the render_for_prompt silent-truncation vector).
Related: #624 (MAX_DIFF_CHARS cap raise + DiffAnalyzer noise filter).

* fix(trusty-search): make warm-boot restore resilient to hung/denied roots under launchd (refs #718)

Part 2 of issue #718. E2e launchd verification of the Part 1 fix (0ba5892)
revealed a second distinct bug: the daemon booted with 0 indexes even though
indexes.toml loaded 57 legacy entries correctly.

Root cause: `collect_all_index_entries` ran `scan_roots_for_colocated_indexes`
(a blocking recursive std::fs walk via `read_dir` + `canonicalize`) *synchronously
on the tokio reactor thread*, then gated ALL index registration — including the
accessible legacy entries — behind it. Under launchd on macOS 26 Tahoe, tracked
roots on `/Volumes/SSD1` (external USB SSD) trigger TCC permission checks that
block `canonicalize` indefinitely, stalling the entire async restore task. The
"restoring N registration(s)" log line never appeared (3.5+ min observation)
because it was sequenced after `collect_all_index_entries` returned.

Fix: extract a new `service/warm_boot.rs` module that implements a two-phase
resilient restore:

Phase 1 — legacy indexes (indexes.toml, fast TOML read from
~/Library/Application Support/ — always accessible under launchd) are collected
synchronously via `collect_legacy_entries` and registered immediately.

Phase 2 — colocated roots are scanned via `collect_colocated_entries`:
- Each root's fs walk runs in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` (blocking calls off
  the reactor).
- Per-root `tokio::time::timeout` (ROOT_SCAN_TIMEOUT = 10 s) bounds any single
  hung or TCC-denied root. Timeout emits `warn!` with the root path and an
  actionable hint: "grant Full Disk Access to the launchd agent in System
  Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access".
- `PermissionDenied` / EPERM pre-flight errors emit `error!` with the same hint.
- One root failing/timing out does NOT abort other roots.

Removes the old `collect_all_index_entries` (dead code after refactor).
`restore_indexes` in start.rs now logs Phase 1 completion independently of
Phase 2, so a future launchd boot is fully diagnosable from the log alone.

- `is_likely_external_volume_detection`
- `scan_one_root_nonexistent_returns_empty`
- `scan_one_root_finds_colocated_index`
- `colocated_scan_partial_failure_still_returns_accessible` (key invariant)

* fix(trusty-search): isolate blocking warm-boot opens on spawn_blocking so launchd daemon stays responsive (refs #718)

The Part 3 fix (commit 67519b3) used `tokio::spawn` to run each per-index
restore as an async task. However `build_indexer_from_entry` contains blocking
`std::fs`/redb/usearch calls (`CorpusStore::open`, `std::fs::read`, mmap via
`index.view()`) that run on tokio *worker* threads. When macOS TCC denies the
`open()` syscall on a path like `/Volumes/SSD1`, the kernel blocks the thread
uninterruptibly — `tokio::time::timeout` fires but cannot cancel a thread frozen
in a syscall. With 57 indexes, all 57 workers froze one by one, starving the
runtime and making `/health` unresponsive for ~5 minutes.

This fix replaces `tokio::spawn(future)` with:

    let handle = Handle::current();
    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || handle.block_on(future))

`spawn_blocking` assigns work to the dedicated blocking-pool thread (default cap
512), not an async worker. When TCC freezes `open()`, that blocking-pool thread
is abandoned (one per index — 57 is fine vs. cap 512), but all async runtime
workers remain free. `/health` stays responsive throughout the entire warm-boot
sequence. `Handle::block_on` is the standard tokio pattern for driving async
futures inside a blocking-pool thread without nesting runtimes.

A new regression test `restore_bounded_runtime_stays_responsive_during_slow_blocking_restore`
uses `std::thread::sleep` (genuine blocking, not async) inside the restore closure
to prove the blocking-pool isolation: the async /health-proxy task (100ms async
sleep) completes while the blocking restore thread is parked in the syscall. This
test would fail if the code used `tokio::spawn` (the Part 3 bug).

README troubleshooting section now explicitly lists "run trusty-search manually"
(not via launchd) as remedy #4, explaining that TCC applies different access rules
to interactive processes vs launchd agents.

This pass guarantees: async runtime stays responsive during warm-boot; the per-index
loop continues past each timeout; terminal summary always emitted (even when 0 of N
indexes restore). Leaked blocking threads (one per TCC-blocked index) are accepted
per the fix spec. Full uninterruptible-open hardening is a follow-up ticket.

chore: upgrade redb 2.6 → 4.x workspace-wide + graceful old-format handling (closes #702) (#707)

* chore: upgrade redb 2.6 → 4.x workspace-wide + graceful old-format handling (closes #702)

Bump `redb` from 2.6 to 4.1.0 across the whole workspace and handle the
on-disk format incompatibility gracefully at every persistent-store open
site.

redb 3.0 dropped support for the v2 on-disk format, so redb 4.x cannot open
an `index.redb` / `kg.redb` / `facts.redb` / `dedup.redb` / `store.redb`
written by redb 2.x — `Database::open`/`create` returns
`DatabaseError::UpgradeRequired(_)`. Left unhandled, that turns a routine
binary upgrade into a hard daemon crash on the first warm boot, or (worse)
the #601/#694 false-healthy bug where a store silently presents as empty and
the daemon reports `status=ready`. redb 4.1.0's MSRV is 1.89, below the
workspace floor of 1.91, so the upgrade is unblocked.

Dependency:
- Root `[workspace.dependencies] redb = "2.6"` → `"4"` (resolves 4.1.0).
- Convert the two local `redb = "2.6"` pins (open-mpm, trusty-search) to
  `{ workspace = true }`.

API migration (mechanical, redb 4.x):
- `begin_read`/`begin_write` moved to the `ReadableDatabase` trait; add the
  trait import wherever those are called. No `RedbKey`/`RedbValue`, `drain`,
  `insert_reserve`, `StorageBackend`, or `check_integrity` call sites exist,
  so the rest of the surface is unchanged. The ~20 `spawn_blocking` wrappers
  around redb calls are untouched and keep working.

Graceful old-format handling (the load-bearing part):
- New classifier (per crate, to avoid cross-crate coupling between the MIT
  standalone crates and trusty-common) matches `UpgradeRequired` /
  `RepairAborted` / `Storage(Corrupted)` / `Storage(Io(InvalidData))` as
  "incompatible format" while explicitly NOT classifying `DatabaseAlreadyOpen`
  or transient I/O (e.g. `PermissionDenied`) — so a destructive recreate never
  fires on a lock or a real disk error.
- On an incompatible-format open, the file is renamed aside to
  `*.v2-incompatible` (numbered to avoid clobbering an earlier backup), a loud
  `ERROR` is logged, and a fresh empty DB is created. The old bytes are
  preserved for inspection / hand-migration.
- trusty-search corpus: `CorpusStore::open` now opens via
  `corpus_recovery::open_corpus_db_or_recreate`, so a stale v2 `index.redb` is
  backed up and replaced with an empty corpus — which is exactly the signal
  warm-boot needs to reindex, rather than reporting a populated/ready corpus.
- memory-core: `try_open_or_snapshot` gains an `OpenMode::Recreated` variant
  (distinct from the existing `ReadWrite`/`Snapshot` lock-fallback modes) so
  KG/vector palace opens surface degraded/needs-rebuild instead of ready;
  the recall/payload/chat stores and the trusty-memory activity log open via
  `redb_open::open_or_recreate`.
- trusty-analyze `facts.redb` and trusty-review `dedup.redb` recreate-empty
  with a clear ERROR (both are re-derivable caches).

- crates/trusty-common/src/memory_core/store/redb_open.rs
- crates/open-mpm/src/memory/redb_recovery.rs

the full classifier truth-table in trusty-common/trusty-search. Workspace

* fix(trusty-review): treat EPIPE on stdin write as non-fatal in spawn_analyze_review (refs #702)

On Linux, a subprocess that exits immediately (e.g. `false`) can close its
stdin pipe before the parent's write_all returns, producing BrokenPipe
(EPIPE).  The previous code propagated that as `AnalyzeClientError::Transport`
via the `?` operator, which masked the real failure and made the test

  spawn_analyze_review_with_fake_binary_that_fails

assert "exit-1 maps to Unavailable" (the second assert!) — the error was
Transport, not Unavailable.

Fix: treat BrokenPipe on the stdin write_all as non-fatal (the child already
exited; the non-zero exit code is the real signal).  Fall through to
wait_with_output and let the exit-code → Unavailable path fire as intended.
All other IO errors still propagate as Transport.

The mapping is semantically correct: a subprocess that exits non-zero before
reading its input means the analyze sidecar is unavailable/broken, which is
Unavailable, not a Transport fault on our side.  The root cause is
env-dependent (POSIX pipe + fast-exit process), not redb-related — the
failure was latent in the original subprocess client and surfaced on the Linux
CI runner where EPIPE is delivered synchronously.

feat(trusty-review): map-reduce Phase 2 — per-file diff splitter (refs #680, closes #698) (#700)

Implements the per-file diff splitter that turns `DiffAnalyzer` output
(`FilteredDiff`) into the flat list of `MapUnit`s the (future) map stage will
review.  Zero runtime behaviour change — nothing in the live runner consumes
the splitter yet (wired in Phase 5, #680).

## New types

- `MapUnitKind` enum: `Review { diff_text }` | `MetadataOnly { note }` —
  typed distinction between LLM-reviewable diff slices and no-cost metadata
  slots.
- `MapUnit` struct: `file`, `status`, `kind`, `diff_char_count`,
  `chunk_index`, `chunk_total`, `hunk_oversized` — one owned value per unit
  of map work; lifecycle details for sub-chunked files encoded in chunk fields.

## Splitter rules (`split_into_units`)

| Input file kind | Output |
|---|---|
| `Kept` w/ hunks, rendered ≤ `per_file_chars` | 1 `Review` unit |
| `Kept` w/ hunks, rendered > `per_file_chars` | N `Review` sub-chunks (whole-hunk boundary) |
| Single hunk > `per_file_chars` alone | 1 `Review` unit, `hunk_oversized=true` |
| `status == "removed"` | `MetadataOnly("deleted file")` |
| `SummaryOnly` disposition | `MetadataOnly("summary-only (fixture/generated)")` |
| `status == "renamed"` + no hunks | `MetadataOnly("rename-only (no content change)")` |
| No hunks (binary / empty) | `MetadataOnly("binary file or empty diff")` |
| Over `total_char_budget` | `MetadataOnly("budget exhausted")` |
| Over `max_calls` ceiling | `MetadataOnly("max-calls reached")` |

## Module layout

- `pipeline/mapreduce/unit.rs` (203 lines) — `MapUnit` + `MapUnitKind`
- `pipeline/mapreduce/splitter.rs` (398 lines) — pure splitter + render helpers
- `pipeline/mapreduce/splitter_tests.rs` (394 lines) — single-file, metadata,
  oversized sub-chunk tests
- `pipeline/mapreduce/splitter_budget_tests.rs` (310 lines) — budget enforcement,
  content, status, edge cases
- `pipeline/mapreduce/mod.rs` (20 lines) — re-export facade

All files under the 500-line cap; `check_line_cap.sh` clean.

`cargo build -p trusty-analyze --no-default-features --features
http-server,load-dynamic` compiles and LINKS on Amazon Linux 2023

  that triggered #605).

  compatible with AL2023), sets ORT_DYLIB_PATH.

destroys the live index.

#603 — non-destructive reindex + atomic swap (safety net, done first):
- Generalize the existing force-only staging mechanism to be the DEFAULT for
  every reindex with a durable corpus. New `service/reindex/staging.rs` holds
  the pure swap-vs-rollback decision (`should_stage`, `resolve_staging`,
  `StagingResolution`); the redb plumbing stays in mod.rs (needs private indexer
  internals). On failure/empty/memory-abort the staged corpus is discarded and
  the previous live index is preserved.

#602 — portable paths + migration re-trigger:
- Canonicalize `ctx.root` to match the walker (`validate::canonical_walk_root`)
  so chunk-write `strip_prefix` reliably yields ROOT-RELATIVE (portable) paths
  instead of falling back to absolute when root_path carries a symlink alias.

  on an incremental reindex after a root move, clear the hash cache to force a
  full re-relativization (live-path analogue of the M002/M003 startup migrations).

#601 — validate non-empty before marking ready (the false-green bug):
- New `validate::reindex_outcome` gate: a full-pipeline index (embedder wired,
  not lexical-only) that walked files but produced ZERO vectors is classified
  Failed, not Ready. New `StageStatus::Failed` + `StageState::failure` make
  `lifecycle_status` report `failed`; a terminal SSE `error` event carries
  `embed_failure_count`/`vector_count:0`/`fatal:true`. Lexical-only and
  no-embedder indexes legitimately have zero vectors and stay Ready.

fail incl. lexical-only & no-embedder exceptions; canonicalization & root-move

- pipeline/verify.rs: run_verification_round — bounded-concurrent (4-way)
  per-finding verification via the verifier role (Haiku by default). CONFIRMED
  keeps confidence; REFUTED demotes it to 0.10 (below every advisory/block gate)
  and records the outcome on the finding (never silently dropped). Config/
  lifecycle verifier errors map to VerifyOutcome::ErrorRefuted and emit the
  verification_model_error signal rather than being swallowed as a refutation.

  enforced by the verifier prompt (verify_prompt.rs) and the forced CONFIRMED/
  REFUTED json_schema/tool-use output.

  (VERIFY_CANDIDATE_MIN_CONFIDENCE); APPROVE/APPROVE* verify only blocking-tier
  (≥0.90) findings.

  surviving (non-refuted) findings via grade.rs::derive_verdict, so a BLOCK whose
  only blocking finding was REFUTED relaxes to APPROVE; a confirmed candidate
  preserves the model's escalation as a lower bound.

  unavailable (ModelNotFound/ModelNotReady/Validation/AccessDenied), emitting
  verification_model_error. Rationale (doc comment): code-intelligence had a prod
  incident where a stale verifier model silently auto-REFUTED every finding,

* fix(trusty-search): surface model-init/chunking progress + finer-grained embed progress reporting

Problem 1 — 46-second unmeasured stall (root cause: lazy-spawn embedder cold-start):
- Add `ReindexPhase::InitializingEmbedder` variant with label "Loading model…".
  `phase_to_bar_slot` maps it to the Chunk bar slot (slot 1) so the bar stays
  focused while the header transitions to "Loading model…", making the 30-60 s
  ONNX/CoreML model-load visible instead of a frozen 0/N Chunk bar.
- Daemon (`service/reindex.rs`): `BatchCtx` now carries an `embedder_pid_slot`
  (the same `Arc<AtomicU32>` already wired for RSS monitoring).  In
  `prepare_and_parse_batch`, before the first non-lexical embed call we check
  whether the sidecar PID slot is zero (= never spawned).  If so, we push an
  `embedder_init` SSE event before `parse_and_embed_files` blocks, and an
  `embedder_ready` event after it returns successfully.
- CLI (`reindex_engine.rs`): handles the two new SSE events by calling
  `set_phase(InitializingEmbedder)` / `set_phase(Embedding)` respectively.

  `self.phase.label()` as the stats-line prefix instead of a hard-coded
  "Embedding…" string.  The `phase_disc` `AtomicU64` in the background ticker
  mirrors the current phase discriminant so the ticker also produces a
  phase-accurate footer, fixing the "Chunking…" header / "Embedding…" footer
  mismatch visible during the 46 s stall.

Problem 2 — Embed progress advances in coarse per-file-batch increments:
- Daemon: after `parse_and_embed_files` returns (embed done, commit not yet
  started) we push a lightweight `chunk_progress` SSE event carrying
  `chunks_done` (batch-local count), `chunks_per_sec` (batch_chunks×1000 /
  embed_ms), and `embed_ms`.  This lets the ticker refresh CPS and ETA within
  seconds of each ONNX embedding completing — before the heavier commit
  (BM25 + HNSW + redb) fires the `batch` event.
- CLI: `chunk_progress` handler updates the `cps_now` atomic immediately so the
  1-second ticker picks up live throughput on the next tick.

* DEFAULT (no --timeout): progress-aware stall detection. The CLI keeps
  watching the SSE stream as long as the per-file `indexed` counter advances
  within a 120 s stall window. It only detaches when there has been no
  progress for 120 s (genuine stall) or when the stream closes normally.
  The old "timed out after 600s" alarm is gone for healthy runs.

* EXPLICIT (--timeout N): hard wall-clock cap, unchanged from the previous
  behaviour. `--timeout 0` still means "wait forever". The detach message
  now distinguishes "still progressing — detaching" vs "no recent progress".

  `stall_secs: u64` (default 120).

  the event loop uses a 1 s tick to check the stall window instead.
- batch and skip event handlers reset `last_progress` + `last_indexed_snapshot`
  on each forward-progress event.
- New public helpers: `run_reindex_opts` and `run_reindex_force_opts` accept

fix(trusty-search): prevent stale index root from dropping valid search results (closes #541) (#543)

* fix(trusty-search): prevent stale index root from dropping valid search results (closes #541)

Three-part fix for the warm-boot root_path staleness bug that caused
silent recall degradation with "dropped N result(s)" WARN bursts.

**Part 1 — Prevention (warm-boot re-canonicalize + persist)**
- Add `canonicalize_best_effort()` helper in `commands/start.rs` that
  resolves symlinks/aliases gracefully, falling back to the stored path
  on error (never blocks warm-boot).
- In `restore_one_index`: after the root_path existence guard, call
  `canonicalize_best_effort` on the stored path. If it yields a
  different canonical form, update `entry.root_path` and persist it
  back to `indexes.toml` so subsequent restarts are stable.
- In `try_locate_moved_root`: canonicalize the newly-found root before
  persisting it, so the #484 relocation path also writes canonical paths.

**Part 2 — Robustness (canonicalize-aware filter)**
- Update `file_is_within_root` with a two-phase check: (a) cheap lexical
  prefix check (no syscalls — hot path unchanged); (b) if (a) fails for
  an absolute path, canonicalize only the index root (not the file, which
  may not exist) and retry. Only results that fail the fast path pay the
  `canonicalize` cost.
- This means symlink aliases (macOS /var ↔ /private/var, volume mounts)
  can no longer cause legitimate results to be dropped.

**Part 3 — Observability**
- Add `trusty_search_dropped_out_of_root_total` Prometheus counter
  (labelled by `index_id`) incremented on every drop; surfaced via
  `GET /metrics` alongside existing counters.
- Add `stale_index_root: bool` to the search response `meta` block
  (`true` when `filtered_out > 0`), giving API clients a machine-readable
  signal without log scraping. Follows the `results_may_be_stale` pattern.
- Improve the WARN log: structured fields (`index_id`, `root`, `dropped`)
  plus an actionable remediation hint (`trusty-search index <path>`).

**Tests added**

- `commands::start::tests::canonicalize_best_effort_falls_back_for_missing_path`

fix(open-mpm): add flush() to async file writes to eliminate read-after-write races (closes #540) (#542)

Four write sites in open-mpm used tokio::fs::OpenOptions + write_all without
a subsequent flush().await, leaving Tokio's spawn_blocking buffer uncommitted
before returning. A reader (same task, different task, or test assertion) racing
that window would observe an empty/short file — the same root cause fixed in
usage::append_usage (PR #532).

Fixed sites (all now follow the error-first pattern: bail on write failure,
then flush):
- context/cluster.rs: ClusterStore::save — the primary flaky instance.
  cluster_save_and_load_roundtrip now stable across 10 repeated runs.
- context/indexer.rs: run_indexer write to entries.jsonl — fire-and-forget
  background task; flush ensures the retriever's subsequent load sees the bytes.
- context/cleaner.rs: clean_once log append to cleaner.log — flush ensures
  the test assertion that the log file exists (and is non-empty) is reliable.
- mistake_log.rs: append_line — two write_all calls replaced with
  error-guarded pattern + flush; the immediate read-back in
  mistake_log_records_nonzero_exit is now race-free.

Safe sites confirmed (no change needed):
- usage/mod.rs: already has flush().await (fixed in #532, reference pattern).
- perf/mod.rs: PerfCollector::flush already calls f.flush().await.ok().
- cli/memories_cmd/ops.rs: export_session already calls f.flush().await.
- ctrl/socket_listener.rs: write_socket_line already calls g.flush().await.
- All tokio::fs::write(path, bytes) call sites: free function flushes+closes
  internally — inherently safe, no change needed.
- interaction_log.rs / state_writer.rs: use std::fs + fs4 advisory locks
  (sync, not tokio::File); not subject to the spawn_blocking buffering issue.
- All std::fs::File write_all sites (tests/tools): synchronous — not affected.

* feat(trusty-memory, trusty-search): auto-update with cargo-install + safe self-restart (closes #537)

Reuses the existing crates.io check primitives in trusty-common::update and
builds the missing second half: perform_upgrade, verify_installed_binary,

not supervised by launchd, a restart hint is printed instead.

* fix(open-mpm): flush tokio File after write_all in append_usage to eliminate CI race

Tokio's File wraps OS calls via spawn_blocking; write_all completes the
future before the kernel buffer is necessarily flushed.  Reading the file
immediately after (as the tests do) could see 0 bytes even though the file
descriptor existed, causing the assertion `lines.len() == 1` to fail with
`left: 0, right: 1`.

Add an explicit `f.flush().await` after every successful write_all so
subsequent reads always observe the written line.  Also add an early return
after a write_all error so the flush path is only reached on success.

Fixes the `usage::tests::append_usage_creates_file` flake seen in CI run
26754347080 (PR #532 Test job).

fix(trusty-search): harden reindex SSE stream against sidecar stalls (closes #reindex-stall) (#516)

Three layered fixes:

Fix A (trusty-common 0.8.2→0.8.3): add 120 s per-call timeout to
StdioEmbedderClient::embed_batch via tokio::time::timeout around the
read_line call on the sidecar stdout. Under memory pressure (Apple Silicon
unified memory, deep reindex queue) the embedderd sidecar can stall mid-batch
and never write a response line; without a deadline read_line blocks forever,
leaving the entire reindex task hung and the SSE stream idle until the OS
tears down the TCP connection. Configurable via TRUSTY_EMBEDDERD_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECS.

Fix B (trusty-search 0.20.3→0.20.4): add 20 s SSE keep-alive heartbeat to
reindex_stream_handler. Uses tokio_stream::wrappers::IntervalStream merged
with the live BroadcastStream via futures::stream::select. Emits an SSE
comment frame (': heartbeat\n\n') — ignored by all spec-compliant clients
including eventsource-stream — so the HTTP body never goes fully idle between
events, preventing OS/proxy idle-connection teardown.

Fix C (trusty-search 0.20.3→0.20.4): add ReindexTerminationGuard RAII
struct to spawn_reindex_with_cleanup. Arms immediately after the semaphore
permit is acquired; disarms only after emit_complete_event completes. Any
unhandled early exit — panic, early return, or cancellation — fires the
guard's Drop impl, which broadcasts {"event":"error","message":"…"} and
sets progress.status = Failed, ensuring subscribers always receive a
terminal frame and never block waiting for a completion event that never arrives.

- service::reindex::tests::reindex_guard_fires_on_early_return
