fix(trusty-search): migrate-storage reconciles against filesystem state + handles legacy pointer-file (closes #491) (#494)

The previous implementation classified indexes as "already colocated" based on the
`colocated` flag in `indexes.toml` — ignoring actual filesystem state. This caused
all 15 user indexes to be skipped silently when a prior migration had set
`colocated=true` but `mkdir` failed because `<root>/.trusty-search` was a legacy
POINTER FILE (a small text file like `index = "itinerator"`), not a directory.

Changes:

  Classification by filesystem (not registry flag):
  - New `classify.rs` module: `classify_index()` returns `IndexMigrationClass` with
    five variants driven entirely by `std::fs` probes:
    - AlreadyColocated: `.trusty-search/` is a dir with populated `index.redb`
    - NeedsMigration: data in app-data, colocated dir missing/empty
    - LegacyPointerFile: `.trusty-search` is a FILE (pointer format) — THE #491 bug
    - SkipDeadRoot: root_path does not exist
    - SkipNoData: no data in either location

feat(trusty-common): error-capture layer with fingerprint dedup (bug-reporting phase 1, #479) (#487)

Adds a `tracing_subscriber::Layer` (`BugCaptureLayer`) gated behind the new
`bug-capture` feature flag. The layer taps ERROR-level tracing events and
persists them as structured `CapturedError` records in a bounded in-memory
ring buffer plus a JSON-Lines append file under the OS data directory
(`<data_dir>/<app_name>/errors.jsonl`).

Key design points:
- **Layer**: `BugCaptureLayer` filters to ERROR only; collects message, fields,
  code location, and crate target (from tracing metadata). Builds a SHA-256
  fingerprint via `normalise_message` (strips digits, hex tokens, home paths)
  before hashing `crate_target|normalised_message|location`.
- **Store**: `ErrorStore` wraps `Arc<Mutex<VecDeque>>` (ring, cap 500 by default)
  plus a JSONL file. Writes are synchronous and non-blocking (open per-append;
  IO errors print to stderr and are silently dropped). `load_from_disk`
  re-populates the ring on daemon restart. Corrupt lines are skipped gracefully.
- **Query API** (for Phase 2): `recent_errors(n)` and `errors_by_fingerprint()`
  aggregate recurrent errors by count.
- **Install helper**: `bug_capture_layer(app_name, capacity, version)` returns
  `(BugCaptureLayer, ErrorStore)` ready for composition with any
  `tracing_subscriber::Registry`. Existing stderr logging is unchanged.
- **Opt-out**: `TRUSTY_NO_BUG_CAPTURE=1` disables capture at runtime (checked
  per-event so it works in tests too).
- **No new deps** in default builds. `bug-capture` feature enables `sha2`
  (already an optional workspace dep). SQLite is NOT required for Phase 1;
  the JSONL store is queryable by Phase 2 and can be migrated later.

fix(trusty-search): write new indexes colocated so search survives first restart (closes #483, closes #485) (#486)

## Root cause

`create_index_handler` called `build_indexer_with_persisted_state`, which
internally constructs a synthetic `PersistedIndex { colocated: false, .. }`.
This routed the corpus store (redb) and HNSW snapshot to the app-data path
(`<data_dir>/indexes/<id>/`).

Meanwhile, `indexes.toml` was written with `colocated = true` (the desired
value). On the next daemon restart `restore_indexes` → `build_indexer_from_entry`
read the persisted entry, saw `colocated: true`, called `colocated_storage_dir`
(which executes `create_dir_all`), and opened an EMPTY `.trusty-search/` that
shadowed the real app-data data → 0 chunks, no corpus store.

The missing corpus store also caused every subsequent `write_schema_version`
call (in the migration runner on restart) to return
"cannot write schema_version: no durable corpus" (#485).

## Fix (Option A — minimal correct fix)

Replace the `build_indexer_with_persisted_state` call in `create_index_handler`
with `build_indexer_from_entry` using a `PersistedIndex { colocated: true, .. }`.

The entry-aware builder routes the corpus store to `<root>/.trusty-search/index.redb`
via `corpus_redb_path_for_entry` → `colocated_redb_path` → `colocated_storage_dir`
(which calls `create_dir_all`). The `.trusty-search/` directory therefore exists
ON DISK before the first reindex, so every write-path probe
(`has_colocated_storage` in persist.rs / reindex.rs) now sees the directory and
routes HNSW and corpus writes to the colocated location too.

Writer and loader now agree on the same path from the moment the index is created.
No `--force` reindex is needed to repair an affected index; new indexes created
after this fix are durable across the first restart without any manual intervention.

Option B (threading the `colocated` flag through `IndexHandle` to avoid the
filesystem probe entirely) was evaluated. With Option A the `.trusty-search/`
directory is created eagerly during index construction, so the filesystem probe
is always consistent. Option B was not needed and was deferred.

## #484 (moved project) — deferred

Detecting a moved project root and falling back to a populated colocated store
requires substantial path-resolution work (updating `indexes.toml`, re-registering
roots). This is left to a follow-up issue. At minimum, a moved project now fails
at the corpus-open step (redb file not found at old root) rather than silently
loading 0 chunks from a freshly-created empty dir — a slight improvement in
error visibility but not a full fix.

## Tests added

- `colocated_create_handler_path_survives_simulated_reload`: the exact #483
  scenario — create with `colocated: true`, write a chunk, drop the indexer,
  reload via the same entry, assert `chunk_count > 0`.
- `colocated_create_path_wires_corpus_store_for_schema_version`: the #485
  scenario — create path must wire a corpus store and it must be inside the
  project root (colocated), not app-data.
- `legacy_non_colocated_path_does_not_panic`: regression guard that the
  `colocated: false` path still builds without panicking.

fix(trusty-memory): emit startup pin-scan log + harden http_addr against staleness (closes #474, closes #475) (#476)

## Bug #474 — startup pin-scan INFO log never emitted

Root cause (dual): (1) When the daemon is launched via `trusty-memory start`
the self-spawned child redirects stderr to /dev/null, so the tracing INFO log
is discarded before reaching any terminal or log file. (2) When started via
launchd without an explicit RUST_LOG env var the default filter is `warn`,
which suppresses the `tracing::info!` call entirely.

Fix: add an `eprintln!` alongside the existing `tracing::info!` for the
startup pin-scan completion message. This dual-emit pattern matches the
`run_http_on` bind-address announcement and ensures the message is always
visible in launchd logs and on the operator's terminal regardless of the
tracing filter level. The `tracing::info!` now also includes elapsed
milliseconds for the scan duration.

New test: `spawn_startup_tasks_populates_pin_map` in `src/main.rs` verifies
the full wiring — a pinned project on disk, `spawn_startup_tasks` fires, and
`AppState::pin_project_map` is populated within 500 ms.

Manual verification: throwaway daemon on port 17777 with RUST_LOG=info now
shows:
  INFO startup pin scan complete: 1 pin(s) discovered in 0ms
  startup pin scan complete: 1 pin(s) discovered in 0ms

## Bug #475 — stale http_addr misdirects stop/doctor

Root cause: an unclean shutdown (SIGKILL, power loss) leaves the
`http_addr` discovery file with the previous daemon's address. If that was
an ephemeral port (e.g. `127.0.0.1:62675` from a `:0` fallback bind), the
new daemon's `single_instance_check` probes the dead port, removes the stale
file, and starts fresh — correct. BUT `doctor`'s `check_daemon_health` reads
the same stale file first, fails the probe, and reports "daemon not running"
even when a healthy daemon IS live on the default port 7070.

Fix: rework `check_daemon_health` to:
1. Attempt the primary probe against the recorded addr (unchanged for the
   happy path — no performance regression).
2. On primary-probe failure (stale/absent addr file, dead port, non-2xx),
   walk the well-known fallback range 7070..=7079 — the same range
   `bind_dynamic_port` prefers — before reporting failure.
3. Emit informative `Pass` messages that tell the operator whether the
   daemon was found via the recorded addr or the fallback scan.

The `write_http_addr_file` atomic-write (tmp + rename) and the clean-shutdown
removal in `run_http_on` were already correct. `stop` uses the process table
(not the addr file) so it is unaffected.

New tests: `check_daemon_health_fails_cleanly_with_stale_addr_and_no_listener`
and `check_daemon_health_fails_when_no_addr_file_and_no_listener` in
`src/commands/doctor.rs` exercise the fallback branches using
TRUSTY_DATA_DIR_OVERRIDE to isolate addr-file reads.

fix(trusty-memory): default LaunchAgent fd limits + single-instance guard + /health fd gauge (#464)

Root cause: the macOS LaunchAgent ran under launchd's default 256-fd soft
limit. With 82 palaces × ~3 redb files (data + KG + vector index) the daemon
exhausted its fd ceiling and every subsequent palace open failed with EMFILE.
launchd's KeepAlive (SuccessfulExit: false) then respawned each crashing
instance into a zombie herd (69 observed) because the new instance failed to
bind the already-occupied TCP port and exited non-zero.

Fix A — LaunchAgent fd limits (trusty-common/launchd.rs +
         trusty-memory/commands/service.rs):
- Added `LAUNCHD_FD_LIMIT = 8192` constant to `trusty_common::launchd`.
- Added `fd_limit: Option<u32>` field to `LaunchdConfig`; `render_plist()`
  now emits both `SoftResourceLimits` and `HardResourceLimits` dicts with
  `NumberOfFiles` when `fd_limit` is `Some`.
- `build_launchd_config` in `commands::service` sets `fd_limit: Some(8192)`,
  so every `service install` / `service start` regeneration permanently
  writes the raised limit into the plist — hand-patches can never be silently
  reverted. ThrottleInterval was already 10 s (preventing hot-loop respawn).
- Tests: `render_plist_includes_resource_limits` (trusty-common),
  `build_launchd_config_uses_canonical_shape` (extended assertions),
  `build_launchd_config_plist_includes_fd_limits_and_throttle` (new).

Fix B — single-instance guard (new src/commands/single_instance.rs +
         src/main.rs):
- New `single_instance_check()` async helper probes the `http_addr`
  discovery file before any bind attempt. If `/health` responds on the
  recorded address, a healthy daemon is already running.
- When alive: emits a log/stderr message and calls `std::process::exit(0)`.
  Exit 0 stops the launchd respawn storm: `KeepAlive { SuccessfulExit: false }`
  only respawns non-zero exits, so exit 0 = voluntary clean shutdown.
- When dead/absent/stale: `Proceed` — normal bind sequence continues.
- Stale UDS socket handling is already handled by `clean_stale_socket()` in
  `transport::uds` (connect-probe distinguishes live vs. stale).
- New `StartupAction` pure enum + `startup_action_from_probe_result()` make
  the decision logic unit-testable without real network I/O.
- Tests: `startup_action_from_probe_result_when_{alive,dead}`,

fix(trusty-search): prioritize user indexing over startup reindex storm + skip dead roots (closes #458) (#460)

**Problem**: On daemon startup, auto-discover queued reindex tasks for every
newly discovered project (observed 44) against a single 2-permit semaphore.
A user running `trusty-search index <new>` then queued at position ~15/44
and sat at "Crawl … pending" for minutes before getting a permit.

**Fix 1 — priority semaphore split**: Introduce a separate
`background_reindex_semaphore()` (1 permit) exclusively for startup/auto-
discover reindexes. The existing `reindex_semaphore()` (2 permits) is
reserved for interactive (user-initiated) requests. The two semaphores are
independent: an interactive request is never blocked by a background backlog.
`spawn_reindex_with_cleanup` accepts a new `priority: bool` parameter that
routes to the correct semaphore. All HTTP reindex handler calls pass
`priority=true`; the auto-discover HTTP POST sends `"background": true` which
flips to `priority=false` in the handler. The routing decision is factored into
`reindex_semaphore_for(priority)` for testability.

**Fix 2 — skip dead root paths**: Before queuing a background reindex, check
that `path.exists()`. Projects on unmounted volumes (e.g. `/Volumes/Kemono`
once wiped) or moved directories are silently skipped — the index registration
is preserved but the reindex trigger is not queued. Logged at `info` so
operators can see which projects were skipped without consulting daemon logs.

**Bonus — /health backlog counter**: `GET /health` now includes
`background_reindex_queue_depth` (count of background tasks queued or
in-flight). Operators can watch this field tick to zero as the startup storm
drains.

**Tests added**:
- `reindex_semaphore_selection_routes_by_priority` — proves the two
  semaphores are distinct singletons routed correctly by the priority flag.
- `interactive_not_blocked_when_background_semaphore_full` — proves that
  saturating the background semaphore leaves the interactive semaphore free.
- `background_reindex_queue_depth_counts_waiting_tasks` — exercises the
  atomic counter behind `/health`'s `background_reindex_queue_depth`.
- `root_path_exists_true_for_real_dir`, `_false_after_removal`,
  `_false_for_never_created` — unit tests for the dead-root skip predicate.

Runtime verification needed: the end-to-end "user index returns promptly
while 44 background tasks queue" property requires a running daemon and is
documented in the module header as needing manual verification after deploy.

fix(trusty-search): serve self-exits on stdin EOF to avoid orphaned MCP workers (closes #457) (#459)

Root cause: when Claude Code closes the pipe to a `trusty-search serve`
process (session end, restart), the process did not exit promptly. The
`run_stdio_loop` in `trusty-common` already returns `Ok(())` on EOF, but the
`reqwest::Client` connection pool spawns background tokio tasks whose
`pool_idle_timeout` defaults to 90 s — the tokio runtime cannot complete its
shutdown until those tasks drain, keeping the process alive as an orphan long
after the client disconnected. Across repeated Claude Code restarts (4–9
observed), these orphans accumulate and hold open file handles.

Fix (serve-side self-exit, not stop-side reaping):
- In `handle_serve` (stdio path only): after `crate::mcp::stdio::run(server)` returns
  (i.e. stdin hit EOF), call `std::process::exit(0)` immediately. This bypasses
  the reqwest pool drain and any other background tasks, guaranteeing the process
  exits the moment its client disconnects. HTTP serve mode is intentionally
  excluded — it has an explicit cleanup path (discovery-file removal) and the
  axum serve loop is the natural lifetime anchor.

Why this approach is safer than reaping from `stop`:
- `stop` only needs to reach the `start` daemon; killing `serve` workers from
  `stop` would disconnect live MCP sessions mid-request and could corrupt
  in-flight JSON-RPC exchanges for other Claude Code tabs still using the server.
  Self-exit-on-EOF lets each `serve` worker manage its own lifetime: it exits
  only when *its* client goes away, leaving unrelated sessions untouched.

Tests (in `trusty-common`, gated behind `--features mcp`):
- `stdio_loop_exits_on_eof`: drives `run_stdio_loop_with_io` with `tokio::io::empty()`
  as stdin (immediate EOF) and asserts the future resolves `Ok(())` rather than

  normal request + a notification through an in-memory duplex, asserting the
  loop processes both and exits cleanly on pipe close.

is the final backstop verified at runtime (spawning the binary and closing its
stdin to confirm exit < 1 s is deferred to PM per the ticket instructions).

fix(trusty-search): repair legacy-index search after path migration (M002/M003) + CLI fixes (#453)

The #402 relative-path migration (M002, shipped in 0.19.0) rewrote redb chunk
IDs from absolute to root-relative on startup but never updated the live BM25
index, the in-memory chunk map, or the HNSW key sidecar. After idle eviction +
rehydrate (or a restart), BM25/HNSW emitted absolute keys that no longer matched
the now-relative redb, so every legacy index returned 0 results for all search
modes — a silent regression on a heavily-relied-on tool.

Fixes:
- M002: add refresh_live_indices_from_corpus() to rebuild BM25 + in-memory map
  from redb immediately after the redb rewrite.
- M003 (schema 2->3): new migration that relativizes hnsw.keys.json key strings
  (String->u64 sidecar only; no re-embed). Idempotent; auto-repairs indexes
  already stuck at schema_version=2 under the broken binary on next startup.
- store.rs: VectorStore::rewrite_keys_to_relative + UsearchStore override
  (clears is_view so save() flushes the rewritten sidecar).
- CLI Bug #1: `query --indexes "a,b"` / `--indexes "*"` now fan out correctly
  instead of falling through to single-index auto-detect.
- CLI Bug #3: `search --json` now emits JSON (was hardcoded human-readable).
- test: #[serial] on migrate_storage tests to fix a TRUSTY_DATA_DIR env race.

Verified on this machine: rustbot, trusty-izzie, and previously-stuck itinerator
all return BM25 + vector results after a plain restart, no manual reindex.

`open-mpm` re-invocation skips the argv-gated probe in mode_dispatch and lands
directly on this path, so it would clobber a live controller's socket — the
exact race called out in docs/research/process-model-and-event-architecture.md
(Q1: "the second one removes the stale socket on startup, breaking the first").

Add CtrlSocket::bind_singleton (+ _default): probe the socket first, and only
clean up + bind when the probe confirms the socket is stale (connection-refused,
not-found, ENOTSOCK, or timeout). When a live controller answers, return
BindOutcome::AlreadyRunning with the open stream instead of clobbering it. Wire
run_ctrl_inner to this variant: on AlreadyRunning it relinquishes the command
port to the incumbent and runs as a local-only REPL.

Also harden stale detection: a leftover non-socket file at the path yields
ENOTSOCK (errno 38) from connect, which was previously mis-classified as a hard
error. is_connection_refused now treats ENOTSOCK as stale so a crashed
controller's placeholder file is cleaned up and taken over.

Tests: bind_singleton_refuses_when_controller_alive (live listener ->
AlreadyRunning), bind_singleton_binds_when_socket_absent, and
bind_singleton_binds_over_stale_socket cover the probe/route/stale-cleanup
branches without spawning a real controller; is_connection_refused_classifies_enotsock
locks in the ENOTSOCK classification.

fix(tga): resolve classify finalization hang, db-lock race, and complexity population (closes #397) (#400)

Three bugs reported against tga 2.2.0:

Bug 1 — classify hangs ~120s at exit with external sources enabled.
Root cause: `#[tokio::main]` builds a multi-thread runtime whose drop blocks
until all background tasks finish, including reqwest's keep-alive connection
pool reaper (idle sockets against a live JIRA server linger ~90s). Fix: build
the runtime explicitly and call `Runtime::shutdown_timeout(0)` after the async
body completes, dropping idle connection tasks immediately. All real work is
awaited before shutdown.

Bug 3 — "database is locked" when classify runs right after collect.
Root cause: connections were opened without a busy_timeout, so a classify that
opened while collect was still checkpointing its WAL hit SQLITE_BUSY and failed
instantly. Fix: set `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000` on every connection open so a
transient checkpoint lock is waited out rather than erroring.

Bug 2 — complexity (1–5) never populated. Bounded investigation: the scoring
logic EXISTS (LLM tier produces it, pipeline persists it, library
`backfill_complexity` works) but was only reachable via the non-obvious
`tga classify --backfill-complexity` flag; the normal classify run consults the
LLM only for low-confidence commits, so rule/JIRA-resolved commits stay NULL.
Not a missing feature — a wiring/discoverability gap. Fix: expose the existing
operation as a discoverable `tga backfill complexity` subcommand (with
--dry-run and --use-llm). No new scoring feature built.

Tests: busy_timeout pragma + second-open-on-same-file (bug 3), complexity
backfill dry-run (bug 2). Version bumped 2.2.0 -> 2.2.1; CHANGELOG updated.

feat(tga)!: 2.0.0 — all-branch walk + uniform filters + CLI docs audit + fetch visibility (#335)

* fix(tga)!: walk all branches by default (refs/heads/* + refs/remotes/origin/*) (closes #331)

tga collect was seeding the revwalk from HEAD only, silently dropping
commits on any branch that was not an ancestor of HEAD. On multi-branch
repos this was losing ~56% of commits (PR branches, feature branches,
hotfixes never merged to main were simply never walked).

BREAKING CHANGE: the new default pushes every local branch head
(refs/heads/*) and every remote tracking ref (refs/remotes/origin/*,
excluding the refs/remotes/origin/HEAD symref) before walking. The
revwalk's internal dedup ensures each commit is yielded at most once;
the INSERT OR IGNORE on the commits SHA primary key provides a second
safety net. If no local or remote refs exist (e.g. CI detached HEAD),
the walk falls back to HEAD so collection does not fail.

Escape hatches:
- Pass --head-only on the CLI to restore the 1.x HEAD-only walk for all
  repos in one command.
- Set head_only: true on a specific repositories[] entry in YAML to opt
  out for that repo while keeping all-branch coverage for the rest.

Migration: existing tga.db files collected with tga <= 1.5.4 are missing
commits from non-default branches. Run `tga collect --force` after
upgrading to recover that history (--force bypasses the collection_runs
skip mechanism so already-collected weeks are re-walked).

Version bump: tga 1.5.4 -> 2.0.0 (major — breaking default change).

- multi_branch_coverage: 2 main + 3 feature commits, all 5 collected

fix(tga): IssueType+JiraProject tiers now report ExternalSource method (closes #321) (#322)

A regression observed immediately after 1.5.2 shipped: commits with a populated
`ticket_id` were getting classified by `regex_rule`, `fuzzy_match`, or
`weighted_sum` — never by `external_source` — even though the JIRA cache WAS
being hit during classification. JIRA's classifier contribution stayed at ~1%
when ~5-10% was expected.

## Why this was masked until 1.5.2

PR #318 (1.5.2) fixed `commits.ticket_id` being NULL during `tga collect`.
Before that fix, no commits even had `ticket_id` to look up, so the misnamed
classification method on JIRA-attributed rows was invisible. Once ticket_ids
started appearing on commit rows, the wrong-method labels became observable.

## Root cause

Two cascade tiers were emitting the wrong `ClassificationMethod` variant —
both tiers classify based on EXTERNAL ticket-system metadata (PM issue type
fields, JIRA project-key mappings), NOT on commit-message text patterns, so
`ExternalSource` is the semantically correct label.

| Tier                | File                                          | Was         | Now            |
|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-------------|----------------|
| 1.5 IssueTypeTier   | classify/tiers/issue_type_tier.rs             | ExactRule   | ExternalSource |
| 1.6 JiraProjectTier | classify/tiers/jira_project_tier.rs           | RegexRule   | ExternalSource |

The wrong labels were swallowing JIRA-driven verdicts into the `regex_rule`
and `exact_rule` analytics buckets, dropping the `external_source` share
back near zero.

## Fix

Two label changes (one per tier), each carrying a Why-comment explaining
the semantic justification. No structural change to the cascade itself —
the tiers fire and win when they should, they were just reporting the wrong
provenance to downstream analytics.

## Tests

Added regression test `jira_project_tier_reports_external_source_method` in
`classifier.rs` to pin the contract: when JiraProjectTier wins, the result
must carry `ClassificationMethod::ExternalSource`. This guards against
future copy-paste regressions.

## Validation

- cargo test -p tga: PASS (66 lib + 1 integration + 3 doc tests; 0 failed)
- cargo clippy -p tga --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean
- cargo fmt --check: clean

## Migration

Existing tga.db files have wrong `classification_method` on JIRA-eligible
commits. Re-run `tga classify` on the affected date range to overwrite
`regex_rule` / `exact_rule` rows with `external_source`. No schema change,
no `tga backfill` subcommand needed.

feat(trusty-search): three-phase reindex progress bar (closes #317) (#319)

The CLI reindex progress bar previously showed nothing during the file
walk — on a large repo this is several seconds of silent startup before
the bar appears and starts moving. Users had no feedback that anything
was happening.

## What changed

The reindex now drives the SAME indicatif `ProgressBar` through three
distinct phases. Each transition resets bar position to 0 and updates
the label; no new bars are stacked.

- **Walking files…** — Phase 1. The daemon emits a new `walk_complete`
  SSE event the moment the file-system walk finishes. The bar fills
  instantly (the walk is synchronous on the daemon side; future work
  could thread a callback for mid-walk progress on truly huge repos).

- **Chunking…** — Phase 2. The `start` event (emitted immediately
  after `walk_complete`) flips the label to Chunking; this is a brief
  sub-second window between walk-complete and the first batch event.

- **Embedding chunks…** — Phase 3. The first `batch` event flips the
  label to Embedding. This covers the bulk of the work (fused
  parse+embed per batch, as the existing pipeline does).

For `lexical_only` indexes, the Embedding phase is skipped: the bar
stays on Chunking through `complete` since no `batch` events fire.

## SSE event additions

- `walk_complete` — emitted by the daemon BEFORE the existing `start`
  event. Carries `{event, total_files, index_id}`. Strictly additive;
  older CLIs hit the catch-all match arm and ignore it.

## Backward compatibility

- **New CLI + old daemon (no `walk_complete`)**: the SSE loop tracks
  `received_walk_complete`. When `false`, the `start` event maps
  directly to Embedding (or Chunking for `lexical_only`) — identical
  to the previous behaviour.
- **Old CLI + new daemon**: ignores `walk_complete`, continues to
  wait for `start` exactly as before. Zero regression.

## Version

trusty-search 0.14.0 → 0.15.0 (feat = minor bump per project convention).
open-mpm's trusty-search dep updated to 0.15.0.

## Validation

- cargo test -p trusty-search: 662 passed, 0 failed
- cargo clippy -p trusty-search --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean
- cargo fmt --check: clean
- cargo check -p open-mpm: passes with new dep version

## Tests

- `phase_transitions_reset_bar` — asserts `files.position() == 0`
  after `set_phase()` for Walking, Chunking, Embedding, ParseEmbed
- `sse_event_parser_drives_three_phase_ui` — exercises new-daemon
  path, old-daemon fallback, and lexical_only path
- `reindex_walks_directory_and_emits_events` — updated to assert
  `walk_complete` is now the first SSE event

## Surprises

- The daemon already had `walk_complete` partially wired in a prior
  partial implementation (lines 1437-1448 of `reindex.rs` with the
  comment referencing this work). Only the CLI side + the existing
  test that expected `start` to be first needed changes.

- No `walk_progress` event was added: the walk is a single synchronous
  call (`collect_files_to_index`) with no mid-walk callback point.
  The walk_complete event causes the bar to snap 0→100% on Walking
  the moment the walk returns. Future work can thread an mpsc
  channel through `walk_source_files_with_options` for mid-walk
  progress on multi-second walks; filed as future enhancement.

fix(tga): populate commits.ticket_id inline during collect (closes #316) (#318)

`tga collect` was writing every commit row with `ticket_id = NULL` regardless
of whether the commit message contained an extractable JIRA-style ticket ID.
On the Duetto CTO corpus, 2,006 of 6,212 uncategorized commits (32.3%) had
clearly-matchable IDs like `BB-2746`, `SRE-3104`, `DRE-405` but were never
attributed to JIRA — collapsing the JIRA classifier's contribution from the
expected 5-10% to about 1%.

The infrastructure already existed: `extract_ticket_id` was a private helper
inside `commands/backfill.rs`, called only by `tga backfill ticket-ids`.
Users who didn't know to run the backfill subcommand had 100% NULL `ticket_id`.

## Fix

- Promote `extract_ticket_id` to the public API of `tga::collect::ticket`
  (sibling of `is_ticketed`), so it can be shared.
- Call it inline at the commit INSERT in `collect::git::extractor`. The
  `commits` row now writes `ticket_id` alongside `ticketed` in a single pass.
- `commands::backfill` imports the canonical version from `collect::ticket`
  rather than maintaining its own duplicate.

## Tests

Added 10 unit tests covering the three reported sample patterns plus the
false-positive guard (`HTTP-200` shape), priority ordering, and multi-line
body matching. Added an integration test that runs `tga collect` against
an in-memory git repo and asserts `commits.ticket_id` is populated at
INSERT time — no separate backfill needed.

`cargo test -p tga`: 546 passed, 0 failed.

## Backward compatibility

`tga backfill ticket-ids` is retained — existing tga.db files with NULL
ticket_ids need a one-time backfill after upgrading. Future `tga collect`
runs against new commits will populate ticket_id automatically.

## Deferred

Optional project-key allowlist (e.g. exclude `HTTP-200` shapes) was
considered but deferred — current word-boundary regex is conservative
enough that false-positive risk is low in practice. File a follow-up
ticket if false-positives become observable.

fix(tga): walk all refs/tags/* not just default-branch ancestors (closes #303) (#305)

Root cause: scan_and_persist loaded ALL commit SHAs from the database (across
all repos in a multi-repo corpus) and upserted rows for EVERY one of them on
each per-repo scan. The last repo scanned overwrote the correctly-computed
on_any_tag=1 values of earlier repos with on_any_tag=0, because commits from
repo A are not ancestors of any tag in repo B.

~554 of 838 security commits in the user's 80-repo corpus were misclassified
as on_any_tag=0. Spot-checks confirmed they ARE on tag 1.10.0 in the
integrations repo (a GitFlow repo where develop is the working branch).

Fix: add repo_name: Option<&str> to scan_and_persist. When Some(name), filter
the SHA load to commits WHERE repository = name so each per-repo scan only
touches its own rows. The tag-walking graph walk (build_tag_map) still
traverses ALL ancestors in the git object store via refs/tags/*, independent
of branch topology — so commits on develop, release/*, or hotfix/* that are
tagged are correctly marked.

Also adds:
- Per-tag debug log line (RUST_LOG=debug tga backfill reachability)
- Integration test: GitFlow develop-tag pattern (2 new commits on develop,
  tagged v1.0.0 while HEAD is on master — both must show on_any_tag=1)
- Integration test: multi-repo cross-contamination regression guard
  (scan repo-B must not clobber repo-A's on_any_tag=1 values)

* fix(tga): tighten JIRA key regex against trailing-digit over-match (closes #285)

The old pattern \b([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{0,9}-\d+)\b was unbounded on the digit
run.  In live E2E testing against duettoresearch.atlassian.net a commit
message "per UIARCH-3288 followed by 5" produced the key UIARCH-32885,
which yielded a 404 from the JIRA API and silently lost the classification
signal for that commit.

Fix (two-layer guard):
1. Regex: replace \d+ with \d{1,7} — caps the digit run at 7 digits
   (highest realistic ticket number at scale; keeps the pattern fast).
2. Post-filter in extract_jira_keys: after each regex match, check whether
   the byte immediately following the match end is an ASCII digit; if so,
   skip the match.  This is the authoritative guard — the regex crate has
   no lookahead, so a bounded match could still be accepted before a longer
   run ends without this check.

New test: extract_jira_keys_no_trailing_digit_overreach covers:
  - "per UIARCH-3288 followed by 5" → ["UIARCH-3288"] (not UIARCH-32885)
  - Two separate keys in one message still both extracted
  - 8-digit run (PROJ-12345678) produces no match
  - 7-digit run at the cap still matches when followed by a space

closes #285

fix(trusty-memory): pre-allocate activity log ID in emit() to preserve emission order (closes #247) (#265)

The root cause of the flaky `activity_endpoint_lists_recent_emits` test
was not a missing flush — `flush_activity_writes` was already in place —
but a concurrent-ID-assignment race. `emit()` spawns one `spawn_blocking`
closure per event; when four events are emitted in rapid succession the
four closures each called `activity_log.append()` which internally called
`next_id.fetch_add(1)`. Because the blocking-pool workers execute in
non-deterministic order, the persisted IDs did not always match the
emission order, so the "newest-first" assertion intermittently saw
`drawer_added` instead of `drawer_deleted` at index 0.

Fix: add `ActivityLog::alloc_id()` (pre-allocates the next id in the
caller's thread) and `ActivityLog::append_with_id()` (writes with a
pre-allocated id, skipping the internal `fetch_add`). `AppState::emit()`
now calls `log.alloc_id()` synchronously before spawning, then passes
the id into the closure which calls `append_with_id()`. The sequence
number is therefore assigned in strict emission order regardless of
blocking-pool scheduling.

Verified: 20/20 consecutive runs pass after the fix (was ~20% failure
rate before).

perf(trusty-memory): eliminate O(N) disk walk + add BM25 write back-pressure (closes #228 #231) (#242)

* perf(trusty-memory): eliminate O(N) palace disk walk from memory write hot path (closes #228)

Every `memory_remember` / `memory_note` write used to trigger two full
palace-registry disk walks:

  1. `tools::lookup_palace_name` called `PalaceRegistry::list_palaces` —
     a synchronous filesystem walk of the data root — to resolve a
     friendly palace name for the `DrawerAdded` SSE event. The call was
     not wrapped in `spawn_blocking`, so the blocking I/O ran on an
     async worker thread.

  2. `service::aggregate_status_event` also called `list_palaces` and
     opened every palace handle to recompute drawer / vector / KG
     triple totals for the `StatusChanged` SSE event — emitted by
     every drawer create + every drawer delete.

For N palaces the per-write cost was 2 * `list_palaces` + N
`open_palace` calls — measurable on hosts with dozens of palaces and
fully redundant given the data is already in the in-memory registry.

Fix:

- Add `AppState::palace_names` (`Arc<DashMap<String, String>>`),
  populated at `load_palaces_from_disk` and `create_palace` and kept in
  sync by rename / delete. `lookup_palace_name` now reads from this
  cache (lock-free `DashMap::get`) and falls back to the palace id on
  miss — no filesystem walk, no `spawn_blocking` needed.

- Rewire `aggregate_status_event` to iterate the in-memory registry
  (`state.registry.list()`) instead of walking disk. Extract the shared
  drawer / vector / triple summing loop into a new
  `collect_palace_stats` helper used by both `status()` (which still
  needs the on-disk view for the dedicated endpoint) and
  `aggregate_status_event` (in-memory view for the SSE hot path).

- Remove the `self.state.emit(self.aggregate_status_event())` call from
  every write hot path (`memory_remember`, `memory_note`,
  `memory_forget`, HTTP `create_drawer`, HTTP `delete_drawer`).
  Lifecycle paths (palace create / delete / rename / dream run) still
  emit so dashboards see structural changes immediately.

- Add `spawn_status_event_ticker` in `run_http_on` that broadcasts
  `StatusChanged` every 30 s. SSE dashboards stay live; the per-write

- Drop the now-dead `web::aggregate_status_event` re-export.

* fix(trusty-memory): replace fire-and-forget BM25 spawns with bounded mpsc channel (closes #231)

Why: the previous BM25 index path used `tokio::spawn` per `memory_remember` /
`memory_note` write. Under a write burst with a slow or unreachable BM25
daemon, the unbounded in-flight task queue grew silently — unbounded memory
growth and a runtime DoS vector.

What: introduces a bounded `tokio::sync::mpsc` channel (capacity 256) plus a
single long-lived worker spawned by `AppState::new`. Writers now `try_send`
onto the channel — never blocking — and a full queue is dropped with a
`warn!` log. The worker handles the daemon RTT off the response path, exactly
as before; behaviour on success is unchanged. When BM25 is disabled the
worker still drains the channel into the void so senders never block.

Highlights:
- Add `Bm25IndexRequest` struct (palace, drawer_id, content, data_dir) and
  `BM25_INDEX_QUEUE_CAPACITY = 256` constant in `tools.rs`.
- Add `pub fn spawn_bm25_index_worker(rx, client, supervisor)` — the single
  worker that drains the channel and forwards to the BM25 daemon.
- Replace `bm25_index_fire_and_forget` with `bm25_index_enqueue` which
  `try_send`s onto the channel and logs on `TrySendError::Full` / `Closed`
  without ever failing the write.
- Add `bm25_index_tx` field on `AppState`; rebuild it inside
  `with_bm25_client_from_env` so the worker holds the real client + supervisor
  once opt-in is resolved.
- Promote the now-blocking `app_state_starts_with_empty_bound_addr` to
  `#[tokio::test]` because `AppState::new` now requires a runtime to spawn
  the worker.
- Add `bm25_index_queue_drops_when_full` regression test that hammers the
  enqueue past capacity and asserts overflow returns `Full` (not panics or
  blocks).

* fix(trusty-memory): replace std::sync::RwLock with tokio::sync::RwLock for prompt_context_cache (closes #229)

The prompt_context_cache on AppState was guarded by std::sync::RwLock,
whose write guard blocks the calling thread for the entire critical
section. `rebuild_prompt_cache` runs from async tool handlers
(kg_assert, add_alias, discover_aliases, kg_bootstrap, remove_prompt_fact)
and from HTTP handlers, so a blocking write guard stalls a tokio worker
thread for the full KG-walk + format + assignment duration.

Switch the field to tokio::sync::RwLock so the guard yields back to the
runtime instead of pinning a worker thread. Update every reader and
writer (production paths in tools.rs/web.rs + the rebuild fn in
prompt_facts.rs + the in-module tests) to .read().await / .write().await.

Tokio's RwLock is infallible, so the .map_err(|e| anyhow!(...))? and
.expect("read lock") boilerplate disappears on the production paths and
in the tests. Updated the AppState doc comment to call out the
async-aware lock and reference issue #229 so future readers don't
revert the change.

* fix(trusty-memory): per-palace write mutex eliminates dedup_gate TOCTOU race (closes #230)

The dedup gate in `tools.rs` read a snapshot of existing drawers via
`list_drawers`, checked Jaro-Winkler similarity against the new content,
then issued the write — a classic time-of-check/time-of-use race. Two
concurrent `memory_remember` (or `memory_note`) calls with identical
content could both see the pre-write snapshot, both pass the gate, and
both land duplicate drawers.

Fix: add `palace_write_locks: DashMap<String, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>>`
to `AppState`, with a `palace_write_lock(palace_id)` accessor that lazily
inserts a per-palace mutex on first use. `memory_remember` and
`memory_note` now acquire the per-palace lock before running the dedup
gate and hold it past `remember_with_options` so the second concurrent
writer observes the first writer's drawer in `list_drawers` and bails.
The lock is per-palace (not global) so writes to different palaces still
run in parallel.

Tested via `dedup_gate_blocks_concurrent_duplicate_writes`: spawns two
tokio tasks that race identical writes into a fresh palace; asserts
exactly one drawer lands and the loser carries the documented
`status = "skipped"` / `duplicate within window` envelope. Verified the
test fails on this branch when the lock acquisition is disabled.

* fix(trusty-memory): wrap activity_log.append in spawn_blocking inside AppState::emit (closes #232)

`AppState::emit` previously called `self.activity_log.append(...)` —
a synchronous redb write + fsync — directly on the calling async task's
thread, blocking the tokio runtime for the duration of every SSE event.
The inline comment claimed the persistence was best-effort and never
blocked the broadcast, but the call itself was blocking.

Offload the append to the tokio blocking thread pool via
`tokio::task::spawn_blocking` and return immediately. The clone is
cheap: `ActivityLog` wraps `Arc<Database>` + `Arc<AtomicU64>`, and
`DaemonEvent` is `Clone`. The JoinHandle is intentionally dropped —
the write stays best-effort as before, with failures surfaced via
`tracing::warn!`. `emit` remains synchronous so every existing call
site (including the sync `dispatch_hook_fired` JSON-RPC handler) keeps
compiling unchanged.

Tests that observed the persisted log right after a burst of emits
would otherwise race the blocking-pool worker. A new
`pending_activity_writes: Arc<AtomicUsize>` counter is bumped before
each spawn and decremented inside the closure; the new
`AppState::flush_activity_writes` async helper polls until the
counter is zero. Five tests are updated to call it before asserting
on the log state — production callers (dashboard `GET /api/v1/activity`)
already tolerate asynchronous settlement and need no change.

* feat(tga): DORA infrastructure — deployments, incidents, CFR/MTTR (closes #207, #208, #212, #213)

Lays the full DORA-metrics foundation in one migration + three new
subcommands. Each piece is independently usable but designed to plug
together so a user can go from `cargo install tga` to a working DORA
dashboard with three commands.

### Schema (migration 0014 — issues #212, #213, #208)

* `fact_deployments` — canonical deploy hub. `deploy_id` PK makes
  re-ingest idempotent. Indexed on repo, triggered_at, environment+status,
  git_sha.
* `fact_incidents` — production-incident observations with
  denormalised `mttr_hours`. FK to fact_deployments.deploy_id.
* `deployment_failures` — derived join used by CFR/MTTR; rebuilt from
  scratch on every `tga dora` run.
* Four pre-computed views: `v_deployment_frequency`, `v_lead_time`,
  `v_change_failure_rate`, `v_mttr`. Reports can SELECT directly from
  these without re-aggregating.

### `tga deployments collect` (issue #207)

Default source is `git_tags` — walks every tag in every configured
repo, matches against `dora.deployment_tag_pattern`, and INSERT OR
IGNOREs into `fact_deployments`. The github_releases /
github_actions sources are stubbed; manual is a no-op. The git-tag
path works against any local checkout with no external credentials.

### `tga incidents collect` (issue #213)

Two paths:
* JIRA SRE quick-win (default): project SRE-flagged work items
  (`project='SRE'` AND `item_type IN ('Bug','Incident')`) into
  `fact_incidents`. Parses dates from the raw_json envelope, handles
  both strict RFC3339 and JIRA's `+0000`-style offset.
* Datadog directory (stub): when `dora.datadog_dir` is set, lists the
  `.json` files but does not parse. The expected envelope shape is
  documented in a TODO so adopters can wire in their own parser.

### `tga dora` (issues #207, #208)

Three jobs:
1. Rebuild `deployment_failures` from `dora.failure_signals`. Each
   signal can match a classification category (`work_type: bug_fix`)
   and/or a commit-message regex (`commit_message_pattern: hotfix`),
   bounded by `within_hours`. A bad regex refuses to match rather
   than silently widening the failure set.
2. Print all four DORA metrics: deployment frequency, lead time for
   changes, change failure rate, mean time to recovery.
3. Honour `--since DATE` to scope reporting to a recent window.

### Config

New `dora:` block in YAML with `deployment_source`,
`deployment_tag_pattern`, `production_branch`, `failure_signals[]`,
`datadog_dir`. Regex validation lives in `Config::validate_ticket_regexes`
so bad patterns fail at load time, not mid-pipeline.

### Tests + docs

Six new unit tests cover the regex matchers, idempotency,
signal-matching truth table, empty-config no-ops, and the JIRA date
parser. README + example-config.yaml updated with the new YAML block
and the `tga deployments | incidents | dora` walkthrough.

feat(trusty-memory): inject creator tags on MCP writes + show memory snippet in drawer rows (closes #202) (#204)

Two related improvements to the TUI drawer activity panel.

Part 1 — Creator attribution on MCP writes
------------------------------------------
The `memory_remember` and `memory_note` MCP tools already merge
`CreatorInfo::new_self(MCP_CLIENT_NAME, CreatorSource::Mcp)` into every
write, but the dashboard could not tell at a glance which writes came
from a specific Claude / claude-mpm session. When the caller passes a
bare UUID as a free-form tag, project it into the reserved
`creator:session=<first-8-hex>` slot so the TUI activity panel and any
grep/jq workflow can pick it out without UUID-shape sniffing.

- Add `CREATOR_SESSION_PREFIX` and `session_tag_from_tags()` to
  `attribution`. The helper scans the supplied tag list in order, skips
  any `creator:*` reserved-namespace entries, and returns the
  formatted tag for the first parseable UUID. Three tests cover the
  happy path, the no-UUID skip path, and the reserved-namespace skip
  path (so a stray `creator:cwd=<uuid-shaped-tempdir>` cannot leak in).
- Wire the helper into both `memory_remember` and `memory_note` in
  `tools.rs`, immediately before the existing
  `CreatorInfo::merge_into()` call.
- Wire the same helper into the HTTP `service.rs::create_drawer`
  path so HTTP-origin writes that carry a session UUID get the same
  projection — the HTTP path was already injecting
  `creator:source=http` via `creator_info_from_http`, this just
  augments it.

Part 2 — Drawer snippet in the activity row
-------------------------------------------
The drawer row format was `<id8> <MM-DD HH:MM>  <creator>` with no
indication of what the drawer actually contained. The endpoint
already returns the full `content` field but the client wasn't
using it.

- Add `drawer_snippet()` + `DRAWER_SNIPPET_MAX_CHARS` (60) to
  `service.rs` and inject a `snippet` field into every entry in
  the `list_drawers` payload. Whitespace-collapsed, trimmed, capped
  with `…`, and rendered as `null` when the drawer body is empty so
  clients can distinguish "no body" from "empty body after
  whitespace collapse". Two new tests cover truncation, whitespace
  collapse, and the empty-body branch; the existing pagination test
  also asserts the new field.
- Add `snippet: Option<String>` to `DrawerInfo` and parse it from
  the API response. When the daemon predates the field, fall back
  to a 60-char client-side truncation of `content` so the panel
  stays useful across daemon versions. The existing
  `parse_drawers_projects_fields` test grows three cases.
- Update `format_drawer_row` to append `  <snippet>` after the
  creator column when present, truncated to 60 chars. Empty /
  whitespace-only snippets are elided so the row collapses back to
  the legacy layout. A new `drawer_row_includes_snippet` test
  covers the four cases (with snippet, no snippet, whitespace-only,
  long-truncated).

fix(trusty-search): token-count guard on ACRONYM_HINT_RE — multi-word acronym queries route to Conceptual (closes #197) (#199)

Why: PR #162 added dense doc strings to classifier.rs containing the tokens
{HNSW, vector, similarity, search}, making classifier.rs BM25-competitive
for the query "HNSW vector similarity search". With ACRONYM_HINT_RE firing
on ANY query containing an ALL_CAPS token, the query routed to Definition
(beta=0.7 BM25), and after RRF fusion classifier.rs outranked store.rs
(where UsearchStore::search lives) — pushing the expected result from
rank 1-3 to rank 5.

What: gate ACRONYM_HINT_RE on token count. The Definition route now only
fires when the query is short (≤2 tokens) OR has no natural-language
(lowercase-leading) tokens. Queries with ≥3 tokens AND lowercase NL words
(e.g. "HNSW vector similarity search") fall through to the multi-noun
branch and classify as Conceptual (alpha=0.8 semantic), letting the
vector lane surface the canonical struct file over docs that merely
mention the acronym.

Short acronym queries (HNSW, BM25 index, RRF fusion, ORT) continue to
route to Definition unchanged — the #117 acceptance criterion is
preserved via the 2-token "HNSW lookup" query in the updated structural
boost test.

feat(trusty-memory): BM25 daemon spawn supervisor — auto-start per-palace subprocess (closes #193) (#194)

Why: trusty-memory ships the trusty-bm25-daemon binary alongside its own
but never actually spawns one. Operators who set TRUSTY_BM25_DAEMON=1
have to babysit one daemon per palace via launchd / manual — the same UX

bm25_client field (same TRUSTY_BM25_DAEMON=1 gate), calls it before
every BM25 index / search, and degrades gracefully (logs + vector-only
recall) when the daemon can't be started.

socket adoption, Send+Sync bounds, probe behaviour, and idempotent
shutdown. New #[ignore]-tagged integration test in
tests/bm25_supervisor_e2e.rs spawns a real trusty-bm25-daemon child,
indexes + searches a document, and verifies clean shutdown. All 260

fix(trusty-memory): health probe uses dedicated palace + always deletes on error (closes #185) (#188)

The /health round-trip used to pick whichever palace `list_palaces()` returned
first (APFS creation order on macOS, so `localLLM` always won) and leaked the
probe drawer permanently when recall errored or returned an empty result —
~1,420 junk `healthcheck`-tagged drawers accumulated in real user palaces.

1. Dedicated probe palace. The probe now provisions a hidden `__health_probe__`
   palace via `ensure_health_probe_palace` and runs the round-trip there, so a
   stray leak (e.g. daemon crash mid-call) is confined to a palace the user
   never sees.

2. Cleanup-before-error invariant. Extracted `run_health_round_trip_inner` so
   the store-recall-forget sequence always calls `handle.forget(drawer_id)`
   *before* propagating any recall error. Both the `Err(_)` and the empty-
   result failure modes used to bypass forget; both are now closed.

3. Reserved-prefix filter. `MemoryService::list_palaces` drops any palace whose
   id starts with `__`, so the probe palace never appears in the admin UI,
   TUI, or chat-tool palace roster. Centralised in `is_reserved_system_palace`
   for future system palaces.

Tests: four new unit tests in `web::tests` lock the invariants — invisible
palace, cleanup on success, cleanup on recall miss, cleanup on recall error.
The three pre-existing `/health` integration tests are now `#[ignore]`d since
every `/health` call now runs the full ONNX round-trip on first request.

* feat(trusty-common): migrations feature — SchemaVersion, MigrationRunner, file stamp helpers (closes #179)

feat(trusty-search): migration framework + M001 per-pub-const Rust re-chunk (#183)

Adds a forward-only, idempotent schema migration framework for redb
corpus indexes. On daemon startup (after restore_indexes), the runner
fires one background task per registered index, advancing each from its
stored schema_version to CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION without blocking the
query path.

`pub const`/`pub static` but have no ChunkType::Constant chunks yet.

tree-sitter parse on irrelevant files. Idempotency: files with existing

feat(trusty-embed-daemon): batching ONNX embedding subprocess with UDS JSON-RPC (#155) (#157)

trusty-memory's in-process embedder serialises all recall queries through a
single ONNX mutex inside FastEmbedder; under 50 concurrent callers p99 hits
~894 ms. Splitting embedding into a dedicated subprocess with a batching
queue eliminates the mutex contention and unlocks coalesced ONNX calls.

                     RpcResponse) + error-code constants
  - socket.rs:       default_socket_path under $TMPDIR plus stale-socket
                     cleanup helper (idempotent unlink)
  - batch_queue.rs:  BatchQueue + worker — 10 ms / 32-item window via
                     tokio::select! against a deadline; oneshot fan-out so
                     each caller awaits its own result with no shared lock
  - server.rs:       UnixListener accept loop + per-connection newline-
                     framed JSON-RPC dispatch
  - main.rs:         clap CLI (--socket, --batch-size, --batch-window-ms),

fix(trusty-memory): per-palace write mutex + create_dir_all guard on L1 snapshot (#154) (#161)

Eliminates the "No such file or directory" race on l1_cache.json under
concurrent memory_remember calls. Two-part fix:
1. create_dir_all before every L1 snapshot rename (defensive, 1 syscall)
   plus per-call unique tmp filename (PID + monotonic counter) so two
   in-process writers cannot trample each other's tmp file.
2. Per-palace tokio::sync::Mutex in PalaceHandle serialises concurrent
   appends to the same palace (remember/forget) without blocking reads or
   cross-palace writes.

Root cause was multiple writers all targeting l1_cache.json.tmp: the
first rename(tmp -> target) succeeded and removed the tmp, then the
second rename failed with ENOENT. The error string reported the dest
path even though it was really the tmp source that vanished.

Concurrent write success rate: ~42% -> 100% (validated by new
remember_concurrent_does_not_lose_writes test in retrieval.rs and
concurrent_save_l1_cache_no_enoent in l1_cache.rs).

Closes #154

* feat(trusty-memory): multi-transport daemon — HTTP + UDS + stdio bridge

Refactor the daemon around a transport-agnostic JSON-RPC 2.0
dispatcher. The HTTP server stays on axum (port 7070) for the
browser UI and existing REST clients, gaining a new POST /rpc
route that accepts JSON-RPC envelopes. A new Unix domain socket
transport exposes the same dispatcher via NDJSON-framed JSON-RPC
2.0 for low-overhead local clients. A tiny ~120-LOC
`trusty-memory-mcp-bridge` binary connects the UDS to Claude
Code's stdio MCP protocol via pure byte copy — it never opens
redb, sidestepping the lock-collision bug that broke
`serve --stdio` before this PR.

Architecture
- transport/rpc.rs: JsonRpcRequest / JsonRpcResponse types +
  dispatch() that routes every method to existing handlers in
  tools.rs (palace_*, memory_*, kg_*, hook_fired, etc.). Plus
  protocol methods ping, tools/list, tools/call, rpc.discover.
- transport/uds.rs: UnixListener + accept loop. Per-connection
  newline-framed JSON pipeline. socket_path_for(data_root)
  derives a per-root socket so multiple daemons can coexist
  without colliding on the canonical $TMPDIR path. Sockets are
  chmod 0600.
- src/bin/mcp_bridge.rs: tokio::io::copy bidirectional between
  stdin/stdout and a UnixStream. Pure byte pipe — verified by
  a test that scans the source for redb references.

- lib.rs: run_http_on now spawns the UDS listener alongside the

The post-#136 recall path surfaces every drawer the palace returns for the
prompt, including those auto-captured by the upstream
`trusty-memory hooks fire claude.user-prompt` hook (wired by
trusty-mpm-core::session_launch into a binary outside this tree). Those

version bump") tagged `claude-session` + `user-prompt`, and they dominate
recall — three sample sessions surfaced the literal token "yes" five
times across semantically distinct prompts.

Why: the in-tree symptom of #139 is fixable independently of where the
auto-capture lives. A tag-based deny list is the cheapest, lowest-risk
gate that does not regress the existing #136 contract.

What:
- New `DEFAULT_DENY_TAGS = ["claude-session", "user-prompt"]` applied to
  recall results before composition.
- New `TRUSTY_MEMORY_PROMPT_RECALL_DENY_TAGS` env override (comma-separated,
  whitespace-trimmed, case-insensitive).
- `filter_drawers_by_deny_tags` returns the original list when the deny
  list is empty, keeps tagless drawers, and matches case-insensitively.
- When the filter empties the recall set, the existing fallback path
  (global hot facts → empty placeholder) takes over — no `Relevant
  memories` section is rendered.

  test for the matcher (empty deny list, case-insensitive, tagless
  drawer, multi-deny).
- `prompt_context_recall_filters_deny_tags` — populated palace where two
  of three drawers carry the default deny tags; only the signal drawer
  surfaces.
- `prompt_context_recall_env_override_extends_deny_list` — palace with
  a custom `noise-tag` drawer; env override filters it; injection

- `prompt_context_recall_all_filtered_falls_back_to_global` — every

fix(trusty-search): Definition-intent boost surfaces struct/enum chunks over usage sites (closes #117)

Layered on top of the #119 classifier upgrade. With #119 alone, the canonical
v0.8.1 benchmark query `HNSW vector similarity search` classifies as
Definition (was Unknown), which already demotes docs and engages the
BM25-heavy weighting. That moved `hnsw_store.rs` from rank 8 to rank ~4,
but usage chunks (`retrieval.rs`, `mmr.rs`, `search.rs`) with high
BM25 TF still won the top slots — they mention HNSW many times even
though they don't DECLARE HnswStore.

`apply_score_adjustments`. When intent == Definition AND a chunk's
`chunk_type` is `Struct`/`Enum`/`Class`/`Trait`/`TypeAlias` AND its
`function_name` contains (case-insensitive) at least one query token,
multiply the score by `STRUCT_DEFINITION_BOOST = 2.0`.

query token `hnsw` lowercased vs function-name `hnswstore` lowercased
— `hnswstore.contains("hnsw")` is true. Tuned to 2.0 because:
  * Large enough to flip the top-3 on the benchmark scenario
  * Small enough to coexist with the branch-modified boost (1.0..3.0)
    when both fire on the same chunk
  * `is_struct_definition_chunk_type` narrows eligibility to
    declaration-shaped chunks only — Functions/Methods/FreeCode don't
    qualify, so usage chunks that call HNSW don't accidentally inherit
    the boost

plants a Struct-typed declaration (HnswStore in hnsw_store.rs) alongside
three high-TF usage chunks and asserts the declaration ranks in top-3.

fix(trusty-search): canonicalize index root paths and follow symlinks

Two bugs caused zero search results when indexing via a symlink path:

   so the symlink alias was stored in the registry. Queries from the
   canonical mount path (/Volumes/Kemono/...) failed path-prefix matching

- create_index_canonicalizes_symlinked_root_path (server)

fix(trusty-memory): make discover_git_remote worktree-robust (closes #116) (#121)

Mirrors the pattern from PR #115 (which closed #113): in a git worktree,
`.git` is a *file* containing `gitdir: <parent>/.git/worktrees/<name>/`,
not a directory, so a direct `read_to_string(".git/config")` returns

worktree-based checkout.

fallback so the existing fixture-based unit tests (which fabricate a

absent from PATH.

guard: builds a real `git init` + `git worktree add` pair in a tempdir
and asserts `discover_git_remote` recovers the origin URL from inside

fix(trusty-memory): make kg_bootstrap worktree-robust (closes #113) (#115)

In a git worktree, `.git` is a file pointing to the parent repo's
`.git/worktrees/<name>/` directory; the `[remote "origin"]` section
lives in the parent's `.git/config`, not in any path reachable from
`<root>/.git/config`. The previous bootstrap scanner read that path
directly and silently dropped the `source_repo` triple in any worktree,
causing `tools::tests::kg_bootstrap_seeds_workspace_facts` to fail in
worktree-based local dev.

Switch `scan_git_config` to shell out to `git -C <root> config --get
remote.origin.url` first — git natively resolves the `.git`-file
pointer, so worktrees, normal checkouts, and submodules all work
uniformly. Fall back to the prior INI scan only when `git` is
unavailable on PATH, preserving the existing fixture-based unit test
(`scan_project_extracts_git_origin`) which fabricates a `.git/config`
file in a tempdir without a real repo.

* fix(trusty-search): canonicalize index root paths and follow symlinks

Two bugs caused zero search results when indexing via a symlink path:

1. validate_root_path in server.rs never called std::fs::canonicalize,
   so the symlink alias was stored in the registry. Queries from the
   canonical mount path (/Volumes/Kemono/...) failed path-prefix matching
   against the stored symlink alias (/Users/masa/...).

2. WalkDir in walker.rs had follow_links(false), silently skipping any
   symlinked subdirectories within the indexed tree.

create_index_handler and reindex_handler overwrite req.root_path with
the canonical form before any downstream consumer (persistence layer,
indexer, path filters, git HEAD probe) sees it. Walker canonicalizes
its root and sets follow_links(true). reindex.rs canonicalizes
handle.root_path before path-filter comparisons.

Three new unix-gated tests added:
- test_canonicalizes_symlinked_root (walker)
- test_follows_symlinked_subdirectory (walker)
- create_index_canonicalizes_symlinked_root_path (server)

591 tests pass. Verified end-to-end: indexing via symlink path now
stores the canonical path in the registry and returns results.

and need to be reindexed to work correctly.

Root cause: redb takes flock(LOCK_EX) on kg.redb and index.usearch.redb.

DatabaseAlreadyOpen. WAL mode not applicable — KG is redb, not SQLite.

Fix — snapshot-on-contention in storage layer:

concurrent_open.rs (new):
- try_open_or_snapshot(path): tries normal Database::create; on
  DatabaseAlreadyOpen copies live file to tmp snapshot (unique path via
  SNAPSHOT_SEQ atomic: <tmpdir>/trusty-memory-snapshot-<pid>-<seq>-<name>)
  and opens snapshot read-only-by-convention
- SnapshotGuard removes snapshot file on drop
- Returns (Arc<Database>, SnapshotGuard, OpenMode) so callers know mode

KgStoreRedb + UsearchStore/HnswStore:
- Consume try_open_or_snapshot, store OpenMode
- Every write method short-circuits with READ_ONLY_ERROR_MSG on snapshot

retrieval.rs:
- PalaceHandle::is_read_only() aggregates KG + vector mode
- remember(), forget(), kg_assert(), dream compaction check it and return
  clear error: "palace is read-only: HTTP daemon holds write lock —
  route writes through HTTP API or stop daemon before retrying via stdio"

Concurrent-access story:
- HTTP daemon (process A): owns live file, full read+write
- stdio client (process B): snapshot fallback, read-only point-in-time
- recall/kg_query/palace_info work; remember/forget/kg_assert fail fast
- Same-process double-open: reuses cached Arc<KgDbState>, no snapshot

RSS to ~72 GB on Apple Silicon during large indexing batches, tripping
jetsam SIGKILL. Candle talks to Metal directly and bypasses CoreML

  with trusty-search's local candle path.

  the trait `Embedder::embed_batch` returns `anyhow::Result` to match the
  existing trait signature.
- Three `#[ignore]`d unit tests cover dimension/normalisation,
  determinism, and similar-vs-dissimilar cosine ordering — matching the

Add an in-memory `StableGraph<String, KgEdge>` cache alongside the redb
TRIPLES table so single-hop traversal (`neighbors`) and multi-hop
queries (`shortest_path`) run without disk I/O. The cache is hydrated
from the active triples on `KnowledgeGraph::open` and kept in sync by
`assert` (adds/replaces edge) and `retract` (drops edge, preserves
nodes).

New public surface on `KnowledgeGraph`:
- `KgEdge` carries predicate + confidence + provenance + valid_from /
  valid_to so callers can rank/filter edges without re-fetching from
  redb.
- `neighbors(entity) -> Vec<(String, KgEdge)>` returns both outgoing
  and incoming directly-connected entities.
- `shortest_path(from, to) -> Option<Vec<String>>` runs unit-weight
  Dijkstra over outgoing edges and reconstructs the path from the
  predecessor map.

Locking model: a single `Arc<RwLock<Adjacency>>` covers the
StableGraph and the `String -> NodeIndex` lookup atomically. Read lock
for queries, write lock for mutations applied *after* the redb commit
succeeds — a failed write never leaves the cache ahead of the store.

Tests in `crates/trusty-common/tests/kg_graph_tests.rs`:
- `hydration_populates_graph` — five edges survive reopen.
- `assert_adds_edge` — single triple visible from both endpoints.
- `retract_removes_edge` — edge dropped, nodes preserved (verified by
  re-asserting against the preserved endpoint).
- `neighbors_returns_connected` — A->B->C chain sees both sides from B.
- `shortest_path_finds_route` — A->B->C returns `[A, B, C]`, plus
  same-node, unknown-endpoint, and disconnected cases.

Cargo: gate `petgraph` (already in workspace deps at 0.8) behind the
existing `memory-core` feature so non-memory crates do not pay the cost.

feat(trusty-common): rewrite KnowledgeGraph internals from SQLite to redb (closes #44)

Replace the rusqlite + r2d2-backed `KnowledgeGraph` with a redb-backed
`KgStoreRedb` storage engine. The public `KnowledgeGraph` API is preserved
verbatim — methods, signatures, return types — so all downstream call sites
(retrieval, registry, web, dreamer) continue to work without changes.

Why redb: pure-Rust embedded transactional k/v store with no native deps,
no r2d2 30s connect-timeout footgun, and O(log n) range scans backing the
temporal-fact intervals model.

Changes:

- crates/trusty-common/src/memory_core/store/kg_redb.rs (new): full
  `KgStoreRedb` implementation — assert / retract / query_active /
  list_subjects(_with_counts) / list_active / count_active_triples /
  checkpoint (no-op) / upsert_drawer / delete_drawer / load_drawers /
  load_drawer_ids / dump_all_triples. History rows are preserved under a
  `hist:`-prefixed key so superseded intervals are still recoverable for
  the #45 migration tool.
- crates/trusty-common/src/memory_core/store/kg.rs: rewritten as a thin
  delegating wrapper over `KgStoreRedb`. `open(path)` derives `kg.redb`
  alongside the legacy `kg.db` path so callers continue to pass the
  SQLite-style argument. Async methods (`assert`, `retract`,
  `query_active`, `list_active`) run blocking redb work on
  `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. All original tests retained.
- crates/trusty-common/src/memory_core/store/kg_sqlite.rs (new):
  legacy SQLite KG read path retained behind the new `sqlite-kg` feature
  flag. Issue #45's migration tool reads `kg.db` via this module; issue #47
  will retire it along with the rusqlite dep.
- crates/trusty-common/src/memory_core/store/mod.rs: register kg_redb
  (always) and kg_sqlite (feature-gated).
- crates/trusty-common/Cargo.toml: add `sqlite-kg` feature.

Process-global `Database` cache: redb forbids two in-process handles to
the same file. The trusty stack regularly opens the same palace from
multiple registries (test setup + `AppState`, foreground + dreamer); SQLite
allowed this and we must preserve the behavior. `KgStoreRedb::open`
consults a `Mutex<HashMap<canonical_path, Weak<Database>>>` and returns
the live `Arc<Database>` when one exists, falling through to a fresh
`Database::create` otherwise. Once all handles drop, the next open
creates a new one.

Tests:

- 14 new unit tests in `kg_redb.rs` covering assert / retract semantics,
  persistence across reopen, drawer CRUD, count_active, history
  preservation, and the multi-handle cache.
- All pre-existing `KnowledgeGraph` tests in `kg.rs` retained and pass
  unchanged (open / assert / retract / list / count / checkpoint / drawer
  CRUD — 13 tests).
- `trusty-memory` suite: 81/81 pass.
- `cargo clippy -p trusty-common --features memory-core` clean.

feat(trusty-search): CoreML memory tripwire — auto-halve batch size on RSS spike

CoreML on Apple Silicon can spike RSS by tens of GB within a single
embed_batch call — the per-batch unified-memory buffer is not released
until the call returns, so the existing inter-batch RSS poller reacts
too late. This adds a tripwire that measures the per-call RSS delta and,
on a dangerous spike, halves the batch size for the remaining sub-batches.

- memory_policy.rs: add DEFAULT_COREML_TRIPWIRE_MB (4 GB) and
  resolve_coreml_tripwire_mb() reading TRUSTY_COREML_TRIPWIRE_MB, with
  the same parse/clamp/warn semantics as resolve_coreml_batch_size().
- ingest.rs: add current_rss_mb() (ps on macOS, /proc/self/status on
  Linux, 0 elsewhere) and wire the tripwire into embed_chunks_in_batches.
  Snapshots RSS before each sub-batch embed and measures the delta after;
  on a trip it logs a warning, halves batch_size (floored at
  COREML_BATCH_SIZE_MIN), and fires once per reindex. CoreML-only —
  CPU/CUDA paths skip it entirely. Non-fatal: a failed RSS probe (0)
  simply disables the tripwire; the reindex never aborts.

feat(trusty-search): redb 16 GiB cache, atomic chunk+entity upsert, throttle HNSW snapshots (closes #29)

Three perf/correctness wins in the reindex pipeline (issue #29):

1. redb cache size 1 GiB -> 16 GiB. The default 1 GiB application cache
   held <10% of a ~14 GB corpus file; on a 128 GB host a 16 GiB cache
   keeps the hot working set resident and cuts disk reads for search
   queries. Applied via Database::builder().set_cache_size in the single
   CorpusStore::open path, covering the live corpus and the --force
   staging file alike.

2. CorpusStore::upsert_batch merges chunk + entity writes into one redb
   transaction. Previously upsert_chunks and upsert_entities each opened
   their own begin_write(); a crash between the two left the corpus and
   the symbol-graph entity table inconsistent. commit_corpus_to_redb,
   migrate_corpus_to_redb, and flush_corpus_to_disk now use the atomic
   path.

3. Throttle the per-batch background HNSW snapshot to every 16 batches.
   spawn_incremental_persist fired a full Index::save after every
   128-file batch (~110 saves on a 14k-file reindex, hundreds of ms
   each). redb already provides per-batch chunk durability, so the save
   is a pure backup; throttling reclaims ~15 s of redundant I/O. The
   reindex orchestrator calls force_incremental_persist after its batch
   loop so the final HNSW state is always durable.

Adds tests batch_upsert_is_atomic_roundtrip and
test_incremental_persist_throttles_to_interval.

feat(trusty-search): complete redb cutover — query-time reads + atomic force-reindex swap (closes #28)

Completes the redb persistence cutover for the chunk corpus:

- Query-time redb reads: `CorpusStore::get_chunks` batch point-reads top-k
  chunk text from the mmap-backed redb corpus inside a single read
  transaction. `CodeIndexer::fetch_chunks_for_ids` joins fused (id, score)
  pairs against redb (on a blocking worker) instead of the heap-resident
  `chunks` HashMap, with a graceful fallback to the in-memory map for
  BM25-only / test indexers and on any redb read error. Both the
  score-adjustment and final materialization stages of `search` now use
  this path, so large corpora no longer require full in-memory retention.

- Atomic `--force` reindex swap: the force-reindex orchestrator stages the
  rebuilt corpus in a sibling `index.redb.tmp`, commits every batch there,
  and atomically renames it over the live `index.redb` only on clean
  completion. On a memory abort the staging file is discarded and the
  original corpus is restored, so the daemon is never left serving a
  half-rebuilt or torn corpus.

feat(trusty-search): wire CorpusStore into indexer commit path and warm-boot rehydration (closes #28)

Phases 2-4 of the durable redb corpus (Phase 1 added CorpusStore).

- Commit path: every committed batch is written transactionally to the
  durable redb corpus alongside the in-memory chunks HashMap, which is now
  a write-through hot cache rather than the durability source of truth.
- Deletion path: remove_file / remove_chunk evict from redb so a warm-boot
  rehydration no longer resurrects deleted chunks.
- Warm-boot: the daemon rehydrates the in-memory corpus + entities from
  redb on startup (load_chunks_from_redb), with a one-time migration read
  from the legacy chunks.json snapshot when redb is empty. A missing redb
  file yields an empty corpus and triggers a reindex, same as before.
- Atomic --force reindex swap: a forced reindex stages the rebuilt corpus
  in index.redb.tmp; on clean completion it is atomically renamed over
  index.redb, and on memory-abort/failure it is discarded with the

perf(trusty-search): re-enable CoreML acceleration via ANE-only compute units (0.3.55)

The previous fix for issue #24 (CoreML EP causing ~72 GB virtual-RSS spike
and jetsam SIGKILL during indexing) forced CPU EP for the indexing flow.
That eliminated the OOM but capped throughput at ~2 files/sec vs the
~15+ files/sec CoreML had previously achieved.

Root cause analysis: the 72 GB spike was specifically caused by
`MLComputeUnits=ALL` (the ort crate's `CoreML::default()`), which allocates
buffers from the GPU side of Apple Silicon's unified-memory pool. The
Neural Engine, by contrast, uses dedicated memory that does NOT inflate
process virtual RSS.

Fix: switch the default CoreML registration to
`MLComputeUnits=CPUAndNeuralEngine`, plus enable `RequireStaticInputShapes`
(prevents per-shape graph recompilation memory) and
`SpecializationStrategy=FastPrediction`, and add an on-disk model cache
under `~/Library/Caches/trusty-embedder/coreml/` so we don't pay the
compile cost on every daemon start.

Net result: CoreML acceleration is back on by default during indexing,
without the OOM risk. Expected throughput is ~10-15× CPU EP (close to
the original CoreML(All) numbers) with steady-state RSS in the hundreds
of MB instead of tens of GB.

Operator controls (all backwards-compatible):
- `TRUSTY_COREML_COMPUTE_UNITS=all` — opt back into the old CPU+GPU+ANE
  pipeline (with the original memory behaviour); also accepts `cpu_gpu`
  and `cpu_only` for completeness.
- `TRUSTY_DEVICE=cpu` — still forces CPU EP everywhere.
- `TRUSTY_INDEX_DEVICE=cpu` — still forces CPU EP for auto-spawned
  indexing daemons. The default for this flag changed from `cpu` to
  `auto` so the new CoreML(ANE) path is used out of the box.

The new `ExecutionProvider::CoreMLAne` variant is added so call sites
that inspect the active provider (batch-size tuning, startup logs) can
distinguish ANE-only from the legacy CoreML(All) tag.

memory pool and inflates virtual RSS to ~72 GB before any inference runs.

feat(trusty-search): separate indexing memory pool (TRUSTY_INDEX_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB)

Adds a dedicated memory budget for the reindex pipeline, independent of
the global steady-state daemon limit (TRUSTY_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB).

Problem: CoreML EP on Apple Silicon allocates from the unified memory
pool (GPU/ANE + CPU share the same physical memory). sysinfo reports
these as process RSS, so a CoreML reindex burst of 70+ GB would trip
the global 32 GB memory guard within 3-4 seconds, aborting the reindex
before any files were processed.

Solution:
- New env var TRUSTY_INDEX_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB controls the RSS ceiling
  consulted by the reindex pipeline's memory poller, post-commit RSS
  check, and per-batch abort gate.
- Auto-tuned to 40% of host RAM, clamped to [2 GB, 96 GB], always ≥
  global limit. On 128 GB: 52 GB (vs 32 GB global). Set to 0 to disable.
- MemoryPolicy derives max_batch_size from the index limit (not global)
  so ORT transient arena cost stays under the right budget.
- Daemon startup banner logs both limits for operator visibility.
- Reindex poller now falls back to global limit when env var is unset,
  so existing deployments are zero-change.

Files changed:
- core/memguard.rs: index_memory_limit_mb() + over_index_memory_limit()
- core/memory_policy.rs: INDEX_MEMORY_LIMIT_* constants + compute fn
- service/reindex.rs: spawn_memory_poller uses index limit

  injection from the process-wide plugin registry.
